S12000033.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). Aberdeen City therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.

N09000001.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). Antrim and Newtownabbey therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Northern Ireland district councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply NI-wide instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Private Tenancies (Northern Ireland) Order 2006 art.65A: all landlords letting under a private tenancy must register. Registration lasts 3 years and costs £70 online or £80 on paper, with a £500 fixed penalty or a court fine up to £2,500. ADMINISTRATION CHANGED RECENTLY: Councils since 1 March 2025, with Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council as lead/host council for all 11 NI councils (previously the Department for Communities). (2) HMO LICENSING under the Houses in Multiple Occupation Act (Northern Ireland) 2016 s.1: 3+ persons as only or main residence forming more than two households, rent payable by at least one. A single NIHMO Unit at Belfast City Council administers HMO licensing on behalf of all 11 NI councils, and can take enforcement action for all of them, so a landlord in Antrim and Newtownabbey does not apply to their own council. Licences run 5 years. Statutory maximum rose from £45 to £75 per person per annum on 1 August 2025 (SR 2025/124). Belfast currently charges £62 per person per year, so £310 per person over a 5-year licence. Penalties run to a £5,000 fixed penalty and £20,000 on summary conviction. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: NARROWER THAN ENGLAND: NI requires MORE THAN TWO households (i.e. 3+). Three sharers from two households are an HMO in England but NOT in NI. PLANNING: Planning permission is also required for a new HMO; Belfast will not process a licence application without it.

E07000105.research: The HMO page is headed "Mandatory licensing of HMOs" and states "All HMOs with five or more people comprising of two or more family units will require a licence to operate." The Private Sector Housing Enforcement and Prosecution Policy separates duty from discretion: "Mandatory Licensing ... The Council is required to have a licensing scheme in place" versus "Discretionary licensing - The Council may, at its discretion bring into force licensing of other residential accommodation, as defined by parts 2 and 3 of the Housing Act 2004". Both discretionary types appear only conditionally, with no designated area, date or fee. The Private Sector Housing Strategy 2022-27 contains no occurrence of "selective licensing" or "additional licensing". No live designation consultation on haveyoursay.ashford.gov.uk. CAUTION: Ashford has an Article 4 Direction covering Aylesford Green, Beaver, Little Burton Farm and South Willesborough wards. That is planning control over conversion to HMO use, NOT licensing, and is a common cause of false positives in scraped datasets.

E07000200.research: The HMO page states "All HMOs occupied by five or more people need a licence. It is an offence to operate without a licence. The fee for a licence is £578.55" - the national mandatory threshold, with no lower threshold and no area carve-out. The council's public register is titled "Register of Mandatory Licences for Babergh" (updated 28 April 2026) with no additional or selective register alongside it. Site search for "selective licensing" returns only Licensing Act 2003, gambling, taxi, animal and SEV results. Negative by absence: Babergh publishes no explicit denial sentence. Committee-paper sweep incomplete (ModernGov required POST).

E08000016.research: IMPORTANT: Barnsley is widely and wrongly listed by third-party aggregators as a selective licensing council with named streets. It is not. Council FOI response FOI/5290 "Additional and selective licencing" answers "Do you run a 'Selective Licensing' scheme? If so, when did this commence? No" and "Do you operate any other 'Additional Licensing' scheme? If so, when did this commence? No", and states "BMBC does not operate a Selective licencing or Additional licencing schemes". The council's now-deleted selective licensing page (live 2019 to at least Dec 2024, now HTTP 404) said "For this reason, the current scheme is no longer being taken forward." Because no designation was ever made there is no start, end or expiry: this is 'approved but never implemented', not 'expired'. For the record only, the abandoned 2018 Cabinet recommendation named Measborough Dyke, Goldthorpe, Wombwell and Elsecar at a proposed £530 for 5 years; none of it was ever in force. Two scraping traps: the meta description of /services/housing/private-landlords/ still mentions "selective licensing schemes" though the page body does not, and a 2018 ASB landlord guide PDF still on the council server refers to "designated Selective Licensing areas in Barnsley" in anticipation of the abandoned scheme.

E07000084.research: Under "When is it licensable?" the council states a HMO must be licensed if it is "occupied by five or more people; flats that have five or more occupants from two or more households who share facilities, but it is not a purpose-built block compromising of three or more self-contained flats" - the national threshold with no borough extension. A 500-page crawl of www.basingstoke.gov.uk found zero occurrences of "selective" in any licensing sense; the only "licensing scheme" hits were a Temporary Exemption Notice and the great crested newt NatureSpace District Licensing Scheme. /selective-licensing and /additional-licensing return HTTP 404. Negative by absence, no explicit denial published. CAUTION: Basingstoke has an HMO Article 4 Direction requiring planning permission to convert a C3 dwelling to an HMO in Basingstoke Town, Chineham, Old Basing, Oakley and Sherborne St John. That is planning control, not licensing.

E07000171.research: The Housing Strategy 2021 to 2026 states "In 2018/19 Bassetlaw considered operating a selective licensing scheme for private rents in certain areas: this was declined in favour of developing a Thriving Neighbourhoods Strategy" and "Bassetlaw District Council consulted on the introduction of selective licensing the outcome was to introduce a Thriving Neighbourhoods strategy". That page shows Last Updated 16 June 2026. The HMO page (updated 22 May 2026) states "Under the national mandatory licensing scheme a HMO must be licensed if it has:- Five or more tenants in two or more households, and Shared facilities". A 400-page site crawl found only historic and rejected references; five candidate selective-licensing URLs return HTTP 404. There is no Worksop, Harworth or Langold designation: those place names appear only in the strategy's demographic description. Status is 'declined', which is neither 'proposed' nor 'expired', so no scheme object is recorded.

E06000022.council: Bath and North East Somerset Council
E06000022.research: The live HMO licence types page states "The Additional licensing scheme finished on 31 December 2023. Before we can approve a new scheme, we will need to carry out a consultation on any proposed new Additional HMO Licensing Scheme. We will update this page as soon as we know if this will or will not happen." and "Mandatory Licensing covers the whole of Bath and North East Somerset." The 2018 Cabinet designation report recommended a scheme "for a period of 5 years commencing on the 1st January 2019" covering "HMOs which house 3 or 4 people in 2 or more separate households in Bath City". Selective licensing has never been designated; the Housing Enforcement and Licensing Policy 2022 refers only to the abstract power under Part 3. Cross-check: the Housing Services Charging Policy 2026 lists HMO fees only under the mandatory test (new £1,025, renewal £925), with no additional or selective fee line. RE-CHECK CANDIDATE: the council has said it will update the page if a new scheme is consulted on.

E06000008.research: Executive Board report of 11 August 2022: "To date the Borough has introduced five Selective Licensing schemes... All selective licensing areas have now expired." and "Given that no selective licensing areas are currently in force in Blackburn with Darwen...". The Hollins Bank area was fully consulted on (7 May to 26 July 2024; 1,153 private rented properties; proposed fee £724; proposed 5-year term; parts of Ewood and Mill Hill & Moorgate wards plus a small part of Blackburn Central) but never designated: the Executive Member Decision of 21 February 2025 "Approved the recommendation to postpone declaring a Selective Licensing Area due to the changing housing market and in order to align any scheme with the emerging Housing Strategy". Additional licensing has never been designated; the only HMO page covers the national test (fee £950 for up to 10 lets, plus £50 per let thereafter). The Housing Strategy 2026-2036 (July 2026) lists both as future options: A60 "Consider the use of Selective Licensing schemes or similar" and A66 "Consider introducing an additional licensing scheme". TRAP: www.blackburn.gov.uk/selective-licensing still 307-redirects to the unpublished consultation page, which now returns Access denied. HIGH re-check priority: the postponement was tied to the Housing Strategy, now published.

W06000019.research: NEGATIVE, sourced. The council's HMO page recites all three Housing Act 2004 regimes generically and never claims to have exercised any: additional licensing is described only as 'A discretionary power that councils may decide to apply to a particular type of HMO', and selective as 'This is where the council MAY declare that certain areas, for example, where there is low demand for housing and/or antisocial behaviour, are appropriate for selective licensing.' A textbook statutory-powers recital, and the single reason a keyword scan flags this council. The only licensable category actually stated is the Welsh mandatory test: 'Three or more storeys high / Have five or more people in more than one household, and / Share amenities such as bathrooms, toilets and cooking facilities.' Applications are handed off to GOV.UK; there is no local scheme application route. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the approved 'Council Wide Fees and Charges 2026/2027' register contains exactly one HMO row, 'Public Protection - Housing | HMO License | 5 Yearly License Fee | £329.90 (2025/2026) | £339.80 (2026/2027)', with zero occurrences of 'selective', 'additional licen' or 'multiple occup' elsewhere in it. Corroborated by two current strategy documents: the Private Sector Housing Renewal Policy 2025-2030 mentions licensing exactly once and only as Rent Smart Wales; the Housing Strategy and Action Plan 2025-2030 (adopted Dec 2025) mentions HMOs once with no designation or proposal. ModernGov was CONTROL-VALIDATED ('zzqqxx' = 0 document hits, 'housing' = 20); 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing' returned only committee-name matches, Licensing Act 2003 and animal-licensing items. Sitemap sweep covered 987 URLs across /en/ and /cy/ with no licensing-scheme page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the statutory-powers recital above; the s.254 HMO definition; Rent Smart Wales; the Welsh mandatory three-storey test (WSI 2006/1712 (W.174)); the fee row 'Notices under s49 Housing Act 2004' (£277.30 per notice, enforcement cost recovery not licensing); and the Welsh homonyms, where all 13 'ychwanegol' hits are 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' (Additional Learning Needs) and the single 'dewisol' hit is 'addysg ddewisol yn y cartref' (elective home education). LIMITATION: the council's own site search is unusable server-side ('council tax', 'zzqqxx', 'selective licensing' and 'HMO' all returned byte-identical 158,661-byte responses), so it is client-side rendered and a nil result there proves nothing. The conclusion rests on the sitemap sweep, the fee register, the two policy PDFs and the control-validated committee search.

E07000033.research: The HMO page (rendering a live register headed "Current HMO Register at 04th August 2026") states "All Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) with five or more occupiers living as two or more households, must have a HMO Licence from their local authority. Where a HMO is occupied by fewer than five people, it will not require a licence." That second sentence is the council's own confirmation that no additional designation exists. Selective licensing was considered and rejected: Growth Scrutiny Committee, 23 October 2020, records "He did not believe that there were any such areas within Bolsover District at this time" and that earlier issues in Shirebrook "had significantly improved and a selective licensing scheme would not be necessary." The commonly repeated association with Shirebrook, Creswell and Whitwell is false; it reflects a concentration of MANDATORY HMO licences plus that rejected 2020 discussion. Nothing was designated, so nothing has expired. The council's 413-page HTML sitemap contains zero occurrences of "selective". Mandatory fee for context: £496 on application plus £111 on grant.

E07000146.council: Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk
E07000146.research: MANDATORY THRESHOLD, STATED EXPLICITLY: 'All Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) occupied by five or more people require an HMO licence', plus any single flat that is an HMO unless in a purpose-built block of three or more flats, with exemptions for housing associations, councils, health authorities, police and fire services. KEY TRAP AVOIDED, AND THE COUNCIL ITSELF DISAMBIGUATES IT: another page says 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) are properties rented out to three or more people who do not form the same household [and] share facilities such as a bathroom or kitchen', immediately followed by 'the criteria we use when deciding whether to licence an HMO is different to the HMO definition above.' The 'three or more' figure is the s.254 DEFINITION, not a licensing threshold. This is a high-risk false positive for any automated scraper. FEE CORROBORATION: new licence 3 to 15 bedrooms, £768 to £1,415 banded by bedroom count; renewal £649 to £1,135; 'There is currently no fee for the variation of an HMO licence.' No discretionary licensing fee line. REGISTER SCOPE: 'The public register for mandatory licensed HMOs is not available online.' The register is labelled mandatory-only; s.232 would require a register for a discretionary scheme too, and none is published. LICENCE A-Z: lists thirteen licence types with no property licensing entry at all. SITEMAP SWEEP: the landlord and housing branches contain no selective or additional licensing URL.

E07000095.research: The council states: 'A rented property is an HMO if the property is the tenant's only or main residence for the duration of the rental period, and either: there are five or more occupants who make up two or more households and share a kitchen bathroom or toilet; or it is a building that is converted into self-contained flats and the conversion did not meet the 1991 Building Regulation standards and more than one-third of the flats are let on short term tenancies.' The fee page lists a single licence product, £1,820 per property plus £159 for each bedroom over 5, paid as two £910 instalments, 'usually valid for 5 years'. There is no second fee line for a selective or additional licence, which a designated scheme would require. 'Selective' and 'additional licensing' are absent across the six-page HMO guide, all checked. IMPORTANT TRAP, the most consequential drafting issue found in this batch: the second limb quoted above is the s.257 converted-block description, and Broxbourne's page presents it as if it independently triggers a licence requirement. It does not. Mandatory licensing under the 2018 Prescribed Description Order catches only s.254 HMOs occupied by five or more persons in two or more households; s.257 converted blocks become licensable only where a council has made an additional licensing designation under s.56. This is a widespread council drafting shortcut, copying the statutory definition into the licensing criteria, and it is a strong false-positive generator because automated extraction reads it as direct evidence of an additional licensing scheme. No designation notice, consultation or committee decision was found anywhere on the domain, and the single-product fee schedule contradicts one existing. Recorded as no scheme, but note the council's own published wording overstates the requirement for converted blocks.

E07000136.research: The adopted SELCP Housing Standards HMO Licensing Policy (approved by Boston Cabinet, 27 January 2026) contains an explicit denial: "The Council do not currently operate an additional licensing scheme but maintain the right to introduce this if considered appropriate during the course of this policy." The policy contains zero occurrences of "selective". Selective licensing was considered in 2013 (options included Boston Town only and Boston Borough) and the council records: "After a major consultation exercise and consideration of all the factors Cabinet decided that licensing was not the appropriate way forward for the Council." A 2022 Task and Finish Group recommended only that Cabinet "Consider the introduction of a Selected Licensing Scheme for specific wards" - no wards named, no designation followed. Overview and Scrutiny, 17 June 2025: "It was agreed that further consideration should be given to the potential for additional licensing schemes... and that the matter should be revisited following the publication of statutory guidance under the Renters' Rights Bill." That is under consideration, not a formal proposal, so nothing is recorded as 'proposed'. The 2026-27 fees schedule lists only mandatory HMO fees (£300 plus £150 per unit). Note: policy is shared across the South and East Lincolnshire Councils Partnership (Boston, East Lindsey, South Holland).

E06000036.research: Rests principally on a complete council-published enumeration of licence types. The licensing index lists every licence the council issues (alcohol, animal, caravan site, charitable collections, commercial, explosives, petroleum, scrap metal, taxi and private hire, weighbridge, roads and street works, scaffolding, environmental permits, cooling tower) and the only property or housing entry in the whole list is 'Houses in multiple occupation licence'. Because that page is an exhaustive index rather than a topic page, the absence of any selective or additional property licence is positive evidence, not merely absence of mention. The living-standards page describes the Public Protection Partnership's functions as 'enforcing Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) management standards', 'licensing of HMOs' and 'providing an advisory service within certain areas of the private rented sector'. That last phrase describes advisory scope, NOT a designated licensing area, and is a plausible false-positive trigger. The XML sitemap contains no occurrence of 'selective', though this is corroborative only since the same sitemap also omits the HMO licensing page. STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: HMO licensing is delivered by the Public Protection Partnership, a shared service with West Berkshire, whose site returns HTTP 403 to all automated access and could not be read; any scheme document would most naturally sit there. Intrinsic risk is low: Bracknell Forest is a small, low-deprivation borough with a limited private rented sector.

E07000067.research: The licensing page states verbatim: 'If you own or are the landlord of a House in Multiple Occupation (HMO), you need a licence if it: is occupied by five or more persons living as more than one household; facilities such as bathroom, living room and kitchen are shared by the occupants.' The mandatory test only. The published 2026/27 fee table contains three lines and no others: new application £595.00, issue of licence £445.00 described as 'Maintenance and monitoring of licence fee. One off with up to 5 year life', and renewal £550.00. No selective or additional licence fee exists. Neither 'selective' nor 'additional licensing' appears on any page in the HMO section; pages 1 to 5 of the guide were checked programmatically. TRAP 1: the DEFINITION page describes an HMO as a property where 'there are three or more tenants who make up two or more households', and also covers s.257 converted blocks. That is the statutory DEFINITION of an HMO, not the licensing threshold. Automated extraction reading the definition page instead of the licensing page will wrongly infer a three-person additional licensing scheme. TRAP 2: the council's own URL slug contains a typographical error, 'occupatlon' spelled with a lowercase L rather than an i, so naive URL construction returns 404 and can cause automated checks to log this council as unverifiable when the page exists and is current.

E07000068.research: Under 'Do you need a licence?' the council states verbatim: 'Yes, a property is classed as a large HMO if it is occupied by five or more persons and it is occupied by persons living in more than one single household, with at least one tenant paying rent. A group of friends sharing a house will not be classed as a single household for licensing purposes.' Only the mandatory large-HMO test is given. Published fees are new licence £890 and renewal £603, with no selective or additional fee line, and 'A licence is issued for a period of five years'. The strings 'selective' and 'additional licensing' were tested for programmatically on the rendered page and are both absent. A site-restricted search returned only mandatory-HMO material: the HMO page, licensing index, fees and charges, registers of licences, private housing, other licensing, premises licences, the online application form and a 'Mandatory HMO Licensing Checklist' PDF. TRAP: Brentwood publishes a leaflet titled 'Property licence - Landlords - do you need a property licence?'. The generic phrase 'property licence' in that title is precisely the string that leads aggregators to record a borough-wide property licensing scheme. That PDF is a compressed scan whose text layer could not be extracted, so its body was not read; however every readable council page confirms mandatory HMO licensing only, the council's own checklist is explicitly titled 'Mandatory HMO Licensing Checklist', and no designation notice exists on the domain.

W06000013.research: NEGATIVE, and the council states it explicitly. Appendix 3 to Bridgend's Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Guidance, before Cabinet 03/02/2026, Council 04/02/2026 and Development Control Committee 05/02/2026, says under its Licensing heading: 'Mandatory HMO licensing: properties with 5 or more residents forming more than one household; comprising three or more storeys; and sharing basic amenities. / Additional or selective licensing schemes for smaller HMOs (not applied by Bridgend County Borough Council).' Licensing is delivered by Shared Regulatory Services, the joint statutory service of Bridgend, Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, linked directly from bridgend.gov.uk. The SRS HMO hub states: 'If your HMO has 3 or more storeys with five or more occupants made up of at least two households and is located anywhere in Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan or Bridgend area you will need a Mandatory HMO Licence. If you own or manage a HMO of any type or size in the Cathays or Plasnewydd area of Cardiff which is not subject to mandatory licensing, you will need to apply for an Additional HMO Licence. Similarly, if you own or manage a HMO which isn't subject to mandatory licensing in the Castleland Renewal Area in Vale of Glamorgan, you will need to apply for an Additional Licence. There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' Bridgend is named for mandatory only. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the SRS 'HMO Licensing in Bridgend' page gives the full ladder effective 1 April 2026 as 'Mandatory HMO Licence Fee: £792 / Mandatory HMO Licence Fee (Renewal): £657' with no small-HMO or per-property tier, and only two forms. Bridgend's corporate Licensing Fees 2026-27 spreadsheet has 12 sheets and zero HMO or housing rows. The Cardiff page on the same SRS site is a useful contrast control: where additional licensing exists, SRS names it and gives it its own fee ladder, so Bridgend's silence is meaningful rather than an omission. Independently verified: Bridgend's own 129KB HTML sitemap contains zero occurrences of 'selective licen' or 'additional licen', and its only 'Multiple Occupation' entry is a planning item. The A-to-Z passed a control and letter S contained no 'Selective' entry. ModernGov was CONTROL-VALIDATED ('zzqqxx' = 0, 'housing' = 29); 'selective licensing' returned only the HMO Supplementary Planning Guidance items. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Cardiff's Cathays and Plasnewydd additional licensing and the Vale's Castleland Renewal Area additional licensing, all published on the SAME SRS website and by far the biggest misattribution risk here; the HMO Supplementary Planning Guidance itself; the s.254 definition; Rent Smart Wales; the Welsh mandatory three-storey test. The Welsh site licensing index returned 47 'trwydd' hits but zero for 'dewisol', 'dethol', 'ychwanegol' or 'amlfedd'. LIMITATION: bridgend.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 522 on three attempts with browser headers, a genuine outage not a bot block; it is a stale host and the live system was searched successfully with validated controls.

E07000144.research: Broadland delivers regulatory services jointly with South Norfolk through a single shared website with district-specific fee pages. The Broadland-specific page lists the entire Broadland fee set and contains only mandatory HMO fees: 5-year licence for up to 5 lettings £835.88; additional fee for 6 lettings or more £38.91 per letting; renewal £835.88; licence changes £38.91. No selective or additional licensing fee exists for Broadland. The shared eligibility page states verbatim: 'You will need an HMO Licence when all the following apply to a property: there are five or more occupants; there is more than one household; occupants share facilities such as a kitchen, toilet or bathroom.' It adds 'Since 1st October 2018, a licence is needed for HMOs regardless of the number of floors in the property', a reference to the mandatory scheme extension, not a local designation. The HMO section comprises exactly six pages and neither 'selective' nor 'additional licensing' appears on any of them. TRAP 1: the section landing page recites the full statutory definition from 'sections 254 and 257 of the Housing Act 2004', including three-or-more-person HMOs and s.257 converted blocks; that is definition, not licensing scope. TRAP 2: the word 'Additional' appears in the Broadland fee table as 'Additional fee for 6 lettings or more', a per-letting surcharge on the mandatory licence, not an additional licensing scheme under s.56. This is a direct false-positive risk for keyword matching on fee tables. TRAP 3: because Broadland and South Norfolk share one domain, a scheme belonging to one district can be misattributed to the other; the fee page relied on here is explicitly the Broadland one.

E07000234.research: The council draws the definition and licensing distinction unusually clearly in its own words: 'Definition of an HMO: Any property which is occupied by at least 3 persons who are not members of the same household', followed immediately by 'To be a licensable HMO the property must be occupied by at least 5 persons who comprise of two or more households and share at least one basic amenity such as a bathroom or kitchen.' The page cross-refers to 'sections 254 to 259 of the Housing Act 2004' for the definition. Only the mandatory threshold is licensable. The strings 'selective' and 'additional licensing' were tested for programmatically and are absent. The related-pages list covers only inspections of HMOs, the public register, landlord fire risk assessment support, LACoRS fire safety guidance and Private Sector Housing contacts, with no designation or area-based scheme. A site-restricted search returned only mandatory-HMO material. TRAP: the '3 or more persons' definition sentence sits directly above the licensing sentence on the same page and is a likely source of scraped false positives suggesting a lowered, additional-licensing-style threshold. STRUCTURAL NOTE: Bromsgrove shares officers and some services with Redditch Borough Council, but publishes its own HMO licensing content on its own domain and it is mandatory-only.

E07000172.research: Confirmed by the council in its own committee papers. The business licence page states verbatim: 'If you rent out a house in multiple occupation (HMO) which is occupied by five or more people forming two or more households, you will require a licence from Broxtowe Borough Council. If granted, a licence will last up to five years.' Mandatory only; enforcement text cites s.72 and s.73 with no s.56 or Part 3 designation. The housing-side page (updated 21/05/2026) says 'HMO licensing scheme. Landlords must get a licence if the HMO has 5 or more unrelated people live in it who form 2 or more separate households'; note the bare phrase 'HMO licensing scheme' there is itself a false-positive risk for keyword scrapers. The council's own site search for 'selective licensing' returns 'No results found'; a search for 'additional licensing' returns only animal, alcohol and gambling licensing charges. DECISIVE: Broxtowe Cabinet, 21 July 2026, item 32.1 'Fit and Proper Person Policy - Private Sector Housing Licensing' (approved; policy created May 2026, next review July 2031). Its Scope section states: 'This policy applies to all properties requiring a licence under: Part 2 (HMO licensing). This policy would also be applicable to all properties requiring a licence under Part 3 (Selective Licensing) of the Housing Act 2004, if any such schemes are introduced.' The conditional 'if any such schemes are introduced' is a council-approved statement as at July 2026 that Broxtowe operates no Part 3 scheme. TRAP 1, high risk: the 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) SPD' is a Supplementary Planning Document controlling HMO concentration through the planning system, together with related Article 4 material; planning, not licensing, and it dominates automated HMO searches of this domain. TRAP 2, high risk: Broxtowe adjoins Nottingham City Council, which does operate large discretionary licensing, and Beeston, Stapleford, Kimberley and Eastwood are frequently conflated with Greater Nottingham in scraped data. TECHNICAL: broxtowe.gov.uk serves navigation-only HTML to plain fetchers and needs full browser rendering; /sitemap.xml returns 404 while the working path is /sitemap.

E06000060.research: Confirmed across the web estate, the statutory enforcement policy and the committee record. The canonical page states: 'A licence is required when a house in multiple occupation (HMO) is occupied by 5 or more persons in 2 or more households. On 1 October 2018 the scope of mandatory HMO licensing was extended. It now covers all HMOs with 5 or more persons, including, for example: flats; bungalows; two-storey properties.' 'Selective' and 'additional licens' were tested for programmatically and are absent. DECISIVE: the 39-page Housing Enforcement Policy was parsed in full and contains zero occurrences of 'selective', 'additional licensing', 'section 56', 'Part 3' or 'designation'. Its section 30 is headed 'Mandatory HMO Licence Enforcement'. A live discretionary scheme would necessarily appear in the statutory enforcement policy. Committee papers were searched: 'selective licensing' returns seven hits, all legacy Wycombe and Chiltern district papers dated 2003-2007 plus unrelated recent items; 'additional licensing' returns taxi unmet-demand surveys and Additional Restrictions Grant material. No designation report, consultation or cabinet decision. Fees are a single mandatory product: £500 non-refundable application fee, then £1,050 new or renewal for a 5-bedroom property, £1,575 through enforcement, £998 for landlord association members, £50 per additional bedroom. No selective or additional fee line. TRAP 1, high risk: the legacy district structure survives only as three administrative routes and three mandatory registers, 'View the Aylesbury Vale area HMO register', 'View the Chiltern and South Bucks area HMO register', 'View the Wycombe area HMO register'. These are s.232 mandatory registers, not evidence of three area-based designations, and 'area HMO register' is a strong false-positive trigger. TRAP 2: the Article 4 Directions page defines them purely as planning instruments and the current list of ten, including 'Four Ashes, High Wycombe' sealed 29 May 2024, contains zero mentions of HMO. RESIDUAL CAVEAT: a full-text crawl of every PDF in the pre-2020 legacy district committee archives was not performed, so an obscure historic designation cannot be mathematically excluded.

E08000002.research: Downgraded to unverified deliberately. The available evidence points to no scheme, but verification could not be made exhaustive and a confident negative is not justified for a high-stakes answer. WHAT WAS CONFIRMED: the HMO licence page sets out the mandatory test only, requiring a licence where the property 'is an entire house or flat which is let to three or more tenants who form two or more households' or 'is a house that's been converted entirely into bedsits', in each case subject to the occupancy test that 'five or more persons live at the property, including children' from 'two or more households' sharing a kitchen, bathroom or toilet. Fees are a single mandatory product: £685.50 base for up to 5 persons, £29.00 per additional letting unit, £66.00 multiple-application discount, £100.00 new licence holder consideration. No selective or additional licence fee. The complete private rented section was enumerated and contains only four sub-pages: Customers, Landlords, Landlord Forum and Private housing repairs. WHY THIS IS NOT ENOUGH: no keyword sweep of the domain was possible. bury.gov.uk serves an empty sitemap.xml with no URL entries; its on-site search ignores the query parameter entirely and returns the same unfiltered set of 2,541 results for any term, including a blank query; democracy.bury.gov.uk does not resolve and bury.moderngov.co.uk returns HTTP 403, so no committee cross-check was possible. The negative therefore rests solely on absence of mention within one small section, with no means of confirming that a selective licensing page does not exist elsewhere on the domain. TRAP 1: the 'three or more tenants who form two or more households' phrasing sits on the same page as the five-person occupancy test and reads out of context like a lowered threshold. TRAP 2: Bury is a Greater Manchester borough and several neighbours do operate selective licensing, which is both a known source of scraped false positives and a reason not to assert a negative on thin verification.

W06000018.research: NEGATIVE, sourced twice over. The council's HMO page states, in its own words: 'Certain HMOs are required to be licensed by the council, however very few actually exist within the county borough. Licensing is restricted to HMOs that are 3 or more storeys in height and house 5 or more tenants, made up from 2 or more families.' The phrase 'Licensing is restricted to', followed by the Welsh mandatory threshold, affirmatively excludes any wider designation. This page was read in a rendered browser session, reached through the real link graph (Housing > Private housing > Houses in multiple occupation); the raw page contains zero occurrences of 'additional licen' or 'selective licen'. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: 'We currently operate a mandatory licensing scheme and the fee is £250 for 5 years.' A single flat mandatory fee with no per-property or small-HMO tier and no separate application route; a self-financing s.56 or Part 3 designation could not exist without its own cost-recovery fee. Wayback shows stability rather than recent change: the fee sentence is byte-stable across snapshots of 23 Jul 2019, 25 Mar 2023 and 20 May 2024, and the HMO page has zero instances of 'selective' or 'additional licensing' in snapshots of 17 Jul 2016, 21 Aug 2019, 30 Mar 2023 and 26 Jan 2026. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2007' cited on the HMO page, which is the s.257 management instrument, the Welsh twin of the England 2007 regulations, not s.56; (2) 'certain additional requirements are necessary for these properties', management-standards wording; (3) on the Welsh site, 'gofynion ychwanegol' and '(Darpariaethau Ychwanegol) (Cymru) 2007', the same two traps in Welsh, with no instance of 'trwyddedu ychwanegol', 'trwyddedu dethol' or 'trwyddedu dewisol'; (4) the voluntary landlord accreditation page; (5) Housing renewal and Private Sector Renewal Strategy pages, which are grants and regeneration; (6) Rent Smart Wales. LIMITATIONS, stated plainly: caerphilly.gov.uk serves SOFT 404s (Kentico returns HTTP 200 with homepage content for unknown paths, confirmed by fetching /robots.txt and receiving the homepage), so URL guessing is actively misleading and the real link graph was navigated instead. Its site search is broken and this was proved with controls: 'council tax', 'multiple occupation', 'selective licensing' and 'zzqqxxvv' all returned exactly 47,559 bytes, so a nil result there proves nothing. caerphilly.moderngov.co.uk returns 522; democracy.caerphilly.gov.uk is up but shares the broken search behaviour, so committee papers were not full-text searchable.

E08000033.research: The HMO page states that properties must be licensed if 'they are occupied by five or more people from two or more households; and there is a shared amenity, such as a kitchen, bathroom or toilet.' The mandatory test only; no ward, area, street or designation is mentioned. It confirms licensing 'is paid for in two stages' and warns that operating without a required licence carries penalties up to £30,000, prosecution, rent repayment orders or inclusion on the rogue landlords database, all mandatory-scheme consequences. The parent section contains only four items: the HMO page, fire safety for landlords, the lettings redress scheme and the housing enforcement policy. Unlike some councils in this batch, Calderdale's own site search is functional and was used: a search for 'selective licensing' returns no housing licensing results at all, only an unrelated land-charges page. TRAP, high risk and actively observed: third-party aggregators publish Calderdale selective licensing landing pages, including one titled 'Selective licensing in Calderdale: streets, fees, postcode check'. These rank in general search results and are a live false-positive source. When one was opened to trace its sourcing, its own body text concedes 'Calderdale does not currently list an active selective scheme', and the only Calderdale source it cites is the mandatory HMO page above. The scheme exists in the page title and URL only. This is precisely the failure mode where a URL and heading assert a scheme the underlying council evidence does not support. TECHNICAL: calderdale.gov.uk /v2/ URLs now 301-redirect to new.calderdale.gov.uk, so stale links return 404. LIMITATION: the Housing Enforcement Policy July 2023 PDF could not be text-extracted, so it was not possible to confirm from the policy document itself which Part 2 and Part 3 powers Calderdale has designated; the public pages and the working site search are consistent in showing none.

E07000008.research: The council's full A-Z of licences lists 26 licence types; the only property-related entries are 'Licensing of houses in multiple occupation' and a register of Temporary Exemption Notices. No additional or selective licensing entry exists. The HMO page states a licence is needed where the property 'is occupied by five or more people forming two or more separate households, or it is a purpose-built flat in a block of up to two flats and occupied as an HMO by five or more people' - verbatim the national mandatory test under Part 2 s.55 as extended by the 2018 Order, not a local designation. Fee explicitly labelled mandatory: £1,133 for 2026-27 (£736 on application, £397 on grant; reduced £603 application fee for renewals submitted 8+ weeks early). FALSE POSITIVE RISK: Cambridge is a high-density student city and scraped datasets routinely assume additional licensing exists here. It does not. Anything reported is most likely the mandatory scheme mislabelled, or planning-side HMO control, which is not licensing.

E07000192.research: The HMO page states licensing is compulsory for properties with 'five or more people in more than one household and share amenities such as bathrooms, toilets and cooking facilities' - the national test only. Fee £1,028.55 per property, split £375.45 and £653.10, with £375.45 refunded if refused; licences last 5 years. The complete Private Sector Housing section navigation was enumerated: Damp and Mould; Houses of Multiple Occupation; Housing Standards and Disrepair; Minimum Energy Efficiency; Mobile Home Sites Fit and Proper Person; Redress Scheme (Lettings); Staffordshire Warm Homes Fund; Energy Company Obligation. No selective or additional licensing page exists. FALSE POSITIVE RISK: the 'Redress Scheme (Lettings)' and 'Mobile Home Sites Fit and Proper Person' pages are separate statutory regimes, not Housing Act 2004 Part 2/3 designations, and are sometimes miscounted by scrapers as licensing schemes.

E07000106.research: The licensing page sets out only the national mandatory test: a licence is needed where a property 'is rented to five or more people who form more than one household' and 'some or all tenants share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities'. It also catches 'purpose-built flats of no more than two units' and exempts blocks of three or more and Specified Educational Establishments. All national regime, no local designation. The full XML sitemap was parsed: the HMO subsection contains only find-out-if-you-need-hmo-licence, change-use-property-hmo, apply-hmo-licence, hmo-standards, hmo-fire-safety and view-register-licensed-hmos. MAJOR FALSE POSITIVE RISK: Canterbury operates an HMO Article 4 Direction; its own page says 'you need planning permission to change the use of a house from a C3 dwelling house to a C4 HMO' and points landlords to a planning mapping tool. That is town-and-country planning control, NOT Housing Act 2004 licensing. As a student city, Canterbury is frequently and wrongly listed by aggregators as having additional licensing.

W06000015.research: CATHAYS: primary designation instrument obtained. Cardiff's own public notice reads: 'Notice is hereby given that the City of Cardiff Council has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of houses in multiple occupation covering the Cathays Community Ward. This scheme will be known as (The City of Cardiff Council's Houses in Multiple Occupation Additional Licensing Scheme 2023). The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The designation was made at the Council's Cabinet Meeting on 20th October 2022... The Scheme will be effective from 1st February 2023 and unless revoked beforehand will cease to have effect on 1st February 2028.' Unambiguous s.56, live today. PLASNEWYDD, THE JUDGEMENT CALL: SRS states 'The Plasnewydd Scheme first came into effect on 3 November 2014 and again went live on 1 January 2021 for a period of 5 years.' By the council's own arithmetic, and by the exact pattern the Cathays notice uses, that term ended on 1 January 2026, seven months ago. No re-designation could be found. Every Cardiff Cabinet agenda for 2024, 2025 and 2026 was scanned (33 meetings) for 'plasnewydd', 'additional licens', 'selective licens', 'multiple occupation' and 'HMO'; the only hit was a School Organisation Planning item. That scan is CONTROL-VALIDATED, since the same parser extracts real agenda item titles from those pages, and the Cathays precedent shows Cardiff makes these designations at Cabinet. RECORDED AS EXPIRED BUT FLAGGED LOUDLY, because the council still presents it in the present tense ('Cardiff Council has declared two areas within Cardiff as Additional Licensing Schemes, namely Cathays and Plasnewydd') and the SRS hub still tells landlords in 'the Cathays or Plasnewydd area' they need an Additional HMO Licence. The linked 'Public Notice Plasnewydd HMO Licensing Scheme' is a BROKEN LINK on the council's own site, pointing at an unrelated 2020 standards document, so no Plasnewydd instrument is publicly available. The public note therefore tells a Plasnewydd landlord to check with Cardiff rather than assume they are clear. SELECTIVE LICENSING: expressly ruled out. SRS states 'There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' Cardiff's own sitemap (1,151 URLs) contains no selective or additional licensing page at all. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, strongly positive: Cardiff's ladder includes 'HMO Shared House or single flat up to 4 bedrooms: Initial Application fee £160, 2nd payment if compliant £230, Total fee compliant £390' rising to £460 at 15+ bedrooms, or £810 to £960 if non-compliant, plus per-flat surcharges. A four-bedroom tier sits BELOW the mandatory five-occupant threshold, which is exactly the small-HMO tell of a genuine s.56 scheme, and the application form is captioned 'both mandatory and additional applications can be completed on the same form'. WARDS: 'Cathays' and 'Plasnewydd' were both checked against the current ONS register via the repo's bundled wards.json and BOTH ARE CURRENT Cardiff wards, so matching is safe in both directions. TRAPS EXCLUDED: cardiff.gov.uk/HMOlicence is a PLANNING page, not licensing, opening 'This information refers to HMOs within the Planning system' before discussing use classes C4 and Sui Generis, LDP policy H5 and the 20 per cent / 10 per cent concentration thresholds for Cathays and Plasnewydd; that concentration policy is planning control and is a strong lookalike for a licensing boundary. Also excluded: the s.254 definition; Rent Smart Wales; and the Vale of Glamorgan's Castleland Renewal Area additional licensing, which appears on the same SRS site and belongs to a different council. LIMITATION: Cardiff's ModernGov document search is unusable via GET (identical empty responses for 'council tax', 'Plasnewydd', 'additional licensing' and a nonsense control), so meeting lists were browsed directly. Note also that srs.wales is not itself a .gov.uk domain; it is the statutory joint regulatory service of Cardiff, Bridgend and the Vale, and cardiff.gov.uk links to it as the authoritative HMO licensing destination.

W06000010.research: CURRENT POSITION, from the council directly: the live Licensing page (updated 04/02/2026) states 'We currently operate one licensing schemes for privately rented properties in Carmarthenshire - a mandatory licensing scheme for houses in multiple occupation (HMO)... Mandatory licensing applies across the whole of Carmarthenshire.' THE EXPIRED SELECTIVE SCHEME was found ONLY by grepping the WELSH-language page, which names the statutory type the English page conceals: 'Ar hyn o bryd rydym yn gweithredu dau gynllun trwyddedu - trwyddedu gorfodol ar gyfer tai amlfeddiannaeth a TRWYDDEDU DETHOL sy'n benodol ar gyfer Ward Ty-isa yn Llanelli.' LEXICAL POINT FOR ALL FUTURE WELSH WORK: the statutory Welsh term in use is 'trwyddedu DETHOL', not the 'trwyddedu dewisol' commonly assumed; searching only for 'dewisol' would have missed this entirely. The English twin page says only the uninformative 'licensing specific to the Tyisha Ward in Llanelli'. Archived copies of the council's own licensing page confirm type and end date verbatim and unchanged across snapshots of 1 Dec 2020, 26 Feb 2021, 18 May 2022 and 29 Mar 2023: 'We currently have one Selective Licensing Scheme in operation, in the Tyisha ward of Llanelli. It will last until July 2, 2019, and complements a Local Lettings Policy which is also in place for council housing in Tyisha.' The council left that paragraph up for roughly five years after its own stated expiry. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, which is what distinguishes a genuine Part 3 designation from boilerplate: those archived pages carry a separate cost-recovery table headed 'Licence fees within a Selective Licensing Scheme area' (Single Household Occupation £240, 2 Flats £360, 3 Flats £480, 4 Flats £600, 5 Flats £720, with LAW-affiliated discounts), together with the correct statutory description 'All privately rented properties within a selective licensing area have to be licensed, regardless of whether the property is an HMO.' Snapshot diffing dates the removal: the wording is present on 21 Apr 2024 and gone by 19 Apr 2025. START DATE NOT VERIFIED: the earliest capture of any Carmarthenshire licensing page is 1 Dec 2020. A Part 3 designation runs a statutory maximum of five years, which would imply commencement on or about 3 July 2014, but no council document states it, so it is recorded as null rather than asserted. LIVE CORROBORATION that nothing is active: the HMO public register lists only three licensed properties and every row's licence-type column reads 'Mandatory'. WARD: 'Tyisha' was checked against the current ONS register and IS a current Carmarthenshire ward, so matching is safe; the Welsh form 'Ty-isa' is not and must not be used as a key. STALE COUNCIL PAGE, FLAG THIS: the letting-your-property page (updated 21/04/2026, NEWER than the authoritative licensing page) still reads 'We currently operate two licensing schemes - mandatory licensing for houses in multiple occupation, and licensing specific to the Tyisha Ward in Llanelli.' A landlord reading only that page would wrongly conclude a selective scheme is live. The licensing page, the fee schedule and the public register all agree it is gone. E07000069.research: The HMO page states that 'an HMO licence is required when a property is rented out to five or more people who, together, form more than one household where some or all tenants share some facilities such as a toilet, bathroom or kitchen' - the national test verbatim, no local designation. N09000004.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). Causeway Coast and Glens therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Northern Ireland district councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply NI-wide instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Private Tenancies (Northern Ireland) Order 2006 art.65A: all landlords letting under a private tenancy must register. Registration lasts 3 years and costs £70 online or £80 on paper, with a £500 fixed penalty or a court fine up to £2,500. ADMINISTRATION CHANGED RECENTLY: Councils since 1 March 2025, with Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council as lead/host council for all 11 NI councils (previously the Department for Communities). (2) HMO LICENSING under the Houses in Multiple Occupation Act (Northern Ireland) 2016 s.1: 3+ persons as only or main residence forming more than two households, rent payable by at least one. A single NIHMO Unit at Belfast City Council administers HMO licensing on behalf of all 11 NI councils, and can take enforcement action for all of them, so a landlord in Causeway Coast and Glens does not apply to their own council. Licences run 5 years. Statutory maximum rose from £45 to £75 per person per annum on 1 August 2025 (SR 2025/124). Belfast currently charges £62 per person per year, so £310 per person over a 5-year licence. Penalties run to a £5,000 fixed penalty and £20,000 on summary conviction. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: NARROWER THAN ENGLAND: NI requires MORE THAN TWO households (i.e. 3+). Three sharers from two households are an HMO in England but NOT in NI. PLANNING: Planning permission is also required for a new HMO; Belfast will not process a licence application without it.

E06000056.research: Three separate council indexes checked, none containing a selective or additional scheme. (1) The housing policy register lists exactly four private-sector policies: a 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing Policy', a Housing Enforcement Policy (under review), a Rogue Landlords Database Policy, and a Civil Penalty Policy under the Renters' Rights Act 2025. No selective licensing policy or designation document. (2) The licensing A-Z lists 16 licence types (alcohol, taxi, food, gambling, animal, fireworks, charity collections, sex establishments, weighbridge, highways, petroleum, street trading, approved premises, scrap metal, tattooist, pavement) and contains no residential property licensing entry at all. (3) The full housing navigation was enumerated and contains no HMO, selective or additional licensing page; 'Services for landlords' covers only the Landlords' Forum, home improvement loans, private lettings and tax advice. LOWEST CONFIDENCE IN BATCH: this is a negative by exhaustive absence, not an explicit denial. Central Bedfordshire publishes no public-facing HMO licensing page at all; its HMO Licensing Policy sits behind a SharePoint link that could not be read. Re-check if a definitive page appears.

W06000008.research: ACTIVE s.56 scheme, designation instrument obtained. CRITICAL SCOPING POINT: the common assumption that this is an 'Aberystwyth-only' student scheme is WRONG and dangerously so. The designation has two limbs. Paragraph 4(a) applies a three-or-more-persons / three-or-more-households test in eight Aberystwyth-area wards. Paragraph 4(b) applies to 'The whole of the County of Ceredigion' for HMOs with five or more persons in two or more households (ANY number of storeys, so it bites below the Welsh mandatory three-storey test) and for s.257 converted flats. Recording this with coverage 'wards' would falsely clear every landlord in Cardigan, Lampeter, Aberaeron and New Quay, so it is recorded as borough-wide with wards null, and the stricter Aberystwyth tier is described in areaDescription instead. WARD STALENESS, THE REASON WARDS ARE NULL: although made on 19 March 2024, the designation reuses PRE-2022 ward names and its Annex A map is stamped 'Printed on: 2018-11-28'. The eight named are Aberystwyth Bronglais, Aberystwyth Central, Aberystwyth North, Aberystwyth Penparcau, Aberystwyth Rheidol, Faenor, Llanbadarn Fawr Padarn and Llanbadarn Fawr Sulien. All eight were checked against the current ONS register via the repo's bundled wards.json: FIVE NO LONGER EXIST (Aberystwyth Bronglais, Aberystwyth Central, Aberystwyth North, Llanbadarn Fawr Padarn, Llanbadarn Fawr Sulien); only Aberystwyth Penparcau, Aberystwyth Rheidol and Faenor survive. The current register instead carries 'Aberystwyth Morfa a Glais' and a single 'Llanbadarn Fawr'. Putting that list in the wards field would have produced silent mismatches in both directions. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the 1 April 2026 schedule carries a SEPARATE line, 'Additional HMO licensing fee per habitable room (for those not subject to mandatory fee) - New Licence £334.00 / Renewal £281.00', alongside the distinct mandatory line, with a 50 per cent discount for ANUK-compliant university HMOs; the application form is titled 'Mandatory and Additional Licensing Application Form'. THREE EXPIRED PREDECESSORS establish a long-running rolling regime: 2009-04-01 to 2014-03-31 (county-wide); 2014-04-14 to 2019-04-13 (Aberystwyth, Llanbadarn Fawr, Borth, Llanfarian and LAMPETER, which was covered then and is not in the three-person tier now); and 2019-04-14 to 2024-04-14. There is a genuine gap of about three months between the third and fourth designations caused by the three-month notice requirement, which is why the current start is 10 July 2024 rather than mid-April. MOST DANGEROUS TRAP FOUND: Ceredigion's own Additional Licensing Review 2023, page 11, contains the phrase 'The Housing Act 2004 (SELECTIVE Licensing) (Wales) General Approval 2007'. This is a COUNCIL TYPO. The same sentence continues '...may introduce an ADDITIONAL Licensing Scheme without obtaining Assembly approval', and the designation instrument itself cites the correct '(Additional HMO Licensing) (Wales) General Approval 2007'. A keyword search would misread this as a live Part 3 scheme; Ceredigion has never operated selective licensing. OTHER TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales; Welsh mandatory HMO licensing under WSI 2006/1712 (W.174), which because of the retained three-storey element already catches many Aberystwyth student houses independently; the s.254 definitional recitals; statutory-power recitals; per-room surcharges; and Article 4 and planning permission requirements discussed for Aberystwyth. The s.257 coverage is NOT the England '(Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' trap: the instrument cites the Wales 2006 Regulations and s.56 directly. LIMITATIONS: Ceredigion's ModernGov search returns blank forms, worked around via cabinet papers on the corporate site; the 2019 designation PDF is gone from both the live site and Wayback, so the third scheme's dates rest on the cabinet report, and the council's own documents are internally inconsistent about it. The council's site search itself passed its control tests, and sitemap raw-HTML greps for 'selectiv' and 'dewisol' returned zero, backed by a Wayback CDX sweep showing no selective-licensing URL ever existed on the domain.

E07000070.research: The council states this explicitly on its own HMO licensing page: 'We do not have Additional or Selective licensing schemes in place.' Fees £900 for up to 5 units then £55 per additional unit (worked example: an 8-unit HMO costs £1,065). Licences run 5 years, determination target 12 weeks. E07000078.research: The HMO page describes only the national mandatory regime: a licence is needed where a property is 'occupied by five or more people, forming two or more households AND tenants share facilities such as kitchen or bathrooms'. E07000177.research: The HMO licensing page sets out a three-part test that is the national mandatory regime word for word: 'It is occupied by five or more people; and Those people form two or more households; and The HMO is not a purpose-built, self-contained flat situated in a block comprising three or more self-contained flats.' E06000049.research: The HMO page states: 'If a HMO is occupied by 5 or more people who form two or more households, there should be a HMO licence in place', applying to buildings, converted flats and purpose-built blocks of up to two flats. E07000118.research: The mandatory HMO licence page states: 'a landlord must have a licence for a privately rented HMO if the property being rented out: is occupied by 5 people or more those people form 2 or more households tenants share some amenities like kitchen, bathroom or laundry.' E08000032.council: City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council
E08000032.research: Unusually well evidenced. The eligibility page states a licence is required for HMOs 'occupied by five or more people, including children' and 'occupied by two or more households' - the mandatory s.55 and Prescribed Description Order 2018 test and nothing else, with no area, ward, street or designation referenced. DECISIVE: the current fee schedule 'HMO licence fees 2026-2027' prices only mandatory licences, banded purely by occupancy: 5-7 occupiers £1,625.05 total, 8-14 occupiers £1,706.32, 15+ occupiers £1,787.56, each split into an initial and a final fee. A live selective or additional designation would necessarily carry its own published fee under s.63 or s.87; there is none. The complete housing navigation was enumerated, 80 links, and every HMO page is mandatory-only: Houses in Multiple Occupation, What is an HMO?, Information for tenants, Register of HMO Licences, Do I need a HMO licence?, Applying for a HMO Licence, Standards and requirements, HMO licence fees 2026-2027. No selective licensing page exists in the housing tree or the business licensing tree. TRAP WARNING: Bradford is a large, deprived West Yorkshire district of exactly the profile that commonly does operate selective licensing, and several neighbouring authorities do, which makes it a high-risk false positive in scraped datasets and in general model recall. The council-published fee schedule is the strongest available disproof and is the citation of record. LIMITATION: the committee system returns HTTP 403 to automated access, so no committee-paper cross-check was possible.

S12000036.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). City of Edinburgh therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.

E07000071.research: The strongest negative in this batch, because the council states it in terms rather than merely omitting it: 'We do not operate additional or selective HMO licensing and there are no Article 4 directions relating to HMOs within the City.' The same page defines licensable stock as properties that 'Are occupied by 5 or more people; Who form 2 or more households; And who generally share 1 or more basic amenity'. Cross-checked against the general HMO guidance page, which repeats the mandatory threshold and mentions no designation. Note the council's sentence also rules out an Article 4 direction, which is planning control over HMO conversion and is not licensing at all. URL TRAP: the canonical path www.colchester.gov.uk/licensing/other-licences/house-multiple-occupation-licensing returns HTTP 404; the live page is served from the new.colchester.gov.uk host.
