E06000026.research: Plymouth initially returned HTTP 403 to every request; per method that was treated as a bot block rather than evidence and retried with a browser user-agent via curl, which got straight through. The 403 was indeed a block. FEE TEST, decisive: the HMO licence application page carries the complete published schedule under 'Cost': 'Initial Application (Full Fee) £1,097', 'Initial Application (discounted fee for holding accreditation) £982', 'Renewal Application (Full Fee) £1,040', 'Renewal Application (discounted fee for holding accreditation) £924'. The page opens 'To reduce sharing problems and to ensure multiple occupancy homes are of a decent standard, landlords need a licence for a large House in Multiple Occupation (HMO).' Large HMOs only. No Part 3 line, no s.56 line, no per-property private-rented licensing fee. LICENSABILITY TEST: the HMO page states 'A HMO is likely to be licensable if all of the following apply: At least 5 people live there forming more than one household [and] It is a HMO'. NAVIGATION TEST: the landlords hub links only to Houses in Multiple Occupation, Private rented accommodation safety, Rent a room in your home and Renters' Rights Act 2025. SITEMAP TEST, the strongest structural evidence: the sitemap index and all three sub-sitemaps were pulled, 5,899 URLs in total, and ZERO contain 'selective'. The only property-licensing URLs on the entire domain are /houses-multiple-occupation-hmo, /apply-house-multiple-occupation-hmo-licence, /hmo-standards, /hmo-register-and-unlicenced-hmos, /standards-and-managing-hmo and /planning-permission-and-houses-multiple-occupation-hmo. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4, confirmed present exactly as warned. The planning page states 'In some areas and for specific buildings we've removed these rights by introducing an Article 4 Direction ... This means you'll have to apply for planning permission if you want to change a house (C3) to a small HMO (C4) in the following neighbourhoods', with a named-neighbourhood list and an areas map. It names neighbourhoods and carries commencement, so it reads like a designation, but it is permitted-development control and NOT Housing Act licensing. (2) THE s.254 DEFINITION, present on the same site and the classic conflation risk: the HMO page opens 'A building, or part of a building, is likely to be a House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) if both of the following apply: at least 3 people live there, forming more than one household [and] they share a toilet, bathroom or kitchen'. That is the definition; the licensable threshold, stated separately on the same page, is at least five people. (3) The accreditation discount on the fee table is a voluntary-scheme discount on a mandatory licence, not a separate regime. LIMITATIONS: Plymouth's Drupal site search is fuzzy and stemmed and cannot deliver a meaningful nil return; the single word 'selective' returned 97 results led by 'Library market day at St Budeaux Library' and a procurement climate statement, so it carried no weight and the sitemap sweep was relied on instead. democracy.plymouth.gov.uk failed TLS certificate verification, so committee papers could not be full-text searched; a very recent cabinet report proposing a future designation would not necessarily have surfaced, though it would not change a landlord's obligation today.

W06000023.research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST IS DECISIVE: the entire housing licence fee page reads 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Fees. Mandatory HMO Licence Fees: The Basic licence fee is £750 for up to 5 rooms and must be paid in full with the application. There will be an additional charge for 6 - 10 rooms of £25 per room, 11 or more rooms will attract an additional charge of £40 per room.' A MANDATORY-ONLY ladder with a per-room surcharge, no flat per-property fee, no small-HMO fee and no separate application route. The HMO licensing page says only 'Landlords that own certain types of HMO have to apply for a licence' and never names a designation, area or dates. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED, STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL: the Enforcement and Complaints page states 'The Housing Act 2004 also allows for HMOs to be inspected and if necessary be licenced under either mandatory or additional HMO Licensing Schemes with associated fees... Local Authorities also have discretion to introduce additional licensing of other HMOs falling outside the scope of mandatory licensing... Note: it is an offence to operate a Mandatory HMO or a HMO covered by an Additional HMO Licensing Scheme without a licence.' This describes the POWER and the GENERIC OFFENCE, never its exercise in Powys. Read alone it would produce a false positive, and it is the single most dangerous passage on the site. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED, RENT SMART WALES: Powys has two RSW pages and the enforcement page says 'From October 2015, the Welsh Government introduced a new Welsh scheme requiring landlords of all rented property, regardless of size, to hold a licence and pay a fee.' That is the Housing (Wales) Act 2014 national regime, and is precisely why a Powys landlord can correctly be told they need 'a licence' while no local designation exists. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: the '£25/£40 additional charge per room', a surcharge on a MANDATORY licence. TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: the s.254 DEFINITION ('let to 3 or more tenants who form 2 or more households'). TRAP NAMED AND EXCLUDED: 'Additional Learning Needs' and 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' pages, which dominate the sitemap on the token 'additional' and 'ychwanegol'. EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE: (a) the full sitemap (3,779 URLs) grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol' and 'licen' contains no selective or additional licensing page; (b) THE SITE SEARCH PASSED BOTH CONTROLS, the positive control 'multiple occupation' returning 126 results including both HMO pages, and the nonsense NEGATIVE CONTROL returning zero results with no results block; against that working engine 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing' returned only OR-matched generic licensing pages with no scheme page, so this nil result is genuine evidence; (c) the ModernGov committee document search ALSO PASSED its negative control, and 'selective licensing' returned just two irrelevant results (Taxi Licensing Sub-Committee minutes 30/01/2025; Local Housing Strategy 2016-2020, Cabinet 22/03/2016), while 'additional licensing scheme' returned only Building Control charges and planning applications. No designation exists in the committee record. Other landlord pages checked and clear. The Welsh mandatory threshold is confirmed in the council's own words: 'a three-storey building with five or more persons in occupation who share facilities'. LIMITATIONS: no 403s or bot blocks were encountered; Powys serves 302 redirects to a cookie-consent URL but full content returns with -L --compressed.

E07000236.research: The landlords page states 'To be a licensable HMO the property must be occupied by at least 5 persons who comprise of two or more households and share at least one basic amenity such as a bathroom or kitchen' and 'The HMO licence is usually issued for a period of up to 5 years and the fee is £163.90 per person.' A single mandatory per-person fee with no selective or s.56 counterpart anywhere on the site. CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy, section 8 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licensing', describes mandatory licensing only, with no Part 3, selective, additional or designation anywhere in the document. SHARED-SERVICE RISK CLEARED: Worcestershire Regulatory Services was checked and ruled out as a possible holder of a scheme. The WRS licensing index covers alcohol and entertainment, animals, pavement, taxi, tax conditionality, gambling and public registers, with NO housing or HMO licensing at all. Redditch's own Private Sector Housing Team runs housing licensing. BROMSGROVE KEPT SEPARATE: Bromsgrove publishes a different fee, '£156.80 per person', on the same mandatory five-person test with no scheme. The distinct figures confirm the two authorities were not conflated in either direction. FEE-SCHEDULE CAVEAT, stated honestly: the corporate Licensing fees and charges 2026-2027 PDF (9 pages, text extracted) contains NO housing or HMO line at all, covering only taxi and private hire, animal activity, zoo, dangerous wild animals, skin piercing, gambling, street trading, scrap metal, sex establishments, pavement licences and hypnotism. Housing fees sit outside that schedule, so its silence is weak evidence and is not the basis of this finding. The probative fee is the single £163.90 per person mandatory figure. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) s.254 definition: the resident-facing HMO page says 'at least 3 tenants live there, forming more than 1 household', while the licensing pages state five or more. (2) A STALE MANDATORY TEST: the enforcement policy still says 'HMOs of three or more storeys, with five or more occupants require a licence', which is the pre-October 2018 wording. That indicates an out-of-date document, not an additional licensing scheme. (3) 'HMO Grants - £25k' in the 2025-26 Financial Plan capital programme is a landlord grant budget line, not a scheme. (4) 'Additional' used as a surcharge word in unrelated fees, e.g. 'Private hire operator licence (per additional vehicle)'. LIMITATIONS: Redditch's own site search is BROKEN and its nil return was discarded; it returned 'No results match your search' for 'selective licensing' and ALSO for the control term 'HMO', despite HMO pages plainly existing. Committee papers were unreachable: moderngov.redditchbc.gov.uk and moderngov.bromsgroveandredditch.gov.uk do not resolve in DNS, and redditch.moderngov.co.uk returned 403. General web search was unavailable and external engines were bot-blocked; because the DuckDuckGo control query never completed, its apparent nil return was not treated as evidence. Residual risk is a designation made very recently and not yet reflected on the website or in the fees.

E07000211.research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE, high confidence, resting on a complete published fee schedule. THRESHOLD: the HMO page states 'HMOs which accommodate five or more persons in two or more households (sharing facilities) require a licence, irrespective of the number of storeys in the building.' FEE TEST, decisive: every row of the 2026/2027 environmental health fees and charges table was captured. The only licensing rows relevant to rented housing are 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) | Five yearly - per property (new application) | £1082 | Licence' and 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) | Five yearly - per property (renewal) | £1082 | Licence'. The remainder is EIR requests, food hygiene revisits, Mobile Home Sites (16 rows), Private Water Supply and Property Inspections. There is NO selective, Part 3, additional or private rented sector licensing row in the current published schedule. A live Part 3 or s.56 scheme is required to be self-financing and would have to carry its own cost-recovery fee; none exists. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, the main risk for this council: Croydon operates borough-wide schemes and directly adjoins Reigate and Banstead. No Croydon material was used or relied on, and the same applies to Epsom and Ewell, Mole Valley, Tandridge and Crawley. (2) 'Property Inspections | Officer Time for Housing Act Enforcement | £65 | Per hour' and 'Formal Notices | £486 | Per notice' are HHSRS enforcement cost recovery under Part 1 of the Housing Act 2004, not a licensing scheme. (3) Mobile Home Sites licensing, including a 'Fit and Proper Person' fee, sits under the Caravan Sites and Control of Development Act and the Mobile Homes Act 2013. A separate regime, neither Part 2 nor Part 3. (4) The £65 register copy fee is administrative. The register itself 'does not distinguish between mandatory, additional, or selective licences', so it is neutral evidence and was not read as positive. (5) 'Landlords of houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) also have additional responsibilities relating to the management of their property' uses 'additional' in a management sense, not s.56. LIMITATIONS: reigate-banstead.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 403 on every path attempted, so cabinet reports could not be scanned. No working site-search endpoint could be found (/search and /search/ both 404), and the consultations pages returned placeholder or mismatched content, so consultation history could not be swept for a proposed-but-never-designated scheme. General web search was unavailable and all external engines were bot-blocked; a DuckDuckGo nil return was obtained but its control query never completed, so it was not treated as evidence. Residual risk is a very recent designation not yet reflected on the site or in the 2026/2027 fees. Noted in passing that Reigate and Banstead is currently running a Community Governance Review and a Local Government Reorganisation process, which would become relevant to ward matching only if a designation were ever made.

W06000016.research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, BOROUGH-WIDE. THE PUBLIC NOTICE WAS VERIFIED VERBATIM by fetching the page with browser headers and extracting the body text: 'Notice is hereby given that on the 21st December 2023 Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of Houses in Multiple Occupation covering all electoral wards in Rhondda Cynon Taf... The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Section 56 - 60 of The Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The Scheme to which the designation applies has General Approval of the Welsh Assembly Government under the Housing Act 2004 (Additional HMO Licensing Wales) General Approval 2007... The Scheme applies to all Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) within the area described above, except those exempted by the relevant sections of the Act and those licensable under the Orders and Regulations made pursuant to Section 55 (2)(a) of the Housing Act 2004 (Mandatory Licensing). The Scheme will be effective from 1st April 2024 and unless revoked beforehand or extended will cease to have effect on 31st March 2029. The Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2009 shall be revoked on the 31st March 2024. All licences issued under this scheme that remain in force at 31st March 2024 shall transfer to the new scheme and remain valid until they expire or are otherwise revoked by the Council or are surrendered.' IMPORTANT DOCUMENT DEFECT, FLAGGED: the notice mislabels the scheme as the 'Scheme 2014'. That is plainly a stale copy-paste in the council's own text; the designation was confirmed on 21 December 2023, runs 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2029, and revokes a 'Scheme 2009'. The OPERATIVE DATES are unambiguous and are what has been recorded; the citation name must not be relied on and must not be read as evidence of a 2014 scheme. COVERAGE: the notice says 'covering all electoral wards in Rhondda Cynon Taf', so coverage is borough-wide with wards NULL. This is the safe encoding: it avoids enumerating ward names entirely, so the major Welsh ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections cannot break matching in either direction. CONTINUITY: the predecessor 2009 scheme was revoked on 31 March 2024 and the new scheme took effect on 1 April 2024, so there was NO GAP in cover, and existing licences were expressly transferred. The 2009 scheme is recorded as expired with end 2024-03-31 as quoted; its start date is not stated in this notice and the 2009 designation itself was not retrieved, so start is null and its coverage is inferred from it being the direct predecessor rather than independently verified. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, EVIDENCED: the full RCT sitemap was swept (7,951 URLs, both EN and CY trees) and grepped for 'selectiv' and 'dewisol'. ZERO hits in either language. E07000124.research: This is 'we checked and found nothing' plus a positive fee-schedule test, not an affirmative council denial, because Ribble Valley publishes no equivalent of Rochford's explicit statement. And we don't have that so we don't actually meet the criteria for a selective licensing scheme for landlords.' E07000075.research: VERIFIED NEGATIVE with an explicit, dated, primary-source denial of both regimes, the strongest evidence in this batch. E09000021.council: Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames
E09000021.research: HIGH PRIORITY council, verified twice independently, both passes agreeing. Kingston is an exception to the usual London-borough pattern of running additional licensing. DECISIVE QUOTE: 'You'll only need a licence if your property has 5 or more people forming 2 or more households and sharing facilities'. The word 'only' plus the 5-person threshold rules out an additional licensing designation, which by definition captures smaller HMOs. The page also confirms 'Purpose-built blocks with 3+ flats don't require licensing'. FEE CORROBORATION: '£319.40 per letting for a new licence' and '£250 per letting to renew', with a £100 discount for accreditation members on new applications, 50 per cent for registered charities, and a £300 late-renewal penalty. Exactly one fee stream. SITEMAP SWEEP, decisive structural evidence: both pages of the sitemap were retrieved in full and the entire site contains ONE property licensing page, the mandatory HMO page. No URL containing 'selective' or 'additional' exists anywhere. The licensing A-Z lists 14 licence types with no discretionary property licensing. DOCUMENT LIBRARY: lists only HMO application, HMO Standards, self declaration, revocation, TEN and variation forms. No designation notice. MAJOR TRAP FLAGGED: the HMO enforcement options page contains the phrase 'offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Act (selective licensing)'. This is NOT evidence of a Kingston scheme. It is verbatim boilerplate from the statutory civil penalties guidance listing offence types, which every council reproduces whether or not it has designated anything. This is the single most likely source of an automated false positive for this borough. METHOD CAVEAT: Kingston's site search is broken for this purpose, returning an identical 3,261-result set for every query, so it was discarded entirely and the finding rests on full sitemap enumeration, the licensing A-Z, the fee schedule and the document library. The housing standards team: ... implement mandatory licencing of houses in multiple occupation'. The council describes its own licensing function as mandatory HMO licensing and nothing else; its enforcement list otherwise cites only Part 1 HHSRS powers. There is NO HMO licence fee, no selective licence fee and no additional licence fee anywhere in it. A live Part 3 or s.56 scheme must carry its own cost-recovery fee; Rutland carries none. The /licensing/ tree contains only alcohol-entertainment-gambling, animal, buying-selling-collecting, child employment and performance, petroleum and explosives, and taxi and private hire. A hypothetical tariff copied from MHCLG statutory guidance; Rutland has no selective licence to fail to obtain. Appendix 2 carries near-identical wording to Runnymede's, confirming a shared national template. (2) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, a live risk flagged and controlled: Rutland's housing standards service is DELIVERED BY Peterborough City Council, so any Peterborough scheme would be easy to misattribute. Rutland's verdict was sourced only from rutland.gov.uk pages and Rutland's own Cabinet papers. (3) ModernGov 'additional licensing' hits are all Planning Committee development-control reports. S12000026.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). Scottish Borders therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.

E07000111.research: SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,922 URLs, grepped for selective / licen / hmo / landlord / multiple occup / private sector hous. ZERO selective- or additional-licensing pages. The only housing-licensing URLs are the single HMO page, an HMO amenity standards PDF, and the private sector housing enforcement policy. The HMO licence fees are: A new application for up to five units is £1,031.17 and £24.40 for each additional unit. To increase the number of HMO occupiers is £102.50.' The page routes licensability to national criteria only. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, all excluded below. No designation report, no consultation report and no designation notice, ever. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) '£24.40 for each additional unit', a per-unit surcharge on a mandatory licence. (2) 2006 OPTIONS PAPER: Cabinet 13/04/2006 'HMO Licensing Charges' states 'HMO licensing consists of two parts: mandatory HMO licensing and discretionary HMO additional licensing'. A pure explainer of the statutory framework. (3) APPROVED-BUT-NEVER-DESIGNATED / ASPIRATION: the 2007-2011 Private Sector Housing Strategy says work 'can be expected to increase if, following the consultation period, the Council adopts additional licensing' and action 1.2 'Consider the implementation of a Landlords Accreditation Scheme and additional licensing'. Conditional aspiration only. The same document expressly rules Part 3 out: 'selective licensing of other residential accommodation (primarily focussed upon areas of low housing demand - and unlikely to be suitable for Sevenoaks District Council)'. Even had it been adopted, a 2007-era designation would have expired by 2012 under the five-year maximum. (4) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, THANET: the 17 June 2014 Housing and Community Safety Advisory Committee pack states 'A selective licensing scheme has been put in place for the two most deprived areas in Kent, Cliftonville West and Margate Central in Thanet'. That is THANET DISTRICT COUNCIL's scheme sitting on Sevenoaks' domain, and a domain-scoped scrape would misattribute it. (5) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: 'Landlords Accreditation Scheme'. (6) STATUTORY-SCOPE BOILERPLATE: a 2018 BRE stock modelling report recites the Act's scope. (7) UNRELATED SENSE: a 2018 Housing Strategy Progress Report mentions 'option to support selective use for high demand areas', concerning housing ALLOCATIONS. E08000019.research: The research brief asserted that Sheffield almost certainly HAS live selective licensing and told the researcher not to report it negative without extraordinary evidence. The evidence is extraordinary, primary, current and unambiguous, and it points the other way. THE PRIOR WAS WRONG. This was independently re-verified by the coordinator via direct fetch with a browser user-agent. Sheffield's landing page carries the summary line 'Details about the now closed Selective Licensing scheme.' SCHEME 1, PAGE HALL: 'A Selective Licence scheme ran in Page Hall from 22 April 2014 to 21 April 2019. This scheme has now ended.' followed by 'Landlords of these properties will no longer be required to apply for a selective licence to rent them out.' The designation was defined by STREETS AND HOUSE-NUMBER RANGES, not wards: Page Hall Road (53 to 135 and 52 to 118), Hinde House Lane (31 to 125 and 34 to 102), and all properties on Hinde Street, Popple Street, Robey Street, Lloyd Street, Wade Street, Lauder Street and Willoughby Street. SCHEME 2: 'A selective licensing scheme operated in areas of London Road, Abbeydale Road and Chesterfield Road, as well as some adjoining streets, between 1 November 2018 and 31 October 2023. If you previously had a Selective Licence for your property in this scheme, there is no need for you to renew as the scheme has ended.' Under 'The following addresses no longer need a licence' it lists London Road 101-661 and 42-524, Abbeydale Road 1-781 and 2-666, Chesterfield Road 13-123 and 30, plus around 35 adjoining streets with specific house numbers. 'On 26 January 2024 a report highlighting the findings from the ... selective licensing scheme was presented to the Housing Policy Committee', a closure report confirming wind-down rather than renewal. WARD-MATCHING FLAG, IMPORTANT: BOTH designations are defined by street names and house-number ranges, NOT by wards. Coverage is recorded as 'streets' and wards is null; no ward list should ever be synthesised for Sheffield. Sheffield did undergo a ward boundary review (its current 28-ward structure took effect in 2016, between the two designations), but because neither designation is ward-based, that review cannot have broken ward matching here. FEE TEST, DECISIVE: the current Fee and Charging Structure Policy (February 2024) was downloaded and text-extracted. Section 2.1: 'This policy details Sheffield City Council's licence fees and charges made during the determination process under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004 and applies to all HMOs requiring a licence in relation to Mandatory Licensing.' The fee table is headed 'Schedule of Fees, Charges and Discounts for HMO Mandatory Licensing', new application up to 5 bedrooms Part 1 £725 plus Part 2 £460 equals £1,185, rising to £3,890 for 50+ bedrooms; renewals £1,135 to £3,840. There is NO selective and NO additional licensing fee anywhere in the document. CURRENT SCOPE: the HMO apply page states 'You need a Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) licence if you own a property that is occupied by 5 or more people forming 2 or more households, regardless of the number of floors'. SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,671 URLs across both sub-sitemaps; exactly three contain 'selective' and all three are the closed-scheme pages. There is no live selective licence application route. COMMITTEE SWEEP: Sheffield's Housing Policy Committee agenda and document listings were enumerated for all 14 meetings from 31 October 2024 through 22 October 2026. ZERO occurrences of 'selective' in any of them. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) THE ADDITIONAL-LICENSING RECITAL: section 1.1 of the fee policy says Sheffield has 'a statutory duty ... to administer and enforce a licensing scheme for mandatorily licensable Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO's) and discretionary powers to implement Additional Licensing Schemes for other HMOs'. This recites the STATUTORY POWER, not its exercise. No designation, area, date or fee accompanies it, and section 2.1 immediately confines the policy to mandatory licensing. (2) s.254 DEFINITION: the HMO information page says HMOs are 'a house or a flat in which 3 or more households live as their only or main residence'; the same page then states 'Some HMOs, occupied by 5 or more will require licensing'. (3) 'Additional fit and proper declaration form' and 'Additional compliance monitoring fee £500', where 'additional' qualifies a form and a monitoring surcharge. (4) EXPIRED SCHEMES PRESENTED AS LIVE: the page for the second scheme is still TITLED 'Apply for a Selective Licence in London, Abbeydale or Chesterfield Road', which reads as live and is precisely the trap the brief warned about; its body text confirms the scheme ended on 31 October 2023. LIMITATION: Sheffield's on-site search FAILED its control test and was not relied on: /search?search= returned the identical 'We've found 841 results' for the control 'houses in multiple occupation' and for 'selective licensing', so it does not discriminate. WebFetch received HTTP 403 from sheffield.gov.uk; that was a bot block, not evidence, and every page was retrieved successfully on retry with a browser user-agent.

S12000027.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). Shetland Islands therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.

E06000051.research: THE DECISIVE SOURCE: Shropshire's Cabinet adopted a new Civil Penalty Policy on 10 June 2026. Its title block reads verbatim: 'Civil Penalties under the Renters Rights Act 2025 and other housing legislation Policy. Policy for adoption by local authorities in England (no selective licensing areas).' Shropshire selected the model-policy variant explicitly drafted for authorities that have NO SELECTIVE LICENSING AREAS. A council-adopted, two-month-old, self-declared negative, and the strongest possible form of evidence for a nil finding. The Cabinet printed decisions confirm adoption rather than proposal: 'RESOLVED: ... To approve the Shropshire Housing Authority Enforcement Policy and Civil Penalty Policy, to take effect immediately, with transitional arrangements allowing the existing policies to operate in tandem for a six-month period to conclude legacy cases.' SITEMAP SWEEP: Shropshire has no XML sitemap (/sitemap.xml 404s), so the HTML sitemap was used: 2,218 URLs collected and grepped. The only housing-licensing hits are the HMO page, landlord responsibilities and the enforcement policy. Notably the licensing-fees tree has ten sub-pages (animal, firework, gambling, taxi, Licensing Act, miscellaneous, public health, caravan-site fit-and-proper) and NOT ONE housing-licensing fee page. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'The licence fee is as follows from 1 April 2026: Payment one: ... £1055.00 up to and including five bedrooms, and a further £176 per each additional bedroom thereafter. Payment two: must be paid within 28 days of the date of your licence. £403.00'. Threshold is the national mandatory one: 'Nationally, HMOs occupied by five or more people, in two or more households, where there is sharing of facilities, eg kitchen or bathroom, must be licensed. This is a mandatory government requirement.' COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control PASSED. 'selective licensing' returns only the June 2026 policy plus AONB terms-of-reference and planning items using 'selective' in other senses; 'additional licensing' returns only hackney carriage and private hire items. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE, the single most dangerous trap in this batch, because it sits INSIDE the very document that proves the negative. The adopted Enforcement Policy lists 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]', and the Civil Penalty Policy lists 'Failure to obtain a selective licence under section 95 of the Housing Act 2004' and 'Failure to comply with selective licence conditions under section 95' (verified at lines 94 and 105 of the extracted text). Read in isolation these look like proof of a scheme; the same document's title block at line 7 says the opposite. (2) 'The Housing and Planning Act 2016 extends mandatory HMO licensing to include additional HMOs of all storeys', where 'additional' qualifies HMOs, describing the October 2018 nationwide removal of the storey test. (3) '£176 per each additional bedroom', a mandatory-licence surcharge. (4) s.254 DEFINITION: 'An HMO is a house or flat that is occupied as a main residence, by more than one household'; the same page sets licensing at five or more. (5) UNRELATED SENSES: Shropshire Hills AONB Partnership terms of reference and a Former Shelton Hospital planning application; a 2019 'Proposed Additional Consultation Relating to the Hackney Carriage and Private Hire Licensing Policy' is taxi licensing. LIMITATION: Shropshire has no XML sitemap AND its on-site search FAILED its control test, being JavaScript-driven and returning byte-identical 299,633-character shells for both 'houses in multiple occupation' and 'selective licensing'. It was not relied on. The negative rests on the 2,218-URL HTML sitemap sweep, the service pages, the fee schedule and a control-passing ModernGov search.

E08000029.research: SITEMAP SWEEP: 1,450 URLs, independently reproduced with an identical count, ZERO containing 'selective'. The only housing-licensing URLs are /housing/homes-multiple-occupation, /housing/renting-private-landlord and /housing/solihull-landlord-forum. SITE SEARCH CONTROL: PASSED, control 'council tax' returned 'Showing items 1 to 10 of 72 results', control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 6 results, and 'selective licensing' returned 3 results, all irrelevant fuzzy word-matches (lists and registers, health information, Balsall Common history). FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'Homes in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) are buildings that contain five or more people, two or more of which are of different households, regardless of the storey level'; 'you will be required to pay the £1,075 non-refundable fee. There are discounts for National Residential Landlords Association (NRLA) members: NRLA discount: £108'; 'Further fees may be included depending on different aspects of your HMO: an additional let or person over 7: £43.00; application for a subsequent licence resulting from the change of the licence holder: £215; inadequate application resulting in the Council reviewing information: £145'. No selective or additional licence fee anywhere. The statutory registers page lists only hackney carriage and private hire driver registers under 'Licensing'. COMMITTEE PAPERS: ModernGov control PASSED. 'selective licensing' returns EXACTLY ONE result in the entire committee archive: Economic Development, Managed Growth and Skills Scrutiny Board, 17 November 2022, 'Draft Housing Strategy'. THE 2022 ITEM IS NOT A DESIGNATION, analysed in full. Appendix 2, page 17, verbatim: 'Selective Licensing policy - Local councils can introduce selective licensing schemes where this is supported by evidence and consultation occurs. A policy would mean that all landlords in a designated area would require a licence.' Entirely conditional and generic, naming NO area, ward, street, start date, end date or fee. Appendix 3 lists '6. Private Rented Sector - Selective Licencing' as a future 'Key Thing to Do' with a four-stage pipeline: '1. Develop evidence base and proposals 2. Agree recommendations 3. Cabinet approval and Consultation 4. Notice and Implementation'. Stages 3 and 4 would each generate a Cabinet report, a statutory consultation and a designation notice, all of which would appear in ModernGov; the archive contains NONE of them. The pipeline never advanced past stage 1. Recorded as no scheme rather than 'proposed', since the only artefact is a four-year-old conditional strategy line with no live proposal behind it. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, BIRMINGHAM, checked explicitly and cleared. Birmingham operates a large selective licensing scheme and Solihull borders it. Every occurrence of 'Birmingham' in the Draft Housing Strategy was inspected: all 14 relate to the Greater Birmingham and Solihull LEP, the Birmingham and Black Country Housing Market Area, the Birmingham and Solihull Integrated Care System, Birmingham Airport and University Hospitals Birmingham NHS FT. (2) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, present here and ADJACENT TO the licensing item, making it especially dangerous. The same Implementation Plan, item 7 (HMOs), reads 'Review the case for working to introduce Article 4 Direction (area based or borough wide)'. The phrase 'area based or borough wide' reads exactly like a designation, but this is planning control over C3-to-C4 permitted development. (3) 'an additional let or person over 7: £43.00', a mandatory-licence surcharge. (4) ModernGov 'additional licensing' hits are all taxi, gambling and premises licensing. (5) VOLUNTARY ENGAGEMENT: the landlord forum and 2025 landlord forum news items are advice and engagement events. LIMITATION: none material.

E06000066.research: SITEMAP SWEEP: wp-sitemap.xml index resolving to 34 sub-sitemaps, all fetched, 5,803 URLs collected, independently reproduced with an identical count. ZERO URLs containing 'selective'. The only HMO URLs are /housing-support/hmo-licensing/, /housing-support/hmo-standards-and-regulations/ and the licensing privacy notice. THRESHOLD: the HMO licensing page, last updated 17 July 2026 and therefore current, states 'The Housing Act 2004 made it mandatory for housing in multiple occupation (HMOs) be licenced' and 'An HMO licence is required if: the property is occupied by 5 or more people, from more than one household; and they share basic amenities'. No second licensable category is described. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim: 'New HMO Licence (5 bed max) ... Part 1 £738 / Part 2 £211 / Total £949 / Additional person over five £43' and 'Renewal HMO Licence (5 bed max) ... Part 1 £625 / Part 2 £211 / Total £836 / Additional person over five £33'. PRIVACY NOTICE CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing team's licensing privacy notice is titled 'Licensing of HMOs and Caravan/Camping', so no Part 3 regime is processed. The public register is county-wide ('the full register which includes the whole of Somerset'), confirming a single unified post-2023 regime. INHERITED DISTRICT DESIGNATIONS, CHECKED AND CLEARED, the key risk for this council. Somerset is a unitary formed on 1 April 2023 from Somerset County Council plus Mendip, Sedgemoor, South Somerset and Somerset West and Taunton. A pre-April-2023 district designation could in principle still run to around 2028 under the five-year maximum. All four predecessor domains now redirect to somerset.gov.uk/we-have-moved/, so the unified site is the authoritative record. Each predecessor domain was additionally swept via the Wayback CDX archive API: ZERO archived URLs matching 'selective' on all four. No such designation ever existed. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, SOUTH SOMERSET / YEOVIL, the biggest trap here. The archived South Somerset site holds hmodirection.pdf, hmo_all_zones.pdf and five zone maps filed under /planning-and-building-control/. The parent page reads 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO's) - Yeovil ... Confirmation of an Article 4 Direction ... South Somerset District Council has confirmed an Article 4 Direction which now requires a planning application to be submitted ... Direction only relates to certain areas of Yeovil ... The Direction came into force on 19th November'. Zone and ward names plus a commencement date make this read exactly like a designation, but it is planning control over C3-to-C4 conversion. (2) 'Additional person over five' fee lines (£43 and £33), per-occupant surcharges on a mandatory licence. LIMITATION: Somerset's on-site search FAILED its control test, rendering results client-side via JavaScript and returning zero result rows even for control queries, so it was not relied on. Somerset's ModernGov also failed its control test: ieSearchResults.aspx returns page chrome only via both GET and POST, so committee papers could not be keyword-searched. A designation existing ONLY in an un-indexed committee report, and not yet reflected in the web estate, the fee schedule or the public register, would not have been detected; since a live designation must by law carry a cost-recovery fee and a public register, this residual risk is low.

E07000012.research: The best-evidenced negative in the batch, because the council has answered the question directly in writing. FOI DISCLOSURE, DIRECT PRIMARY ADMISSION: the council publishes its own FOI responses. 'Request 8596 Selective Licensing Scheme Property Licenses' asks 'regarding your Selective Licensing Scheme (if you have one in place)' and South Cambridgeshire's own responses are: '1. What was the estimated number of properties that were thought to require a Selective License from the outset? - None'; '2. How many licenses have been granted? - None'; '3. How many properties are the Council aware of, that are unlicensed and require a license - None'. 'Request 8597 Civil Penalties for Selective Licensing Scheme' similarly answers 'How many Civil Penalty Notices were issued relating to privately rented properties in years 2018 and 2019? - None' and '- Not applicable'. SITEMAP SWEEP: 757 URLs, independently reproduced, ZERO containing 'selective'. FEE TEST: mandatory only, quoted verbatim from the current schedule, verified by direct fetch: 'HMO Licence Fees 2026/2027 - The application fee for a 5-year licence for 2026/2027 is £895 for up to 5 bedrooms, any additional bedrooms are priced at £36 per room. Renewal of the licence is £544 for up to 5 bedrooms, any additional bedrooms are priced at £24 per room.' SECTION INDEX: /housing/renting-privately/ lists nine pages (HMO, poor condition, mobile homes, moving in, landlord legislation, private sector housing guide, Renters' Rights Act, and two council lettings brands). No selective licensing page. The HMO guidance and regulations pages were fetched and grepped: no mention of selective or additional licensing; the only application routes offered are 'Apply for a House in Multiple Occupation Licence' and 'Apply to renew a House in Multiple Occupation Licence'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) STATUTORY-POWERS BOILERPLATE, which would have caught a careless sweep, because two LIVE pages contain the words 'additional licensing' and 'selectively licence' in close proximity: 'The legislation introduced a new definition of a House in Multiple Occupation and requires mandatory licensing of HMO's with 3 Storeys or more and with 5 or more occupants. This legislation also includes powers to introduce additional licensing ... and also to selectively licence properties', under a heading literally reading 'Housing Act 2004 Part 2 and 3 - Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation'. A Part 2-and-3 heading on a live council page is exactly the shape of a true positive. But these describe the POWER in the Act, not its exercise: no designation, area, ward, date or fee accompanies them, and the council's own FOI answer confirms zero licences. (2) s.254 DEFINITION: the guidance page defines an HMO as '3 or more tenants are occupying the property who form 2 or more households'. (3) 'any additional bedrooms are priced at £36 per room', a surcharge on a mandatory licence. (4) The three PDFs matching 'selective licensing' are FOI REQUESTS, and their content is a negative rather than a positive. LIMITATION: the on-site search FAILED its control test (client-side JS rendering, zero result rows even for control queries) and was not relied on. ModernGov also failed its control test, returning chrome only, so committee papers could not be keyword-searched, and democracy.scambs.gov.uk did not resolve. The FOI responses date from around 2020; their currency is carried forward by the 2026/2027 fee schedule and the current sitemap sweep, both consistent with no scheme.

E07000039.research: THRESHOLD: the live HMO pages (a three-chapter article reached by crawling the live private-landlords page) state 'from 1 October 2018 HMOs with five or more occupiers forming two or more households regardless of the number of storeys will be subject to HMO licensing' and list only the three mandatory categories. No selective or additional licensing is mentioned anywhere in the three chapters. FEE TEST, which CORRECTS an initial finding that South Derbyshire publishes no HMO fee at all. The housing fees and charges page DOES carry a housing-licensing section headed 'Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation', covering 'Application for new licence', 'Amendment of licence' and 'Transfer of licence', charged hourly at 'Manager £65 / hour, EHO £54 / hour, Assistant £42 / hour'. So the mandatory regime is fee-bearing, which makes the fee test properly discriminating here: there is a mandatory HMO licensing fee line and NO selective and NO s.56 additional licensing fee line. The separate Licensing fees and charges page was read in full and covers only private hire, food export certificates, animal licences, gambling and scrap metal dealers. SITEMAP SWEEP: 748 URLs, independently reproduced, ZERO containing 'selective'. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THAT SWEEP: the sitemap is STALE, every loc using the retired south-derbys.gov.uk domain and omitting the live HMO page entirely, so it was NOT treated as sufficient on its own and was supplemented with a live crawl and an archive sweep. ARCHIVE SWEEP: Wayback CDX queried for BOTH southderbyshire.gov.uk and the legacy south-derbys.gov.uk domain across their full recorded history: ZERO archived URLs matching 'selective'. CONSULTATIONS: the licensing policy-consultations page carries only a 'Draft Animal Welfare Licensing Policy 2026-2031'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) NEIGHBOUR BLEED, DERBY CITY, actively checked and clean. Derby City Council has operated selective licensing and South Derbyshire wraps around it, so a Derby scheme description on a South Derbyshire page would be easy to misattribute. All three South Derbyshire private-rented-sector pages were grepped for 'derby city' and 'selective': ZERO hits. (2) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: the landlord support page describes accreditation requiring landlords to 'abide by the EMLAS Code of Management, prove they are fit and proper ... and have at least applied for any licences that they should hold by law'. The East Midlands Landlord Accreditation Scheme is voluntary, and the phrase 'any licences that they should hold by law' does not create a designation. (3) s.254 DEFINITION: chapter 1 opens 'A house or a flat in which three or more people forming two or more households share some basic facilities'; chapter 2 then correctly sets the licensing trigger at five. (4) 'additional benefits in tenant support services' on the landlord page, an unrelated sense. LIMITATION: this is the weakest-sourced negative of the twelve, though still adequately sourced. The on-site search FAILED its control test (returning HTTP 411 or client-side-only results, with zero result rows for control queries) and was not relied on. The CMIS committee system is ASP.NET postback-driven and could not be keyword-searched, and southderbyshire.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 522; committee papers were therefore not reachable. The sitemap is stale as noted. The finding rests on the live HMO pages, the hourly-rate housing fee schedule, the dual-domain archive sweep and the consultations page.

E06000025.research: EXPLICIT DISPROOF on the council's own service page: 'We only operate the national mandatory HMO licensing scheme. You must have a licence if you are renting out a large HMO in England or Wales. Your property is defined as a large HMO if all the following apply: it is rented to 5 or more people from more than one household; some or all the tenants share bathroom or kitchen facilities...'. FEE TEST: mandatory bands only, '£936 from 1 April 2026' with 'an additional £46 is made for each additional unit of accommodation', which is the per-unit surcharge on a MANDATORY licence and is the documented false positive, not s.56. SEARCH CONTROL FAILED AND WAS DISCARDED: /?s=selective+licensing and the control /?s=houses+in+multiple+occupation returned byte-identical 70,809-byte responses (a JS SPA shell serving the beta homepage), exactly the Sheffield failure mode, so the nil site-search result proves nothing and was not relied on. SITEMAP SWEEP instead: /sitemap.xml 404s; /wp-sitemap.xml resolves to a 7-part index, 1,912 URLs, zero 'selective'. That sitemap only covers the legacy A-Z, so the live service site beta.southglos.gov.uk was reached via /atoz/private-sector-housing/ and its own sitemap swept at /sitemap/sitemap-index.xml, 921 URLs, zero 'selective'. No boundary review issue, since there is no designation and no wards.

That is the mandatory threshold only; no lower trigger and no designated area anywhere. FEE TEST: the HMO licensing page carries only £446.40 and £144.00, mandatory bands with no separate cost-recovery fee for any area-based scheme, which a live self-financing selective scheme would require. S12000029.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). South Lanarkshire therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.
