E06000021.research: TWO FINDINGS, BOTH FROM PRIMARY COUNCIL SOURCES, BOTH INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR VIA DIRECT FETCH. (1) EXPIRED SELECTIVE LICENSING. The live page /selectivelicensing (breadcrumb: Home > Housing and neighbourhoods > Private renting and landlords > Selective Licensing Evaluation Report) states VERBATIM: 'In 2014 the following areas in Fenton and Cobridge were designated as Selective Licensing areas', lists the streets reproduced in areaDescription, then states unambiguously: 'These selective licensing schemes ended on the 4th August 2019.' THIS IS THE SHEFFIELD PATTERN: a URL that still reads /selectivelicensing describing a scheme that lapsed seven years ago. Read the body, not the title. START DATE: the council gives only the YEAR, 'In 2014'. A five-year designation ending 4 August 2019 implies commencement on or about 5 August 2014, but the council does not publish that date, so start is null rather than synthesised. COVERAGE is 'streets' and wards is null because the designation is defined by a STREET LIST. Wards were NOT inferred from the street list. Note Stoke-on-Trent had a ward boundary review effective from the 2015 elections, AFTER this 2014 designation, which is a further reason not to back-derive ward names. Supporting document: 'selective_licensing_evaluation_report_2020', published AFTER the scheme closed, consistent with expiry rather than continuation. (2) PROPOSED CITY-WIDE ADDITIONAL LICENSING, PUBLISHED 4 AUGUST 2026, ONE DAY BEFORE VERIFICATION. Council news article 2118, 'Measures to limit citywide numbers of houses of multiple occupation and ensure they meet high standards', Published: Tuesday, 4th August 2026, states VERBATIM: 'At the same time, the council is proposing, subject to the outcome of statutory consultation, an Additional Licensing Scheme for HMOs across the city.' and 'This would bring smaller HMOs into a formal regulatory framework and allow the council to set and enforce standards. Existing licence conditions would be strengthened.' It confirms it is NOT yet designated: 'The proposals - which will be considered by the ruling cabinet next week - are part of drive to limit the growth of HMOs.' Status is therefore 'proposed', with start, end and fee null. Landlords do NOT need an additional licence today, but this is live and moving and MUST be re-checked after the cabinet decision and any statutory consultation. CRITICAL SEPARATION, THE ARTICLE 4 TRAP, PRESENT IN THE SAME ARTICLE: the package also includes 'a city-wide Article 4 Direction, which would remove development rights that currently allow family homes to be converted into HMOs without the need for a planning application.' That is PLANNING control over C3-to-C4 change of use, NOT licensing, and creates no licence requirement and no rent repayment order exposure. The article also describes proposed PLANNING density caps ('HMOs make up more than 5% of all residential properties within a 50-metre radius', 'a cap on the total number of HMOs within each ward ... 4% ... 2.5% ... 1.5%') which are Local Plan policy, not a designation; none of it was recorded as a scheme and no wards were derived from it. METHOD: SITEMAP SWEEP PASSED ITS CONTROL. /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200, 544,051 bytes, 5,090 URLs. The control grep for 'multiple_occupation' returned a genuine hit, so a nil result would have been meaningful. The grep for 'selective' returned exactly four URLs, all relating to the closed Fenton/Cobridge scheme and its evaluation report. There is no live selective licensing application route. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: all five pages of 'Environmental health and trading standards - fees and charges' were retrieved. No selective and no additional licensing fee appears. The only 'Additional licensable activity £207.50' line sits in an ANIMAL-LICENSING block alongside 'Host families' and 'Re-inspection', and is not s.56. The current private renting section lists only damp mould and condensation, landlord benefits account, problems with a privately-rented home, local housing allowance, universal credit, HMOs, tell us about a change in tenant, MEES and supported housing. NEIGHBOUR BLEED guarded against: no Newcastle-under-Lyme material was used.

E07000221.research: PRIMARY SOURCES, stratford.gov.uk only. (1) 'Advice on Houses in Multiple Occupation' splits HMOs into exactly two categories and is decisive: 'HMOs come in two categories: Unlicensed HMOs - three or more people in two or more households / Licensed HMOs - five or more people, in two or more households.' A council operating s.56 additional licensing could not describe 3-4 person HMOs as 'Unlicensed HMOs'. (2) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, 'Fees and Charges 2026-27', the current published schedule linked from the HMO application page. The ONLY housing licence application fee lines are 'House in multiple occupation (HMO) Inspection Fees - NEW Applications / Number of occupants:- / 5 to 10 / 11 to 15 / 16 to 20 / 21 +' and the parallel renewals table, with the note '*It is now a requirement for authorities to charge in two parts for HMO fees. Part A is non-refundable, Part B is payable once the licence has been approved. The charge is 75% for Part A, followed by 25% for Part B.' Every band STARTS AT 5 OCCUPANTS. There is no 3-4 occupant band and no separate selective or property licence fee anywhere in the 2,027-line schedule. (3) 'Practical Guide to Licensing of HMOs', section 3: 'HMOs containing 5 or more occupants, in 2 or more households, except those converted to entirely self-contained flats, regardless of the number of storey's, MUST have a licence to operate. This is known as Mandatory HMO Licensing.' It adds 'there will be more HMOs which do not require licensing than those that do'. (4) SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml (generated 2026-07-31) lists 919 URLs including all 77 homes-properties and 43 licences-permissions pages; ZERO contain 'selective' or 'additional'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (a) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the Fees and Charges schedule contains 'Offences in relation to licensing of HMOs under Part 3 of the Housing Act 2004 (Section 95, Housing Act 2004) / Failure to obtain a licence (section 95(1))' and the parallel Part 2 s.72 line. This is the s.249A civil penalty matrix present in nearly every enforcement policy. (b) '21 + Fee for 16 to 20 occupants PLUS additional fee per group of up to 10' is a per-occupant surcharge on a MANDATORY licence. (c) s.254 definition: 'properties occupied by three or more people, in two or more households'. (d) STATUTORY-POWER STUB: the 2018 Practical Guide CONTENTS lists a sub-heading 'What is Additional Licensing' under section 3, but the word 'additional' occurs only 3 times in the entire 12-page document, and the section 3 body describes ONLY Mandatory HMO Licensing with no designation, area, dates or fee. A description of the power, not its exercise. (e) Article 4 Directions treated as planning. LIMITATIONS: Stratford's main site search PASSED its control ('houses in multiple occupation' returned 'About 48 results' and surfaced the correct pages); the real query 'selective licensing' returned 'About 54 results' but every one was an OR-match on 'licensing' alone (taxi, gambling, scrap dealers, alcohol, sex establishments, street trading, pavement) with no selective-licensing content, so this is a trustworthy nil. Stratford's ModernGov document search FAILED its control: results load via AJAX and the control and real queries returned byte-identical 29,395-byte shells, so committee-paper search was unusable and its nil result proves nothing; the sitemap sweep and current fee schedule are relied on instead.

E07000082.research: PRIMARY SOURCES, stroud.gov.uk only. (1) DECISIVE: the current 'Private Sector Housing Renewal Policy 2025-30', 3,748 lines of extracted text. Its seven key objectives are listed and objective 4 is 'Mandatory Licensing of Houses In Multiple Occupation (HMOs)'. The body states: 'Objective 4: Mandatory licensing of Houses In Multiple Occupation (HMO). Powers under the Housing Act 2004 require Mandatory Licensing of HMOs that comprise of 5 or more people in two or more separate households. The appropriate licensing fee which at time of adoption has been set at £1,398 for a 5 year licence.' Enforcement paragraph: 'Currently, there are 27 licensed HMOs in Stroud.' The words 'selective' and 'additional licensing' appear ZERO times in the entire policy. A council operating or planning either scheme would have to set it out in its private sector housing renewal policy. (2) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'The mandatory HMO licensing fee is £1398 for a 5 year licence per property', split into a non-refundable £403 first part and £995 balance on approval. A raw HTML grep for '£' returns ONLY £1398, £403 and £995. A single fee, expressly labelled mandatory, with no second application route. A raw-HTML grep of this page for 'selective', 'additional licen' and 'designat' returns zero hits, so nothing is hidden in a collapsed accordion. (3) The council's only housing licence register is the 'HMO Licensing Register', published as 'Stroud District Council Public Register of Licensed HMOs, Updated: June 2025'. The full registers index lists an HMO register, Licensing Act 2003 registers, pavement and street-trading registers, contracts, FOI, AI, community asset and council property registers, but NO Part 3 or selective register. Housing Act 2004 s.232 requires a register for each licensing type operated, so its absence is corroborating negative evidence. (4) SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returns an HTTP 500 error page and /sitemap, /sitemap-index.xml and /sitemap.aspx all 404, so the HTML site map at /site-map was used instead. It enumerates 1,432 URLs; ZERO contain 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the Private Sector Housing Renewal Policy consultation page was checked in case it PROPOSED a scheme; it does not, and there is no options pipeline toward one. Article 4 Directions were not treated as licensing. No Gloucester City or Cheltenham scheme was imported. LIMITATIONS: STROUD'S SITE SEARCH FAILED ITS CONTROL QUERY AND IS BROKEN: the visible search page is client-side rendered and returned an identical 19,032-byte shell with no result text for both queries, and its underlying API returned exactly {"suggestions":[],"recommendations":[],"showMoreCount":0} for the CONTROL phrase 'houses in multiple occupation' as well as for 'selective licensing'. Because the control returned nothing, a nil search result from Stroud proves nothing and was not relied on. Stroud's ModernGov also loads results via AJAX and returned equal-length shells, so committee-paper search was likewise unusable. The 1,432-URL site-map sweep, the current 2025-30 policy PDF, the single mandatory fee and the registers index are relied on instead, and they agree.

E08000024.research: EXPLICIT SELF-DECLARED NEGATIVE, RECOVERED FROM EMBEDDED PAGE JSON. Sunderland's HMO service page is a GOSS form-driven page whose accordion content is NOT present in the rendered DOM as plain text: it is base64-encoded inside a JavaScript variable 'HMOLICENCEPAGEFormData'. This is exactly the Stevenage collapsed-accordion trap. The 17,785-byte base64 blob was extracted from the raw HTML and decoded. It contains two named content fields, 'SELECTIVELICENSING' and 'ADDITIONALSELECTIVELICENSING', BOTH of which read VERBATIM AND IDENTICALLY: 'Sunderland City Council does not currently operate any Additional or Selective Licensing schemes for rental properties.' An unambiguous, current, on-domain statement covering BOTH s.56 and s.80. CORROBORATION IN THE SAME DECODED CONTENT: 'Smaller HMOs (those occupied by 3 or 4 persons in 2 or more households) are still deemed as HMOs but do not require a licence in Sunderland', emphasised in bold in the source. A council operating additional licensing could not say that. The rendered page also states the mandatory threshold: 'You must have a licence for a HMO if five or more people are living in two or more households'. SITEMAP SWEEP PASSED ITS CONTROL: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200, 877,737 bytes, 5,846 URLs, and is FRESH (homepage lastmod 2026-08-03). CONTROL: the grep for 'Multiple-Occupation' returned genuine hits, so a nil result is meaningful. The grep for 'selective' across all 5,846 URLs returned ZERO matches. The only housing licensing URLs are mandatory ones, and the title of article 15811 is itself explicit: 'Mandatory licensing for HMOs'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, genuinely present here and load-bearing. The decoded content states: 'in its capacity as local planning authority Sunderland City Council has imposed what is known as an Article 4 Direction which took effect in December 2013. This remains affecting the former city council wards of Barnes, Hendon, Millfield, St. Michael's and St. Peter's'. This is PLANNING control removing permitted development rights for C3-to-C4 conversion up to six persons. It is NOT licensing. Hendon and Millfield are precisely the areas most often wrongly reported as selective licensing areas in Sunderland. NO wards were recorded, because there is no designation. NOTE ALSO that the council itself calls these the 'FORMER city council wards', confirming a ward boundary review has occurred since 2013, a further reason those names must not be propagated into a licensing dataset. (2) The s.254 DEFINITION trap, resolved by the council's own statement that 3-4 person HMOs do not require a licence. (3) PLANNING THRESHOLD trap: 'Under permitted development rights it is lawful for any residential property in Sunderland area to be an HMO as long as there are six or fewer occupants. If there are seven or more occupants, the property requires a change of use planning permission'. Planning permission is not a licence, and the decoded text expressly warns 'your HMO licence application if successful does not grant or give the required consent that may be required ... in terms of planning permission'. (4) 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' is a statutory instrument title about s.257 HMO management, NOT s.56. (5) NEIGHBOUR BLEED guarded against: no Newcastle upon Tyne or County Durham material was used. LIMITATION: sunderland.gov.uk sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial returning HTTP 403 to a plain request. THIS IS A BOT BLOCK, NOT EVIDENCE, and was defeated with a browser user-agent plus Accept, Accept-Language, Referer and --compressed, after which the page returned HTTP 200. No expired scheme was found; the council's own wording is 'does not currently operate any', with no reference to a former scheme.

E07000214.research: PRIMARY SOURCE: the council's only HMO and landlord licensing page. VERBATIM: 'A house in multiple occupation (HMO) is a property rented to three or more people who form two or more households who share some basic facilities such as kitchen, bathroom and living room.' Then, separately and decisively: 'All properties let to five or more people, who form two or more households should have a HMO Licence.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, strongest evidence: the 'Cost' section reads in full 'If you require a HMO licence, you will be charged a fee. This must be renewed every five years.' / '£896.20' / '£773.70 if you are a member of any nationally recognised landlord accreditation scheme or association.' A SINGLE mandatory band with an accreditation discount. There is no selective fee, no additional fee and no second application route anywhere on the site. CORROBORATING PDF: the linked 'HMO Information Sheet.pdf' (26,594 characters extracted) contains ZERO occurrences of 'selectiv' and ZERO of 'additional licen'. It refers throughout only to mandatory licensing, e.g. 'To operate a mandatory licensable HMO without one is a strict liability criminal offence' and 'If there are five or more occupants in the house including the live-in landlord and their family, then it is a mandatory licensable HMO'. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml (Drupal simple_sitemap, lastmod 2026-07-27) yielded 1,202 URLs. Grepping for 'selectiv' returned ZERO matches. Grepping for 'hmo|multiple-occ' returned exactly one housing URL (the other hits were 'Watchmoor Reserve' park pages, matching on the letters 'hmo' inside 'Watchmoor', the same substring gotcha recorded for Rushmoor). Grepping for 'licen' returned 100+ URLs, all animal activities, alcohol and premises, gambling, scrap metal, street trading, taxi, caravan sites, sex shops, tattooists and hypnotism. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The s.254 HMO DEFINITION trap: the page opens with the 'three or more people' definition followed by a caution that such a property 'must register it with the Council'; the LICENSING threshold is stated separately and explicitly as five or more. Three-person HMOs are NOT licensable. Reading the definition as an additional-licensing scheme would be the classic error. (2) 'Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' appears in the raw HTML as an outbound legislation.gov.uk link, a statutory instrument title, NOT s.56. It was the only 'Additional' string on the page outside cookie-banner text. (3) The £773.70 accreditation rate is a DISCOUNT on the single mandatory fee. LIMITATIONS: (a) The council's own site search FAILED its control query: the control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned no visible result rows (rendered client-side) and the real query returned an almost identical payload (43,221 vs 43,211 bytes). Not relied on; the 1,202-URL sitemap sweep is the substitute. (b) The COMMITTEE-MINUTES CHECK WAS INCONCLUSIVE: ModernGov's ieDocSearch.aspx returned a BYTE-IDENTICAL 45,264-byte response for the control and for both real queries, with zero document links in any response. The committee search is BROKEN and its nil result is not evidence. The negative rests on the service page, the fee schedule, the PDF and the sitemap, all consistent and primary. CONTEXT, not a scheme: a site-wide banner notes Surrey local government reorganisation from April 2027; Surrey Heath still exists and still administers HMO licensing today, and reorganisation neither creates nor removes a designation.

E07000113.research: PRIMARY SOURCES, swale.gov.uk only. THRESHOLD AND SCOPE, VERBATIM: a licence is needed where the property is 'occupied by five or more people, including children, who aren't related, married, in a civil partnership or living together as if they're married' and 'the occupants share things like a kitchen or bathroom between them'. Also 'You'll need a separate licence for each property' and 'A HMO licence lasts for five years.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, DECISIVE: the Fee section reads VERBATIM 'You'll need to pay £896 for a HMO licence or £761 if you're an accredited landlord.' The dedicated apply-and-pay page repeats it. A SINGLE band with an accreditation discount, with no selective fee, no additional fee and no second application route anywhere in the licensing section. CORROBORATION: the only guidance document Swale links from these pages is titled 'Guide to Houses in Multiple Occupancy and Mandatory Licensing'; the council's own document title says MANDATORY. The full HMO service tree is exactly five pages (introduction, apply-and-pay, renew, change, appeal) with no discretionary-scheme page. SITEMAP SWEEP PASSED ITS CONTROL: robots.txt declares the sitemap, which returned HTTP 200 at 273,753 bytes with 1,183 URLs. CONTROL: the grep for 'multiple-occupation' returned nine genuine hits, so a nil result is meaningful. The grep for 'selective' across all 1,183 URLs returned ZERO matches. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, genuinely present in the sitemap at /your-council/consultations/article-4-direction-affecting-houses-in-multiple-occupation-approval. PLANNING control over C3-to-C4 change of use, filed under consultations rather than licensing. It creates no licence requirement and is NOT a Part 2 or Part 3 designation. (2) TWO PLANNING SPDs also matched the HMO control grep and are likewise planning: 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Document' and 'Conversion of buildings and houses into flats and houses in multiple occupation supplementary planning guidance'. (3) 'Landlord forum' is a consultative meeting. (4) 'Calculate your licence fee' is the generic licensing fee tool covering alcohol, gambling and street trading. (5) The £761 accredited rate is a DISCOUNT on the single mandatory fee. (6) NEIGHBOUR BLEED guarded against: no Medway, Thanet or Canterbury material was used. LIMITATIONS: (a) THE www HOST IS A BOT BLOCK. https://www.swale.gov.uk/sitemap.xml returned HTTP 403. That is a block, not evidence: the bare host returned HTTP 200 and the full 1,183-URL sitemap. (b) No working control-tested committee-paper search was obtained, so an unpublicised historic committee discussion cannot be positively excluded; the current fee schedule, five-page service tree, 'Mandatory Licensing' guide title and zero-hit sitemap sweep are consistent and all primary. NOTE FOR FUTURE RE-CHECKS: the Isle of Sheppey and Sheerness are sometimes assumed to carry a selective licensing scheme; nothing on the council's own domain supports that, and the fee schedule positively contradicts it.

W06000011.research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, FRESHLY RE-DESIGNATED. The designation and the fee schedule were verified verbatim. The statutory public notice (last modified 16 February 2026) reads: 'Notice is hereby given that the City and County of Swansea has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of houses in multiple occupation in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas Electoral Wards. This scheme will be known as The City and County of Swansea's Additional HMO Licensing Scheme 2025. The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Section 56 - 60 of The Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The designation was made at a meeting of the Council of the City and County of Swansea on 2 October 2025... The Scheme will be effective from 14 February 2026 and, unless revoked beforehand, will cease to have effect on 14 February 2031... Failure to apply for a licence is an offence under Section 72(1) of The Housing Act 2004 for which a person may be fined up to £20,000. An application may also be made to the Residential Property Tribunal to make a Rent Repayment Order requiring the repayment of up to 12 months' rent collected during the time the property was unlicensed.' CORROBORATION: the HMO Licensing Policy 2025 para 6.8 states 'Council, by way of this policy, revokes the designation made in 2020 in respect of Castle, Uplands and St Thomas wards and the subsequent addendum to include Waterfront in 2022, that scheme will cease to have effect on 14 February 2026', and confirms the new scheme 'specifically applies to all HMOs which do not come within the remit of mandatory licensing within the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards including HMOs defined under Section 257, Housing Act 2004 i.e. poorly converted blocks of self-contained flats.' Para 1.3 records that additional licensing has run in Castle and Uplands 'since the introduction of the legislation in 2006', with St Thomas added in 2020 and Waterfront in 2021/2022. Para 1.5: 'Additional HMO licensing schemes have a maximum five years duration.' The live service page states 'Additional Licensing applies in the Castle, Uplands, Waterfront and St Thomas wards of Swansea. All HMOs, irrespective of size, have to be licensed in these wards... Student accommodation which is owned and managed by a university is exempt from licensing.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED DECISIVELY, table extracted from the live fees page (last modified 1 April 2026), single discounted payment: 3 occupiers £1,096; 4 £1,176; 5 £1,256; 6 £1,336; 7 £1,416; 8 £1,496; 9 £1,576; 10 £1,656; rising by £80 per occupier to 20 occupiers £2,456. Early renewal runs £1,024 to £2,384. THE LADDER STARTS AT THREE OCCUPIERS, NOT FIVE. A mandatory-only authority's ladder starts at five, so this is conclusive cost recovery for sub-mandatory HMOs and therefore a genuine s.56 scheme. The widely-quoted £2,456 figure is confirmed as the 20-occupier single-payment fee. WARD NAMES VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT REGISTER, THE HIGHEST-RISK ITEM, AND IT PASSES. Swansea's electoral arrangements were reviewed and new wards took effect at the May 2022 elections, which is when Waterfront ward was created. The designation was made on 2 October 2025 and took effect on 14 February 2026, BOTH AFTER that review, so the names are current, not stale. Swansea's live ward list was independently pulled from its democracy site and all four (Castle, Uplands, Waterfront, St Thomas) appear verbatim in the current 31-ward register. NO stale ward names flagged. Coverage is 'wards' because the designation is expressed in whole electoral wards, not streets. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, EVIDENCED IN BOTH LANGUAGES: zero URLs containing 'selectiv' across 6,744 English sitemap URLs; zero 'trwyddedu dewisol' across 6,890 Welsh URLs, where the only 'dewisol' hits are elective home education and discretionary housing payments; zero occurrences of 'selective' in the full HMO Licensing Policy 2025; and zero across ten further housing and landlord pages. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES. (2) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION: the working brief warned Swansea has one. IT DOES NOT. Zero hits for 'article 4' across the HMO and planning pages. In Wales the C4 use class came into force in February 2016 WITHOUT permitted development rights for C3 to C4, so planning permission is always required and no Article 4 is needed. Swansea's planning control is instead LDP Policy H9 plus HMO and purpose-built student accommodation SPG. The policy itself says at para 1.11 that licensing 'cannot address HMO density issues, which are a Planning matter'. (3) '(ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS) (WALES) REGULATIONS 2007', a s.257 MANAGEMENT instrument. (4) 'FEES FOR ADDITIONAL OCCUPANTS', per-occupier laddering. (5) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL at policy para 6.1. (6) The s.254 definition at para 5.2. (7) Borough-wide MANDATORY licensing, which is not a designation. LIMITATIONS: swansea.gov.uk returns HTTP 403 to plain requests; this is a BOT BLOCK, NOT EVIDENCE, and adding a browser User-Agent plus Accept, Accept-Language and Referer returned HTTP 200 on every page. The council's own site search is JavaScript-driven and UNUSABLE, the positive control returning a response byte-identical in size to the nonsense negative control, so no nil result from it is relied on. THE PREDECESSOR: the 2020 scheme ceased on 14 February 2026, the same day the new one took effect, so cover was continuous; it is not recorded as a separate object because it is immediately superseded and its precise start date is not published.

E06000030.research: NEGATIVE, sourced, with an unbroken chain 2005 to 2019 to 2021/22 to 2023 to 2026. (1) THE ORIGINAL DECISION NOT TO DESIGNATE. Environment and Leisure Overview Committee, 6 December 2005, item 22 'Houses in Multiple Occupancy'. After a statutory-powers recital at 5.12-5.14 the report states VERBATIM at 5.13: 'It is unlikely that Additional or Selective licensing would be justifiable in any area of Swindon at the present time.' And at 5.29: 'At the present time there is insufficient evidence to seek additional selective licensing powers for any area of the town. Swindon is an area of high housing demand and there is no substantiated link between anti social behavior and the concentration of HMOs in certain areas.' (2) GOVERNING POLICY. Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy (February 2019), para 7.8.8, VERBATIM: 'At present there are no declared Additional or Selective Licensing schemes in Swindon. Where a need for such arises in the future the Council will review whether to declare such a scheme.' Approved at Cabinet 6 February 2019. This is an affirmative statement of nil status, NOT civil-penalty boilerplate; the policy's civil-penalty section is separate and makes no reference to Part 2 or Part 3 designations. (3) STILL CURRENT AFTER AMENDMENT: the committee system holds 'Minor Amendment to Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy 2019' (issue notice 25 March 2022), whose tracked-changes appendix is headed 'February 2019 v2. February 2021' and retains para 7.8.8 VERBATIM AND UNAMENDED. (4) MOST RECENT AFFIRMATIVE CONFIRMATION, OCTOBER 2023: 'Cabinet Member Q&A - Cabinet Member for Housing', Overview and Scrutiny Committee 16 October 2023, para 3.36 VERBATIM: 'There are currently 330 Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) that are licensed under the mandatory scheme in Swindon. The mandatory scheme captures private shared houses with 5 or more unrelated occupants who share amenities. Swindon has no Additional or Selective licensing schemes in place.' (5) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, PASSED: schedule headed 'Application fees for HMO licence 2026 to 2027 - effective from 1 April 2026', banded by OCCUPANT COUNT only: 'Up to 10 occupants / Online / £800.23 / £673.88 / £1,474.11'; paper £1,755.18; 'More than 10 occupants' £1,684.70 online and £1,965.48 paper. No selective fee, no additional fee, no second application route. (6) CURRENT GUIDANCE: 'If the HMO occupies five or more people from more than one household, the property requires a licence.' All five HMO sub-pages grepped for 'selective', 'additional licen', 'section 56', 'section 80' and 'designat': ZERO hits. (7) SITEMAP SWEEP, CONTROL PASSED: 10,745 URLs, control 'houses_in_multiple_occupation' returned 10 hits, and no selective or additional licensing page exists. (8) COMMITTEE SEARCH, CONTROL PASSED. METHOD NOTE WORTH RECORDING: plain curl against ieSearchResults2.aspx returns 'No results found for your query' for EVERY query INCLUDING controls, because the working URL needs DT=3&SB=true plus a real session; a curl-only nil result here would have been worthless. The real form was driven in a browser. Control 'council tax' returned results (PASS); control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 20+ results including 'Fee Structure for Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing' (PASS). Quoted phrase searches: 'selective licensing' 6 results, 'additional licensing' 14 results, 'landlord licensing' 0, 'borough wide licensing' 0, 'section 80 of the Housing Act' 0. No designation, consultation or proposing report. Known index limitation: the DocType sub-indexes for Consultations, Mini-site pages and Library documents return nothing even for control terms, so those are broken; DocType=3 works and was used. TRAPS EXCLUDED, each named: (a) 'SELECTIVE LETTINGS', the biggest trap here because filenames contain 'selective': 'Selective Lettings Policy for Council New Build Schemes', 'Selective Lettings Railway Village, Swindon' and site plans for Penhill and Malmesbury Gardens. The Malmesbury Gardens PDF was downloaded and read: it describes a Cabinet Member Decision Note of 6 September 2010 governing CHOICE-BASED LETTINGS ALLOCATION of 13 council new-build homes via 'Swindon Home Bid'. Social housing ALLOCATION, not Part 3 licensing. (b) MHCLG DEVOLUTION LETTER, Council 16 January 2025, quoting central government: 'We will also be changing the process for selective licensing, so that local authorities will no longer need to seek Secretary of State approval when implementing schemes covering more than 20% of their area or private rented sector.' NATIONAL POLICY, not a Swindon designation. (c) ASB Task Group 2007 contains one bullet, 'Consideration given to using selective licensing of landlords', with no recommendation or resolution following. (d) Swindon's HMO activity in 2011-2014 ran through PLANNING, not licensing; its only Article 4 directions are Bishopstone and Swindon Railway Village conservation-area directions, neither an HMO C3-to-C4 direction. (e) 12 of the 14 'additional licensing' hits are Licensing Panel decisions imposing 'additional licensing conditions' on pubs and shops. (f) 'Re-designation of Some Town Centre streets for Street Trading Purposes'. (g) s.254 definition trap. (h) 'speech_and_language_selective_mutism'. (i) Two 2025/2026 town-centre landlord news items read in full: no designation. (j) 'Licensing initiatives' pages cover 'Ask for Angela', LSAVI and Wheelchair Accessible Vehicles. (k) 'district_level_licensing' is Natural England great crested newt licensing. LIMITATION: Swindon's public website search is JavaScript-driven and returns only a 1,738-byte shell to curl, so it could not be control-tested and was given no weight; the sitemap sweep and browser-driven committee search were used instead and both passed their controls.

E08000008.research: PRIMARY SOURCE: the council's HMO page, reached via /housing/private-sector-housing. THRESHOLD, VERBATIM, in a highlighted note at the top: '(As of 1st October 2018 HMOs that are occupied by five or more people that form two or more households with any number of storeys will be licensable.)' DECISIVE NEGATIVE WORDING, VERBATIM: 'Not all HMOs are licensable so landlords need to look at the criteria below.' and, under 'If the HMO is not licensable under the guidelines above?', 'If your HMO is not classed as a licensable HMO (see above) then you do not need to apply for a licence. you still need to abide by the Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (England) Regulations 2006'. A council operating s.56 additional licensing could not tell landlords that non-mandatory HMOs need no licence. The page frames the scheme as mandatory: 'Under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004, owners and landlords must now get a licence to manage certain larger, higher-risk Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs).' NOTE that MANDATORY licensing also sits in Part 2 (ss.55-61); s.56 is the additional-licensing power, and nothing on the page exercises it. The word 'selective' does not appear anywhere on this page. SITEMAP SWEEP PASSED ITS CONTROL: Tameside's XML sitemap index is a Liferay per-layout index listing 2,110 sub-sitemaps, which is not practically fetchable, so the council's own HTML sitemap was used (HTTP 200, 508,992 bytes, 1,934 links). CONTROL: the grep for 'hmo' returned a genuine hit, so a nil result is meaningful. The grep for 'selective' across all 1,934 links returned ZERO matches. The housing section it enumerates contains no selective-licensing page and no second landlord licence route. CORROBORATION: the housing standards enforcement policy page was fetched and grepped for both 'selective' and 'additional licen': ZERO hits for each. This is notable because the enforcement policy is normally where the s.95 civil-penalty boilerplate appears, so here not even the boilerplate false positive arises. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The s.254 DEFINITION trap: the page defines an HMO as a home where 'three or more people live, and at least two groups of people live separately within the home, and facilities such as bathrooms and kitchens are shared'; the licensing threshold is stated separately as five or more. Three- and four-person HMOs are NOT licensable in Tameside. (2) 'Additional information / documentation must be presented when requested by an Officer' is ordinary English about paperwork, not s.56. (3) NEIGHBOUR BLEED actively guarded against: Manchester and Salford both operate discretionary schemes and Tameside borders them, so this was the highest-risk council in the batch for contamination. Every source cited is on tameside.gov.uk. LIMITATIONS: (a) TAMESIDE'S SITE SEARCH FAILED ITS CONTROL QUERY AND ITS NIL RESULT PROVES NOTHING. The search returns HTTP 200 for both queries, but results are rendered client-side by Liferay: extracting every link from the CONTROL response and from the real response produced the SAME eleven links in both cases, all site chrome. The control returned no HMO result despite the HMO page indisputably existing. NO weight was placed on it. (b) The A-Z index is incomplete (letter H lists Housing Services and Housing Benefits but not the HMO page), so it was used only as a supplementary check; letter S contained no 'selective' entry. (c) No control-tested committee-paper search was obtained, so an unpublicised historic committee discussion cannot be positively excluded; a live designation would have to appear on the service pages and in a fee schedule, and it does not.

E07000215.research: PRIMARY SOURCE, EXPLICIT NEGATIVE. Under the heading 'When an HMO requires a licence' the council states VERBATIM: 'Under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004 all local authorities are required to operate the mandatory HMO licensing scheme.' immediately followed by 'Tandridge District Council does not operate an Additional or Selective Licensing Scheme.' An unambiguous, self-declared negative for BOTH s.56 and s.80, published by the council on its own domain. This string was confirmed in the RAW HTML via curl with a browser user-agent, not merely in a rendered summary. Threshold, VERBATIM: 'An HMO will require a licence if it is occupied by five or more persons forming two or more households. This includes HMOs occupied by a live in landlord and four or more tenants.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'An HMO licence costs £868.50 and lasts for five years. However, we may issue a licence for a 12 month period if we consider the management arrangements to be unsatisfactory.' A SINGLE mandatory fee, with no selective fee, no additional fee and no second application route. The reduced 12-month licence is a management-standards sanction under mandatory licensing, not a separate scheme. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, genuinely present so excluded explicitly. The same page states VERBATIM: 'Tandridge District Council has introduced an Article 4 Direction in relation to HMOs in Caterham on the hill, Caterham Valley and Whyteleafe. This removes permitted development rights for all HMOs in these areas.' PLANNING control over C3-to-C4 change of use. It is NOT licensing, creates no licence requirement and triggers no rent repayment order. Recorded here solely so it is not mistaken for a designation; the three named areas are the Article 4 area, NOT a licensing area, so no wards are returned. (2) The s.254 HMO DEFINITION trap: 'An HMO is defined in law as a house or flat in which three or more unrelated persons, forming two or more households share an amenity'. Three-person HMOs are NOT licensable in Tandridge. (3) A further PLANNING trap on the same page: 'An HMO requires planning permission if it is to be occupied by 7 or more persons.' Planning permission is not a licence, and the page itself flags the distinction: 'The Licensing of HMOs is governed by the Housing Act 2004, this is separate to Planning Legislation and Building Control regulations.' (4) The 'Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004' recital is the statutory-powers recital for MANDATORY licensing. VERIFICATION OF THE SECTION: the full private-housing sub-page list contains exactly four internal sub-pages plus one outbound GOV.UK link: Houses in multiple occupation, Energy savings advice and grants, Smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, Enforcement policy, and gov.uk/private-renting. There is no selective or additional licensing page and no second application route. The Renting-your-property page covers only the Private Rented Access Scheme (a tenant-matching scheme, correctly excluded) and Renters' Rights Act duties. The Enforcement policy page returned no 'selective', no 'additional licen', no 'Part 3' and no s.95 boilerplate. LIMITATIONS: (a) SITEMAP SWEEP NOT POSSIBLE. /sitemap.xml returns a DotNetNuke 404 error page and /sitemap also 404s. /SiteMap.aspx returns HTTP 200 with 92,291 bytes but contains ZERO href attributes, so it yields no crawlable URL list. robots.txt declares no Sitemap directive (the line is commented out as an unedited DNN template default). (b) THE COMMITTEE CHECK WAS INCONCLUSIVE: ieDocSearch.aspx returned a BYTE-IDENTICAL 28,731-byte response for the control and for both real queries, with zero document links (results are proxied to a client-side Cludo search). BROKEN, so its nil result proves nothing. NEITHER LIMITATION UNDERMINES THE NEGATIVE, because the council has published an express, current, on-domain statement that it operates neither scheme, backed by a single-band mandatory-only fee.

E07000045.research: NEGATIVE, sourced, with an unusually explicit council statement made twice. (1) PRIMARY STATEMENT. Housing Enforcement Policy 2025 (adopted by Executive 4 March 2025; landing page last updated 19 November 2025), section 2.05 'HMO Licensing', VERBATIM: 'We operate a mandatory licensing scheme under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004, which applies to all HMOs that are occupied by five or more persons, comprising two or more households and share facilities.' Immediately followed by, VERBATIM: 'We also have powers to extend licensing schemes to include both Additional and Selective Licensing Schemes, but currently do not operate either. This is kept under review.' Repeated VERBATIM in the appendix: 'A mandatory licence scheme currently operates in Teignbridge ... There are other schemes, namely Additional and Selective Licensing which are available to the Council not currently in operation but kept under review.' The adopting Executive report refers only to 'the Council's approach to mandatory licensing of HMOs'. (2) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, PASSED. 'Approved fees and charges 2026-2027'. Under 'Housing Fees and Charges' the licensing lines read VERBATIM: 'Licences HMO 346.00 (Part 2**)'; 'New Application (non-accredited landlord) 531.00 (Part 1)'; 'New Application (accredited landlords) 346.00 (Part 2) / 265.00 (Part 1)'; 'Re-licensing HMO (accredited landlord) 346.00 / 292.00'; 'Additional fee per units of accommodation 37.00'; '** Part 2 Fee - Fee to cover costs of running, managing and enforcing the scheme.' The word 'selective' appears ZERO times in the entire 63-page schedule. Every HMO fee is a mandatory-licence fee split Part 1 / Part 2, differentiated only by accredited vs non-accredited landlord. No scheme could be funded. (3) LIVE PAGE: 'You must apply for a mandatory HMO licence if your property: is occupied by five or more people; forms two or more households; shares facilities'. (4) SITEMAP SWEEP, CONTROL PASSED. /sitemap.xml 404s, but the bare /sitemap returns HTTP 200 and is a real XML urlset of 1,298 URLs. Freshness verified: latest lastmod 2026-08-04, the day before verification, and all 1,298 URLs are on the single live host, so this is NOT a stale or legacy-only sitemap. CONTROL: grep 'multiple-occupation' returns the HMO page. Grep 'selective' across all 1,298 URLs returns ZERO hits. (5) SEARCH CONTROLS, ALL PASSED. ModernGov: positive controls 'council tax' and 'houses in multiple occupation' both PASS; NEGATIVE control 'zzqxwv nonsense term' correctly returned 'No results found for your query'. Main site search: positive control PASS (8 results, HMO page first); negative control returned '0 results'. Both discriminate, so their nil results are meaningful. Real queries returned only loose word-matches, none a designation. TRAPS EXCLUDED, each named: (a) CIVIL-PENALTY BOILERPLATE, THE SINGLE MOST LIKELY THING TO BE MISREAD HERE: the enforcement policy's offence schedule lists VERBATIM 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses under Part 3 [section 95]' and 'Maximum Court fine ... for failure to license an HMO or Part 3 House - Unlimited'. This enumerates offences the council COULD charge and is directly contradicted by section 2.05 of the same document. (b) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL, negated in the same sentence by 'but currently do not operate either'. (c) 'Additional fee per units of accommodation 37.00' is a PER-UNIT SURCHARGE on a mandatory licence. (d) 'Additional Licensable Activity 250.00' and related lines sit in the ANIMAL WELFARE block (Zoo licence, Dangerous animals, Dog Breeding), nothing to do with housing. (e) VOLUNTARY ACCREDITATION: reduced fees for NRLA and South West Landlords Association members, a discount not a scheme. (f) s.254 DEFINITION trap. (g) s.257 RECITAL: 'the self-contained flats situated within the S257 HMO may be subject to Additional HMO, Mandatory HMO, or Selective licensing' describes what the law permits generally, not what Teignbridge has designated. (h) ARTICLE 4: a sitemap grep returns ZERO Article 4 hits, so the commonest error does not arise here. (i) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: no Exeter, Torbay or Plymouth material was relied on. No limitations: every search used passed its control query.

E07000076.research: PRIMARY SOURCE, DECISIVE: the council's own 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Policy', Introduced September 2021, Updated September 2024 (11 pages), linked from the live HMO service page. THE WORD 'SELECTIVE' APPEARS ZERO TIMES IN THE ENTIRE POLICY, AND 'ADDITIONAL LICENSING' ZERO TIMES. Its licensing section is headed '4.3 HMO MANDATORY LICENSING' and states VERBATIM: 'Mandatory HMO Licensing was first introduced in Part II of the Housing Act 2004 and came into force in 2006. The rules on HMO licensing were amended in October 2018 and now, an HMO must be licensed if it accommodates at least 5 people in 2 or more different households ... There are currently 34 HMOs in the Tendring district that require a mandatory licence.' Section '4.5 NON-LICENSABLE HMO'S' is the clinching evidence, VERBATIM: 'not all HMOs are required to be licensed which applies to properties where at least three but less than five tenants live in a property forming more than one household ... whilst a licence is not required by law, the properties are still required to meet standards as set out in the Housing Health and Safety Rating System'. It quantifies them: 'There are an estimated 149 non-licensable HMOs in the district.' A council operating s.56 additional licensing could not have 149 unlicensable HMOs. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, VERBATIM: 'There is fee payable to obtain a licence for an HMO in the district and this currently costs £878.00 with an additional charge of £25.00 per room for properties with over six rooms. The licence will generally last for five years.' ONE fee for ONE mandatory scheme. THIS COUNCIL REQUIRED EXTRA CARE BECAUSE ITS PUBLIC-FACING PAGE IS AMBIGUOUSLY WORDED. The live page asks 'Do I need a licence?' answering 'Yes - if you want to rent out an HMO, you must apply for a licence before you start', immediately after defining an HMO as '3 or more people live there'. READ LITERALLY THAT WOULD IMPLY ADDITIONAL LICENSING, AND IT IS WRONG. The same page's later section restores the threshold: 'If your HMO has 5 or more people from 2 or more households, and they share things like kitchens or bathrooms, you must...'. The loose sentence was NOT treated as evidence of a designation; it was resolved against the council's formal 2024 policy, which is explicit that 3-4 person HMOs are non-licensable. Worth flagging for any re-check. SITEMAP SWEEP PASSED ITS CONTROL: HTTP 200, 232,855 bytes, 1,879 URLs on the live host. CONTROL: the grep for 'multiple-occupation|hmo' returned three genuine hits, so a nil result is meaningful. The grep for 'selective' across all 1,879 URLs returned ZERO matches. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, AND TENDRING HAS AN UNUSUALLY BROAD ONE, so this is the single most important exclusion for this council. Policy section 3.1 states VERBATIM: 'There is a district wide Article 4 Direction in operation in the Tendring area. The Article 4 Direction came into force in May 2013 ... Tendring District Council has made an Article 4 Direction removing this permitted change in all parts of the district and therefore any proposal involving the creation of an HMO or bedsits in the Tendring District will require planning permission.' A DISTRICT-WIDE HMO Article 4 is very easily mistaken for district-wide licensing. It is PLANNING control, creates NO licence requirement and carries NO rent repayment order exposure; the council's own page for it sits under Planning and Building Control. (2) JAYWICK SANDS AND CLACTON REGENERATION, flagged specifically in the brief. The full news list was read: the Jaywick and Clacton interventions are CAPITAL REGENERATION and grant programmes ('£20million of exciting projects to regenerate Clacton and Jaywick Sands', 'Sunspot', 'Jaywick Sands Healthy Homes Team', road repairs, community gardens, new town and parish councils) plus a 'Jaywick Sands Place Plan' under Planning Policy. NONE is a licensing designation. There is no Jaywick or Clacton selective licensing scheme on the council's domain. (3) Civil-penalty and statutory-powers material in the policy enumerates powers, not designations. (4) 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' is a statutory instrument title about s.257 management, NOT s.56. (5) 'an additional charge of £25.00 per room for properties with over six rooms' is the classic per-room surcharge trap. (6) 'Essex Amenity Standards', described as 'a pan-Essex agreement to ensure consistent management and conditions standards in all HMOs across the County', is a VOLUNTARY inter-authority standards agreement. (7) The s.254 DEFINITION trap on the live page. LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY: the authoritative HMO Policy PDF is hosted on legacy.tendringdc.gov.uk, a legacy subdomain, rather than the main www host; it is linked directly from the current live HMO page, so it remains the council's published policy, but a future re-check should confirm it has not been superseded on the new platform. No control-tested committee-paper search was obtained. Neither point undermines the negative, which rests on an explicit 'non-licensable HMOs' section, a single mandatory fee and a zero-hit control-passed sitemap sweep.

E07000093.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. The Additional HMO licensing scheme would apply in cases where it is expected that an especially high number of HMOs concentrated in any area would give rise to additional problems. Selective licensing can require any private rented property to have a licence... The adoption of such additional schemes would not be warranted within the Test Valley area currently, although this will be kept under review. Accordingly, at present the Council will operate the mandatory HMO licensing scheme only.' FEE TEST PASSED: the HMO page (Last Updated 17 July 2026) lists 2025/26 and 2026/27 as 'Licence application (up to 5 year licence)' 455.00 / 466.00; 'additional charge per room for HMO above 5 rooms' 25.00; 'Licence renewal' 374.00 / 383.00; Part 2 'Operation charge (HMO licensing scheme)' 249.00; 'Supplementary operation charge' 330.00 / 338.00. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4 directions: TVBC has nine since 1972 plus five earlier and EVERY one is a named land parcel (Staddlestone Farm, The Middleway, Land adj Cottage Road Middle Wallop, Wellow Drove, Blackwater Bridge, Allens Copse, Stockbridge Road Timsbury, Newtown Road Awbridge, Upper Clatford, King Lane Over Wallop, plus pre-1972 New Street, Linkenholt Estate, Rooksbury Mill, Castle Lane North Baddesley, Butlers Wood). None is a C3-to-C4 HMO direction, and Article 4 is planning control not licensing in any event. (5) The Council Tax privacy notice recital, the only other site-wide hit for 'selective': 'Parts 1-4 of the Housing Act 2004 (Housing Conditions, Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation, Selective ...)', a data-protection legal-basis recital. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times in the entire 10-page consolidated fee list, and the only other housing-related licence block is caravan and mobile home site licensing. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the Draft Civil Penalty Policy lists 'offences in relation to Licensing of houses under Housing Act 2004 Part 3, (Section 95)' adjacent to s.30, s.72, s.139(7) and s.234. (2) Article 4 directions: Tewkesbury's are conservation-area directions (Ashleworth Green, Bishops Cleeve) withdrawing permitted development for 'replacement windows, new fences and walls or domestic extensions'. Nothing to do with HMOs. (3) 'District licensing scheme' under biodiversity is GREAT CRESTED NEWT district licensing under the Conservation of Habitats Regulations. The name is dangerously close to district-wide property licensing and is not it. (4) 'Private lettings scheme - Support for landlords' is a voluntary incentive scheme (£100 finder's fee, deposit paid in full) to source affordable tenancies, the 'selective lettings' trap. (5) The per-person surcharge above five occupants. CONFIDENCE NOTE: unlike Test Valley, Tewkesbury publishes no document saying in terms 'we do not operate selective licensing'. The negative rests on four independent lines: no fee line in the current consolidated schedule, no page in a complete 965-URL sitemap, no committee paper in a control-validated ModernGov search, and an HMO page setting the threshold at five occupants. Sound, but one notch below Test Valley's certainty. LIMITATION: WebSearch budget exhausted before work began. No live consultation on either scheme type was found, and a designation would statutorily require public consultation first.

E07000102.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE, WITH A LIVE REVIEW COMMITMENT. This council came closest in the batch to a genuine positive and was resolved against primary committee papers. TWO DECISIVE SOURCES. (1) TRDC's own HMO Licensing Policy, April 2026 (approved Policy and Resources Committee 29 June 2026), section 5 'Types of Licensing': s.5.2 Additional Licensing, 'At the time of adopting this policy, Three Rivers District Council does not operate an Additional Licensing scheme, however reserve the right to adopt Additional Licensing at any point if required. This position will be reviewed every 12 months.' s.5.3 Selective Licensing, 'At the time of adopting this policy, Three Rivers District Council does not operate a Selective Licensing scheme, however reserve the right to adopt Selective Licensing at any point where evidence demonstrates it would address local housing problems.' Section 4 confirms scope: 'Under the mandatory licensing scheme currently operated by the council, a property must be licensed... Is occupied by five or more people / Forms two or more households / Shares basic amenities.' (2) Policy and Resources Committee, 26 January 2026, item PR1424 'REVIEW OF HMO ADDITIONAL LICENCING AND CONSIDERATION OF ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION'. The printed minutes record RESOLVED: 'Based on evidence at this time, additional licensing for HMOs is not progressed, however, this will be reviewed in 12 months' time. Based on evidence at this time, that an Article 4 direction is not progressed...' A Cooper/Edwards amendment to replace 'is not progressed' with 'is progressed' on both limbs was PUT TO THE VOTE AND LOST, For 4, Against 8, Abstention 1. IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: the narrative section of those same minutes contains the loose phrase 'HMOs... were already regulated through the Council's additional licensing scheme'. This is minute-taker error, resolved against the officer report in the supplementary agenda, which states at 3.1.9 'The council currently operate a mandatory HMO licensing scheme' and at 3.1.16 'it is the Officer recommendation that at this current time any progression with additional licensing by the council would currently be disproportionate and premature.' The report records only 13 licensed HMOs in the district and notes 'no other local authority located within Hertfordshire has introduced additional licensing'. HISTORY: Full Council on 21 October 2025 asked officers to review 'an additional licencing scheme, which would require landlords of small HMOs occupied by less than five occupants to apply to the council for a licence', which produced the January 2026 decision. Explored, formally declined, no consultation, no fee. RE-CHECK around January to April 2027 when the 12-month review falls due. FEE TEST: TRDC's 'Licensing Fees 2026-2027' contains no property or HMO licensing fees at all; its headings are Hackney Carriage and Private Hire, Sex Establishment, Street trading, Premises Licence, Club Premises Certificate, TEN, Personal Licence, gaming permits, Small Society Lottery, Scrap Metal, Pavement Licence and Hypnotism. CONTROLS: TRDC's own site search is BROKEN; the control, real and nonsense queries all returned the same ~318KB client-rendered page with an identical default listing (similarity of nonsense vs real query 0.9995). The on-site meetings archive is STALE, ending 30 April 2023, and 2026 meeting URLs return a soft-404 catch-all listing rather than a 404 status. The live committee system is moderngov.threerivers.gov.uk (threerivers.moderngov.co.uk and democracy.threerivers.gov.uk do not resolve); its document search PASSED controls. Sitemap sweep of sitemap-0.xml (2,773 URLs) found exactly one HMO service page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) LIVE DISTRICT-WIDE ARTICLE 4 CONSULTATION, the exact look-alike: 'Article 4 Direction - Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) District wide', agreed at Policy and Resources 1 June 2026, representations by 16 August 2026, in force about 12 months later. It is PLANNING: 'The Direction will require an application to be made to the council for the grant of planning permission before a property can be developed into an HMO.' (2) A 2022 Article 4 Direction (effective 29 March 2024) covers Class E to C3 commercial-to-residential, unrelated to HMOs. (3) s.254 definition on the landing page versus the stated mandatory threshold of five. (4) 'Additional fee' lines in the fee PDF are a premises licence surcharge for events of 5,000+ attendance; 'Additional site 649.00' is Scrap Metal Dealers Act. (5) 'decision made by a designated officer under delegated authority' is officer delegation, not a s.56 or s.80 designation. (6) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: TRDC shares services with Watford BC; every source relied on is TRDC's own. LIMITATION: WebSearch budget exhausted. No expired designation was found and none is referenced in any policy or committee paper.

E07000115.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Primary source, under the heading 'Licensing HMOs': 'We only operate mandatory licensing of HMOs that meet one of the first three tests above and where the property is occupied by five or more people made up of more than one household. A mandatory HMO licence is not required for self-contained flats in purpose built blocks of three or more flats.' The word 'only' is the council's own. FEE TEST PASSED, verbatim from the same page: 'Fees from 1 April 2026 are as follows: new HMO licence - £810; renewal HMO licence - £727'. One licence type, one route, no discretionary cost-recovery fee. Historic fee decisions use the same framing: Communities and Housing Advisory Board 14 Nov 2016 and Cabinet 9 Feb 2017 set 'fees and charges in respect of the mandatory licensing scheme for Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) and Caravan Sites'. CORROBORATION: the Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy 2022, p.14: 'The Housing Act 2004 introduced a mandatory scheme to licence HMOs, and this was extended in 2018 to include an HMO occupied by five or more people, comprising two or more households...' No other licensing scheme is described anywhere in its 40 pages. INDEPENDENT RAW-HTML CHECK: all five pages of the landlords and tenants guide were fetched with a browser user-agent and grepped in RAW HTML (not rendered text) for 'selective' and 'additional licen': zero occurrences on every page. Note the bare host tmbc.gov.uk does not resolve; www.tmbc.gov.uk returns 200. CONTROLS: the real search endpoint is /site-search/results/?q= (the /search?q= form 404s). The engine demonstrably returns zero, so its nil findings carry weight; it also indexes ModernGov documents. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate, the decisive one here: the only 'selective licensing' text in the 2022 enforcement policy is the s.249A relevant-housing-offences recital, 'Failing to licence a house subject to selective licensing under Part 3 (section 95(1))' and 'Failing to comply with the condition of a selective licence issued under Part 3'. (2) Article 4 Direction scoping report, Housing and Planning Scrutiny Select Committee 19 May 2026, item 22: planning not licensing, AND not made: 'the evidence base within the Borough was limited... the Council's Strategic Housing Market Assessment did not support the introduction of an Article 4 Direction at this stage.' Worth re-checking after that date, but it can only ever create a planning requirement, never a licence. (3) Every 'additional licensing' search hit was a Licensing and Appeals Committee page or the Statement of Licensing Policy 2025-2030. (4) The consultations page lists only a closed alcohol licensing policy consultation. (5) s.254 definition: the page sets out the Standard test, Self-contained flat test and Converted building test as what an HMO IS, then separately states the five-person threshold. LIMITATIONS: ModernGov's native mgSearchResults.aspx returns 'Error - page unavailable', so committee papers were searched via the council site search, which passed controls and did surface ModernGov PDFs and decision records; good coverage but not exhaustive. A 2006 Cabinet report 'Housing Act 2004' mentions selective licensing and could not be retrieved (302 cross-host redirect); immaterial, because any 2006 designation would have expired by 2011 at the latest and every current source states mandatory-only. WebSearch budget exhausted before work began.

E06000027.research: NEGATIVE. Flagged for extra scrutiny as a coastal unitary with large bedsit stock in Torquay and Paignton; checked hard and cleared. FEE TEST PASSED, the entire housing licensing fee schedule verbatim: 'HMO licences last up to 5 years and have two payment parts: Part 1: Processing the application (non-refundable); Part 2: Managing the licence (paid after approval)... New application £2,007 (£485 / £1,522); New application (enforced) £2,859; Renewal application £1,709 (£428 / £1,281); Renewal application (enforced) £2,054.' There is no selective licence fee and no additional-HMO licence fee anywhere on the site, and applications are made via the single GOV.UK mandatory route. THRESHOLD TEST, INDEPENDENTLY DECISIVE: the council's 'quickly check if your property is an HMO' page gives worked examples: 'A house occupied by 5 students (2 of whom are living together), who share a kitchen and bathroom. Licensable because there are 5 occupiers in 4 households sharing basic amenities.' and 'Two bedroom bungalow shared by 2 couples. Not licensable because there are only 4 occupiers.' Under an additional licensing designation a 4-occupant, 2-household share WOULD be licensable; Torbay states positively that it is not. This also resolves the ambiguously-worded trap on the apply page ('To rent out an HMO, you need a licence'), exactly as with the Tendring precedent. The 'what is an HMO' page names exactly one scheme: 'Mandatory HMO licensing scheme. From 1 October 2018 mandatory licensing is no longer limited to certain HMOs that are 3 or more storeys high...'. RAW-HTML SWEEP: 11 housing and landlord pages grepped in raw HTML: 'selective' 0, 'additional' 0, 'designat' 0. CONTROLS: site search PASSED both ways; control returned 124 results, nonsense returned 'Your search did not match any documents', and 'selective licensing' returned ONE document, a procurement page 'How we invite bids and select suppliers', a stem match on 'select'. Note /sitemap.xml 404s while the bare /sitemap returns 200 with 5,825 URLs; that sweep found only HMO-landlord pages. COMMITTEE PAPERS: the mgSearchResults.aspx path does not exist and returns a byte-identical 5,074-byte 404 for every query INCLUDING the control, which would have been a false nil; the working endpoint is ieSearchResults.aspx via POST. That PASSED controls (16 document hits vs 0 for nonsense, with a distinct response size). The exact phrase 'selective licensing' returns 5 documents in Torbay's ENTIRE committee history, latest 2012: a 2012 scrutiny review recommending 'That targeted selective and/or additional licensing of houses in multiple occupation be prioritised', and the Mayoral Record of Decision of 14 June 2012 in which that recommendation was NOT accepted, being deferred to a service review and budget prioritisation 'as additional resources will be required.' Never designated, and absent from committee papers in the 14 years since. MOST RECENT PRIMARY SOURCE, 13 months before verification: Cabinet 14 July 2025, 'Housing Standards Civil Penalty Policy and HMO Licence Conditions Review', a full review describing only mandatory licensing. CORROBORATION: the Housing Strategy 2023-2030 contains zero occurrences of 'licen' or 'HMO'; the HMO register (last updated July 2026) holds 144 licensed properties, consistent with mandatory-only, whereas an additional scheme across Torquay and Paignton would produce many hundreds. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4, and a correction to the working assumption: Torbay does NOT have an HMO Article 4 direction. Its statutory MHCLG dataset holds exactly two records, Polsham (11 April 2002) and Churston (5 November 1998), both conservation-area directions. A bay-wide C3-to-C4 HMO Article 4 was PROPOSED to Council on 16 May 2012 but does not appear in the adopted dataset. (2) Civil-penalty boilerplate: the single 2025 hit is 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses under Part 3 [section 95]'. (3) 'Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' is the s.257 statutory instrument, not s.56. (4) Cabinet Appendix 3 'List of additional conditions for Torbay HMO's' is extra conditions on mandatory licences. (5) s.254 definition versus the stated threshold of five. (6) All 'additional licensing' hits were taxi, private hire, alcohol, club premises, gambling permits and leaflet distribution. (7) Torbay's voluntary Landlord Accreditation Scheme was closed to new applicants from July 2012. WARD NAMES: not applicable; no designation has ever been made, so no ward or area list exists. LIMITATIONS: WebSearch budget exhausted. ModernGov's date-range filter is server-side broken (StartDate/EndDate POST params ignored), compensated by verifying the index covers 2025-2026 material and reading dates off each hit.
