W06000020.research: NEGATIVE, SOURCED, AND THE MAIN PAGE IS A TEXTBOOK STATUTORY-POWERS TRAP. THE TRAP FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: a raw-HTML grep of the HMO page returns SIX hits for 'selectiv' and TWO for 'additional licen'. Every single one is a generic recital of the statutory framework, not a designation. The page says: 'Do all HMOs have to be licensed? No. Under the Housing Act 2004 there are three types of licensing: Mandatory (required by law)... Additional licensing of HMOs - A discretionary power that councils MAY decide to apply to a particular type of HMO... Selective licensing of other residential accommodation - Properties that are not subject to HMO licensing COULD be covered under a selective licensing scheme. This is where the council MAY declare that certain areas... are appropriate for selective licensing.' Note the modal verbs: 'may decide to apply', 'could be covered', 'may declare'. There is NO designation, NO named area, NO commencement or expiry date and NO fee attached to either discretionary type. The hit count is inflated because the page body is duplicated in an embedded JSON content payload as well as the rendered HTML, exactly the collapsed-JSON pattern that causes false positives, so the six hits are really the same two sentences counted three times. This is the single most likely source of a wrong answer at Torfaen. THE POSITIVE EVIDENCE OF MANDATORY-ONLY: (1) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the applying-for-a-licence page states a SINGLE FLAT FEE, 'The fee is £708.00 for a 5 year licence.' There is no ladder, no small-HMO or sub-mandatory band, no per-property fee and no separate application route. That page returns ZERO raw hits for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen'. (2) REGISTER TEST: the public register ('Register updated 5 August 2024') contains exactly ONE licensed property: 'Licence No 151780, Issue Date 31/7/2024, Expiry Date 31/07/2029, Station House, 1 Station Street, Abersychan, Pontypool, NP4 8ph, Max Occupiers 5, Storeys 3.' Five occupiers and three storeys is precisely the mandatory threshold. Under an additional licensing scheme the register would necessarily contain sub-mandatory HMOs; it contains none. (3) SITEMAP SWEEP: the full sitemap (3,522 URLs covering both the /en/ and /cy/ trees) grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol', 'amlfedd' and 'trwydd' returns ZERO hits for every one of those terms in both languages. The only HMO pages on the entire site are the four English pages and their four Welsh mirrors. WELSH THRESHOLD: Torfaen states the mandatory test in the Welsh three-storey form, consistent with WSI 2006/1712 (W.174). OTHER TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES, the reason a Torfaen landlord can correctly be told they need 'a licence' while no local designation exists. (2) The s.254 DEFINITION: 'A House in Multiple Occupation HMO (sometimes called a house share) is a property rented out by at least 3 people who are not from 1 household and who share basic amenities' defines an HMO, NOT a licensing threshold; the 'at least 3 people' figure must not be read as a trigger. (3) The s.257 CONVERTED-FLATS TEST. (4) The 'converting a property to an HMO' planning page. LIMITATIONS: the council's own site search was not relied on; the negative rests on the complete 3,522-URL bilingual sitemap sweep, raw-HTML greps of all HMO pages, the single flat fee and the composition of the public register.

E07000046.research: NEGATIVE. Treated as elevated risk because Torridge is coastal (Bideford, Northam, Westward Ho!) and coastal towns with bedsit stock are where designations cluster; cleared on primary evidence. PRIMARY SOURCE, the only HMO licensing page, verbatim: 'HMO Licences - With effect from 1st October 2018, The Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Description) (England) Order 2018... Its effect is that mandatory licensing will apply to HMOs that are below three storeys (as well as to those of three or more storeys) where the property: is occupied by 5 or more persons; and is occupied by persons living in two or more separate households; and who share an amenity such as a kitchen, toilet, bathroom or lounge'. And decisively: 'A property that is classed as an HMO does not necessarily need licensing, but is still an HMO.' That sentence is incompatible with any additional licensing designation. The only application route is the GOV.UK mandatory route. INDEPENDENT RAW-HTML CHECK of that page: zero occurrences of 'selective' or 'additional licen'. FEE TEST PASSED: 'Fees and Charges 2026-27'. The entire Housing section contains these and only these licensing lines: 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Licence / Part A - Application Fee (Plus DBS Fee) / Part B - Grant Fee (Management and Enforcement) / Renewal' and 'HMO Licence Variation / Inspection required / No Inspection required'. 2026/27 values against the HMO licence rows are £341.00 (Part A) and £787.00 (Part B). CAVEAT: this PDF's text layer misaligns its price columns, so the label set is authoritative and the individual figures are indicative. There is no selective and no additional licensing fee anywhere in the schedule. CONTROLS: Torridge's site search PASSED both ways; control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 376 loose hits, nonsense 'zzqqxwplop' returned 'found no results', and 'designation' returned 227 hits with genuine neighbourhood-plan results, proving the engine indexes that term. Against that working engine: 'selective licensing' no results; 'additional licensing' no results; 'selective licence' no results; 'licensing scheme' one result (Boat and Skipper licences). SITEMAP SWEEP: 2,032 URLs, independently retrieved and grepped; the only HMO URL in the entire estate is /hmos, and every other 'licen' URL is boat skipper, animal welfare, scrap metal, caravan and camping, gambling, taxi or alcohol licensing. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The 'HMO Licensing Scope and Schemes' PDF, the most dangerous item here. Its title reads like a designation and it contains a full section headed 'Additional Licensing Schemes'. It is a generic statutory explainer, 'An LHA can make an additional licensing scheme...', signed off 'Produced by Environwest (UK) Ltd for Torridge District Council January 2007'. Pure statutory-powers recital. (2) The Housing Enforcement Policy May 2026: 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]' sits inside a bulleted list headed 'The Council has the power to impose a Civil Financial Penalty for the following'. (3) The housing-regulation page: 'Failure to obtain a selective HMO licence [S.95(1)]', again inside a list of offences the team CAN investigate. (4) Article 4 Directions: conservation-area and heritage permitted-development control, returned alongside Conservation Areas and the Local Heritage List. (5) s.254 definition wording versus the stated threshold of five. LIMITATION, THE ONE GENUINE GAP: the ModernGov committee search FAILED its control; it returned nothing for any multi-word phrase and nothing for 'HMO', while 'housing' did return 5 results, i.e. the index responds but not consistently, and the ieSearchResults POST was tried across DocType 0-4. NO INFERENCE, POSITIVE OR NEGATIVE, SHOULD BE DRAWN FROM TORRIDGE COMMITTEE PAPERS. The negative rests on the fee-schedule test, the explicit 'does not necessarily need licensing' wording, a complete sitemap sweep and a control-validated site search returning zero for every phrase variant. WebSearch budget was exhausted before work began.

E08000009.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Flagged as a metropolitan borough between Manchester and Salford, both of which do run schemes; cleared on five converging primary sources. STRONGEST SINGLE SOURCE: Trafford's own completed DLUHC return, 'Local authority returns form: damp and mould in private rented properties', issued after the Secretary of State's letter of 19 November 2022 and published as an appendix to Council papers. Q1 'Please provide the full name of your local authority:' - 'Trafford Borough Council'. Q6 'Do you run any Selective and/or Additional Licensing schemes in your area?' - 'Neither'. Q7 'If you do run any licensing schemes, approximately how many properties are covered?' - 'N/A'. Source: democratic.trafford.gov.uk, Council 20 March 2024. SECOND: Executive report 27 November 2017, para 1.11, explicitly rules selective licensing out: 'Latest available data confirms that there is only one ward where this level is exceeded for private rented property, Priory Ward. Currently there is no evidence base for Priory ward which identifies that the criteria for selective licensing are being exceeded. This in itself means that we cannot consider Selective Private Sector Licensing.' Priory Ward is named ONLY as the ward meeting the private-rented-proportion precondition; NO DESIGNATION WAS EVER MADE, so it must not be rendered as a scheme or a ward list. FEE TEST PASSED, complete table verbatim: 'Fee on application for a licence £1012 up to and including 6 bedrooms, plus an additional fee of £25 for every bedroom thereafter'; 'Fee on granting of a licence £211'; 'Application to vary licence £331'; 'Pre-licence application advice £435'. One licence route, one fee stream. SCOPE PAGE: 'A property will require a mandatory HMO licence if it is rented to five or more people from more than one household', and no additional or selective tier appears anywhere in the 8-page HMO guide. The public register (Dec 2025) holds 76 licensed HMOs with NO licence-type column, consistent with a single mandatory regime. CONTROLS: the council site search uses parameter search_api_fulltext; the obvious 'search' parameter is silently inert, a methodology trap worth recording. Control returned the HMO page, SPD6 and Article 4 Directions; negative control 'zzqxwvnonsenseterm' returned 'No items to show', proving it can return zero. COMMITTEE PAPERS: the live system is democratic.trafford.gov.uk. Note trafford.moderngov.co.uk returns Cloudflare 522 (origin down) and democracy.trafford.gov.uk does not resolve; a 522 is not evidence. democratic.trafford.gov.uk PASSED both controls. Six differently-worded queries returned only planning applications, conservation-area appraisals, taxi licensing, climate reports and the enforcement policy. SITEMAP SWEEP: a two-part index (lastmod 2026-08-05), 2,704 URLs, 'selective' zero and 'additional.{0,3}licen' zero. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Article 4 Direction, borough-wide, and Trafford does have one, removing permitted development rights for C3-to-C4 conversion, introduced because of University Academy 92: 'There is an Article 4 Direction in place across Trafford that relates to Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs).' It triggers a PLANNING APPLICATION, never a licence. (2) s.95 civil-penalty and RRO boilerplate in the Place Directorate Enforcement Policy 2025, which alone generated 3 of about 11 committee hits. (3) The per-bedroom surcharge. (4) s.254 definition versus the threshold of five on the very next page. (5) 'Selective schools': the same 20 March 2024 Council document discusses grammar-school admissions ('All Trafford Selective Schools'). (6) Housing Allocation Policy 2025, the 'selective lettings' trap. (7) A grep hit for 'S56' on the HMO page proved on inspection to be random base64 noise inside a JavaScript blob, not a statutory reference, a direct illustration of why raw HTML must be read in context. (8) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Manchester or Salford was relied on. No expired scheme was found and no trace exists in committee records back to 2013; the 2017 wording 'we cannot consider' indicates none had ever been made. LIMITATIONS: WebSearch budget exhausted. ModernGov result pagination did not respond to a Page parameter, so the top 10 per query across six differently-worded queries were reviewed rather than an exhaustive list.

E07000116.research: NEGATIVE. PRIMARY SOURCE, verbatim: 'HMO licensing - HMOs must be licensed where they are occupied by five persons or more in two or more households. This includes any HMO which is a building or a converted flat where householders share amenities such as a toilet, personal washing facilities or cooking facilities.' And: 'HMO standards - Whether your HMO needs a licence or not, it must meet our HMO standards.' The second sentence expressly contemplates unlicensed HMOs, which is incompatible with an additional licensing designation. FEE TEST PASSED, and this is the strongest single item, same page verbatim: 'Licence fee - We have reviewed our HMO licensing fee structure and made some changes... From 1 April 2026, the fees are as follows: Occupancy / Licence fee - 5-7 occupants £813 - 8 or more occupants £908'. And renewals '5-7 occupants £701 - 8 or more occupants £748'. THE FEE LADDER STARTS AT FIVE OCCUPANTS. There is no band for 3-4 occupants, which an additional scheme would necessarily need, and no per-dwelling selective fee. The structure was reviewed as recently as 1 April 2026, so it is current and not a stale page. RAW-HTML FORENSICS: this page was grepped in raw HTML rather than rendered text; zero hits for 'selective', 'additional licen' and 'designat', and zero base64 blobs (specifically checked for the encoded-in-JavaScript pattern that concealed an answer on Sunderland). STRUCTURAL SWEEPS, used because the site search is unusable: (a) the A-Z index is server-rendered and complete; the only dwelling-licensing entry is 'Licensing of houses in multiple occupation', and there is no 'Selective licensing' or 'Additional licensing' entry. (b) the HTML sitemap is comprehensive with 65 housing links; the control 'multiple occupation' is present exactly once and 'selective' and 'additional licen' zero times. (c) the Have Your Say page contains zero mentions of HMO, multiple occupation, selective or additional licensing, so there is no live consultation. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The civil penalty policy for landlords: 'offences in relation to licensing of houses under Part 3 of the Act (section 95 Housing Act 2004)' appears in the s.249A list of offences for which a penalty MAY be imposed. (2) s.254 definition on the HMO page: 'An HMO is defined as a building... which is let to three or more persons forming two or more households'; the same page sets the licensing threshold at five. (3) 'Planning legislation - Where there are more than six tenants planning permission is required' is planning (sui generis), not licensing. (4) Article 4 Directions: these are PROPERTY-SPECIFIC directions on named premises (7 Vale Avenue, Angel Food and Wine, Apple Pie Farm, Bidborough Stores, Brokes Wood, Brunch Cafe, Cadogan House and others). Not a district-wide HMO C3-to-C4 direction. (5) Caravan site licensing and the fit and proper person register are Caravan Sites Act and Mobile Homes Act 2013 regimes. (6) The 'Tunbridge Wells Landlord Incentive Scheme' is a homelessness-prevention incentive, the 'selective lettings' style trap. LIMITATIONS, STATED PLAINLY: (a) WebFetch is bot-blocked (HTTP 403); worked around with curl plus a browser user-agent, which returned 200, and the 403 was not treated as evidence. www.tunbridgewells.gov.uk redirects to the bare host. (b) The XML sitemap sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial, so the server-rendered HTML sitemap and the A-Z were substituted; both are complete. (c) The site search is a client-side Cludo widget and is UNUSABLE over HTTP; control, real and nonsense queries all returned a byte-identical 50,373-byte shell. Not relied on. (d) THE ONE GENUINE GAP: the ModernGov committee search FAILED its control, returning 'No results found' even for the single word 'licensing', across DocType 0-4. NO INFERENCE SHOULD BE DRAWN FROM TUNBRIDGE WELLS COMMITTEE PAPERS EITHER WAY. The negative rests on the fee-schedule test, the explicit 'whether your HMO needs a licence or not' wording, the complete A-Z and HTML sitemap sweeps, and the absence of any consultation on Have Your Say. A designation consulted on but not yet fee-bearing would not be caught by the fee test alone, which is why Have Your Say was checked separately. (e) WebSearch budget exhausted.

E07000077.research: NEGATIVE. PRIMARY SOURCE describes mandatory licensing only: 'You must have a licence from us if you're renting out a large HMO in the district. Your property is defined as a large HMO if it is a: building let to 5 or more people from 2 or more separate households who share amenities...'. Raw-HTML grep of that page, flattened and case-insensitive: 'selective' 0, 'additional licen' 0, 'article 4' 0, 'designat' 0. FEE TEST PASSED, the full 2026/27 Environmental Health and Private Sector Housing schedule, complete HMO block verbatim: 'HMO licence fee for up to 5 bedrooms * part 1 fee 658.00'; '* part 2 fee 736.00'; 'HMO licence fee for 5 letting rooms or more - charge per additional room 39.00'; 'renewal charge 736.00'; 'incomplete application 39.00'; 'Reminder letter on failure to apply for a licence 39.00'; 'Variation of licence 12.50'; 'Missed appointment 166.00'. Footnote: '* The total cost of licensing an HMO in 2026/27 will be £1,394.00... The licensing period is 5 years from the date the application was made.' The Private Sector Housing section that follows lists only immigration inspections, improvement and prohibition notices and mobile-home fit-and-proper fees. COMMITTEE PAPERS, CLEAN ZERO ON A VALIDATED ENGINE: the ModernGov document search for 'selective licensing' returned 'No results found for your query selective licensing.' Controls both ways: 'houses in multiple occupation' returned results; 'additional licensing' returned 10+ results, all false positives (Manual Enhanced DBS certificates, Hackney Carriage policy); nonsense 'zzqqnonsense999' returned 'No results found'. Engine proven working in both directions, so the nil is evidential. FRESHEST POLICY: Cabinet 14 April 2026, item CAB103, adopted the new Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy 2026 'and mandatory HMO licensing conditions to take effect from 1st May 2026'. Appendix 2 is headed 'Standard conditions: HMO licences granted under Part 2 of the Housing Act 2004' with zero mentions of selective licensing, additional licensing or s.56 Housing Act 2004 anywhere in it. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Civil-penalty boilerplate, and this council's policy literally contains it: para 11.2, 'The Council has the power to impose a Civil Financial Penalty for the following: ... Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]', in a list alongside s30, s72, s139, s234 and banning orders. The single most likely source of a false positive here. (2) A NEW AND EASILY-MISSED TRAP: 'section 56' appears three times in that same policy but is SECTION 56 OF THE RENTERS' RIGHTS ACT 2025 (marketing a letting without stating the proposed rent, and rent bidding), NOT s.56 of the Housing Act 2004. (3) 'charge per additional room £39.00' is a per-room surcharge. (4) Article 4 directions: Uttlesford has them, but they are site-specific land directions ('land at Friars Lane Hatfield Heath', 'land at Attridges Farm High Roding'). The Article 4 hub has zero mentions of HMO, C4 or houses in multiple occupation. (5) s.254 definition versus the stated threshold of five. (6) 'Essex amenity standards for HMOs' are shared county standards applied to mandatory licences, not a joint designation. (7) 'HENHAM NP AREA DESIGNATION' is a neighbourhood plan area designation under the Localism Act. LIMITATIONS: (a) Uttlesford's www host intermittently 403s, exactly the pattern to watch for: /landlords and the Article 4 page returned 403 on www while the BARE uttlesford.gov.uk host returned 200, and one search request hit a transient WAF 403 that succeeded on retry. All were bot blocks and none was treated as evidence. (b) Uttlesford's own site search is an OR-matching engine; 'selective licensing' returns 141 hits purely by matching 'licensing'. It DID pass the negative control, so it works, but it has no phrase precision; ModernGov was the precise instrument. Note also that /search?query= 404s; the correct endpoint is /article/4829/Site-search?q=. (c) Uttlesford publishes no historical 'we never had one' statement; the no-expired-scheme conclusion rests on the ModernGov archive returning zero relevant designations at any date, and any pre-2008 designation would have expired by statute long ago. (d) WebSearch budget exhausted. (e) No live consultation on either scheme type was found.

W06000014.research: THIS RECORD IS DELIBERATELY MARKED UNVERIFIED BECAUSE TWO CURRENT COUNCIL-CONTROLLED SOURCES DIRECTLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER on the one question that matters: whether a landlord with a sub-mandatory HMO in central Barry needs a licence today. Getting this wrong in the permissive direction risks an unlimited fine and a rent repayment order, so no confident answer has been forced, and no scheme object is recorded in either direction. WHAT IS SOLID. (a) NO SELECTIVE LICENSING, stated expressly by the council's own regulatory service in both languages, confirmed by raw-HTML grep: the SRS HMO page states 'There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' The Welsh version states 'Ar hyn o bryd, nid oes ardaloedd lle ceir trwyddedu dewisol.' The SRS Business Plan 2026-27 contains zero occurrences of 'selective'. This negative is firm. (b) The Vale delegates HMO licensing to SHARED REGULATORY SERVICES, its statutory joint regulatory body with Cardiff and Bridgend, which is why no HMO page exists on valeofglamorgan.gov.uk itself. A sweep of all 11,591 URLs in the council's own sitemap returns zero hits for 'hmo', 'multiple-occup', 'selectiv', 'dewisol' or 'ychwanegol' outside three old Rent Smart Wales news items. THE CONFLICT, VERIFIED AT RAW-HTML LEVEL. Inside a collapsed accordion on the generic SRS HMO page, visible only on grepping the raw HTML and not the rendered text, the council states: 'If you own or manage a HMO of any type or size in the Cathays or Plasnewydd area of Cardiff which is not subject to mandatory licensing, you will need to apply for an Additional HMO Licence. Similarly, if you own or manage a HMO which isn't subject to mandatory licensing in the Castleland Renewal Area in Vale of Glamorgan, you will need to apply for an Additional Licence.' The Welsh page repeats it. That is a live instruction to landlords, in the present tense, on a council-controlled site. The scheme was genuine historically: the council consulted on a 'Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMO) Additional Licensing Scheme' for the Castleland Renewal Area with the consultation running until 14 March 2012, and its own HMO Licensing page in January 2016 listed 'Additional Licensing - As in the Castleland Ward' alongside an 'HMO Licensing Enforcement Plan 2012-2017'. FOUR CURRENT PRIMARY SOURCES POINT THE OTHER WAY. (1) REGISTER TEST: the live public register (dated in-sheet 05/01/2026) has a single worksheet literally named 'Public Sheet - Mandatory' holding ten properties, every one 3-4 storeys with 5-9 occupiers. There is no 'Additional' sheet and not one sub-mandatory licence, including at Holton Road, Vere Street and Harvey Street addresses that sit inside the Castleland area. (2) FEE TEST: the Vale-specific SRS page returns ZERO raw-HTML occurrences of 'castleland', 'additional' and 'selectiv', and lists only 'The HMO licensing scheme is to be self-funding and the following fees will apply: Mandatory HMO Licence: £792; Mandatory HMO Licence (Renewal): £657.' No additional-licence fee and no additional application route. By contrast the sibling Cardiff page on the SAME site sets out its schemes, dates, public notices and a graduated additional-licensing fee ladder, proving the site does distinguish scheme types, so the absence on the Vale page is meaningful. (3) SRS Joint Committee 'Fees and Charges', 17 December 2025, lists for the Vale only the two mandatory fees. (4) SRS Business Plan 2026-27 and Annual Report 2025-26 mention additional licensing ONLY as 'Additional HMO Licensing at Cathays and Plasnewydd' and 'Redeclare the Plasnewydd Additional Licensing Scheme in Cardiff'; 'Castleland' appears ZERO times in either. Underpinning this, the council's own archived page for the renewal area says 'The Area was declared in April 2010... The Renewal Area has a twelve-year lifetime', so the underlying renewal designation lapsed around April 2022, and a s.56 designation cannot in any event exceed five years. WHY THIS IS UNVERIFIED RATHER THAN A NEGATIVE: the weight of current evidence (register composition, fee schedules, committee reports, service plans) says the scheme is not operating, and the SRS page is demonstrably stale elsewhere, since it still presents Cardiff's Plasnewydd scheme as running from 1 January 2021 for five years when that ended on 31 December 2025 and the business plan schedules its redeclaration. But a council page telling landlords they need a licence is not something to overrule silently in a product carrying this risk. The public note therefore leads with the conflict and directs the user to confirm with the council. DATES NOT ESTABLISHED: no designation or revocation dates could be found from any primary source. Vale committee minutes are online only from 2019, no 2012 cabinet report is archived, and the 'Additional Licensing' sub-page of the old council site was never captured by the Wayback Machine. WARDS: the Castleland Renewal Area is STREET-DEFINED, and the Vale had major ward boundary changes at the May 2022 elections, so the 2016 page's phrase 'Castleland Ward' is both imprecise and probably stale. NO WARD LIST HAS BEEN SYNTHESISED. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) CARDIFF'S CATHAYS AND PLASNEWYDD SCHEMES, the single biggest attribution risk here because they are described on the very same shared SRS website the Vale uses; they belong to CARDIFF Council. (2) RENT SMART WALES. (3) STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL: 'Where an area of Additional Licensing is designated, the Council can decide on which type of HMO is covered by the scheme' describes the power, not its exercise. LIMITATIONS: the Vale's own site search FAILED its control test, requiring a POSTed viewstate, with every GET including the control query returning 'No results found', so no nil result from it is evidential. Substantial evidence here sits on srs.wales rather than a .gov.uk domain; srs.wales is the Vale's own delegated statutory regulatory service, linked from the council's apply-online page, and its fee and business-plan reports are published on valeofglamorgan.gov.uk, so it was judged authoritative, but this is a departure from a strict .gov.uk-only rule and is flagged. RECOMMENDATION: this record should be resolved by a direct written enquiry to Shared Regulatory Services rather than by further desk research, because the published record is internally inconsistent.

E07000180.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE AND VERY RECENT. PRIMARY SOURCE (also served by /hmo, which 301s to it), verbatim: 'The council is not currently operating any additional or selective HMO licensing schemes.' The page carries dateModified 2026-07-23T15:19:05+00:00, thirteen days before verification. This was independently re-fetched and the string confirmed in raw HTML. The page is Vale-specific, not shared boilerplate: 'In Vale of White Horse, a house in multiple occupation (HMO) must have a licence if: It is occupied by five or more people; and Those people form two or more households; and The HMO is not a purpose-built, self-contained flat situated in a block comprising three or more self-contained flats.' FEE TEST PASSED, verbatim table (Bedrooms / Part one fee / Part two fee / Total): 'up to 5 £620 £414 £1,034; 6 £644 £429 £1,073; 7 £667 £445 £1,112; 8 £691 £460 £1,151; 9 £714 £476 £1,190; 10 £737 £492 £1,229'. Footnote: 'All fees are set locally by the council, reviewed annually and cover the five year licence period.' Also 'Additional HMO advice visits are charged at £196.' The ladder starts at 'up to 5' bedrooms; there is no selective fee, no additional HMO fee and no second application route. JOINT POLICY, WITH THE SHARED-SERVICE CAVEAT HANDLED: the South and Vale Housing Enforcement Policy, April 2024, states 'The councils operate a mandatory HMO licensing scheme as specified by Part 2 of The Housing Act 2004.' Across the full 47-page extracted text (126,892 characters) 'selective' appears 0 times and 'additional licen' 0 times; extraction was validated (100 hits on 'licen', HMO licensing chapter present). CAVEAT RECORDED: this document covers BOTH South Oxfordshire DC and Vale and is hosted on southandvale.gov.uk. It is linked from Vale's own enforcement policy page so it does apply, but the Vale-specific negative does NOT rest on it; the whitehorsedc.gov.uk statement above is Vale-branded and more recent. SITEMAP SWEEP, substituting for the broken site search: sitemap.xml resolves to post-sitemap plus page-sitemap plus page-sitemap2, totalling 2,017 URLs. Exactly one HMO licensing page exists and zero URLs contain 'selective' or 'additional'. COMMITTEE PAPERS: the ModernGov search for 'selective licensing' returned 7 results, ALL false positives dated 2008-2012 (Scheme of Delegation, Constitution Review, Council and Audit and Governance papers), all OR-matches on 'licensing' inside constitutional documents. Controls validated: control returned 10+ results; nonsense returned 'No results found for your query zzqqnonsense999.' TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'Additional HMO advice visits are charged at £196' is an advice-visit charge on the mandatory regime. (2) Part 3 and s.95 statutory recitals in the joint enforcement policy, and 'not a fit and proper person to hold a licence under Part 2 or 3 of the Housing Act 2004' in the banning-order section. (3) 'Additional enforcement options for HMOs', a heading referring to overcrowding notices under s.139, not s.56. (4) The bedroom bands to 10 are a mandatory licence fee scaled by room count, not a lower-threshold scheme. (5) 'three or more self-contained flats' is part of the s.257 purpose-built-flat EXCLUSION test, not a three-person additional scheme. (6) 'For HMOs housing over 6 occupants you must also ensure you have planning permission' is planning; no HMO Article 4 direction was found anywhere in the 2,017-URL sweep. (7) 'White Horse Lettings' and 'Homes for Ukraine landlords' are not Part 3. LIMITATIONS: (a) Vale's own site search is BROKEN and was not relied on; ?s= returns near-identical server HTML for every query (12,502 / 12,516 / 12,500 bytes for 'selective licensing' / the control / nonsense), the only occurrences of query terms being the JSON-LD title echoing the query back. (b) WebSearch budget exhausted. (c) No live consultation on either scheme type was found. (d) Any pre-2008 designation would have expired by statute long before today.

E08000036.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE. Flagged as a metropolitan borough with a plausible ward-based designation; cleared on primary committee evidence, independently retrieved and read in full. THE COUNCIL'S OWN WORDS: scrutiny report to the Regeneration, Employment and Skills Overview and Scrutiny Committee, 24 November 2021 ('WARDS AFFECTED: ALL'), para 5.3: 'Properties rented out in England are not currently registered or licensed and landlords do not need to declare that they own or manage property, unless they have a house in multiple occupation with 5 or more occupants or there is an additional or selective licensing scheme in place in their local arear. There is currently no selective licensing scheme in the Wakefield District.' FORMALLY REJECTED: the minutes record 'Resolved - (1) Based on the information received and after careful consideration the Committee feels that on balance both a district wide and/or selective licensing would not be the best strategy for Wakefield to manage the private rented sector at the present time. (2) The Committee supports the view that there are less expensive and better focused ways of tackling any private rented sector issues. However, the Committee believes that selective licensing is something that should be kept under review should the circumstances change.' The briefing was explicit that this was Part 3, and officers stated Wakefield fails the entry tests: 'Wakefield does not have low demand, indeed the private rented sector was strong and properties were at a premium.' An indicative fee of 'around £750-£1000 for each privately rented property' was discussed but never adopted. FEE TEST PASSED, the only property licensing fee table on the entire site, verbatim (Property Size / Standard fee / Responsible Landlords Scheme members): '5 bedrooms £847 £677; 6 to 10 bedrooms £1,031 £824; Above 10 (per unit) £1,031 plus extra £40 per bed space over ten units, £824 plus extra £32'. The schedule STARTS AT 5 BEDROOMS. There is no fee line for a non-HMO dwelling and none for a 3-4 occupant HMO, the two things selective and additional schemes must charge for. CONTROLS: site search validated both ways; the control returned relevant hits and the nonsense query returned the explicit string 'Your search for zzqxwvnonsense12345 returned no results', with all four responses byte-distinct. Searches for 'selective licensing', 'additional licensing', 'property licensing', 'licensing designation' and 'private rented sector licensing' returned only alcohol, animal, taxi, streetworks and adult-education results. SITEMAP GOTCHA RECORDED: /sitemap.xml 404s while the bare /sitemap returns 200 with 1,844 URLs. The full housing branch (63 URLs) contains no licensing page beyond the mandatory HMO one. ModernGov validated both ways; democracy.wakefield.gov.uk does not resolve. 'selective licensing designation' returns only 3 results across the entire committee archive back to 2003, the sole relevant one being the November 2021 minutes; the remaining hits are Internal Audit Plans from 2004 to 2014 matching the audit phrase 'selective areas of activity'. Every 'additional licensing' hit is a Licensing Committee minute. EXPIRED SCHEMES: none found. The 2021 report's 'there is currently no selective licensing scheme' is written as a settled baseline, not as a lapse. Of the areas commonly rumoured, Airedale, Hemsworth, South Elmsall, Eastmoor, Lupset, Portobello, Castleford, Knottingley and Featherstone, none returned any licensing designation on either search engine. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION FOR SMALLER HMOs, the critical trap here. Made 23 October 2024, confirmed by Cabinet 15 April 2025, sealed 9 May 2025, in force 24 October 2025. It removes permitted development rights for 3-6 occupant HMOs in six areas: Castleford Centre North, Castleford Smawthorne, Wakefield Agbrigg, Wakefield College Grove, Wakefield Lincoln Street and Wakefield Peterson Road. This is PLANNING PERMISSION, NOT LICENSING. THESE ARE NAMED AREAS DEFINED BY MAPPED BOUNDARIES, NOT WARDS, and must not be converted to a ward list. (2) The news article 'Stricter HMO rules come into force' (24 October 2025) reads as licensing at a glance but is that Article 4 Direction and says so. (3) Conservation-area Article 4 directions at Heath, St Johns, Whitwood Terrace and 28 Blenheim Road. (4) Civil-penalty boilerplate in the 2017 Cabinet report. (5) The 2021 report's own statutory recital immediately followed by the denial. (6) The per-bed-space surcharge. (7) s.254 definition versus the threshold of five. (8) The Wakefield Responsible Landlords Scheme, voluntary accreditation giving about a 20% fee discount. (9) The Private Sector Leasing Scheme and the letting-agent Redress scheme. (10) 'Better Homes Agbrigg' (began February 2023; predecessors College Grove and Primrose Hill) is area-based PROACTIVE ENFORCEMENT, easily mistaken for a designation because it is area-targeted and overlaps two Article 4 areas, but it explicitly says 'If your property is a HMO, occupied by 5 or more people... you must hold a relevant HMO licence.' (11) 'Walton Public Notice Designation' and 'Crofton Public Notice Designation' are Neighbourhood Area designations under the Localism Act. (12) 'Additional Learning Support'. (13) NEIGHBOUR BLEED CONTROLLED: the 2021 minutes discuss LEEDS (its scheme, £300k preparation cost) and Enfield (the 2014 High Court quashing), and the 2017 report benchmarks Bradford, Calderdale, Kirklees and Leeds HMO fees. All are other authorities' schemes cited as comparators. LIMITATIONS: WebSearch budget exhausted. wakefield.gov.uk without www does not resolve (connection failure, not a block). RE-CHECK WORTH SCHEDULING: the 2021 resolution keeps selective licensing 'under review', and a refreshed Housing Plan to 2030 was out for consultation in summer 2026.

E06000007.research: NEGATIVE, DECLARATIVE, TWICE OVER. Flagged as a unitary with central wards where a designation was plausible; cleared. EXPLICIT COUNCIL STATEMENT: the council's 'HMO licensing - further information' PDF lists all three Housing Act 2004 licensing types under headings '2. Additional Licensing' and '3. Selective Licensing of other residential accommodation', then states verbatim: 'Warrington Borough Council has no plans to introduce Additional or Selective Licensing anywhere within the Borough.' SECOND, CURRENT GUIDANCE (HMO Guidance May 2024): 'If you operate a HMO with 5 or more people living in it, who live together as 2 or more households then it must be licensed... There is another type of licensing known as Selective Licensing but this is not carried out in this authority at present.' FEE TEST PASSED, the complete Housing standards section of 'Fees and Charges 2026-2027' (page updated 7 April 2026): 'House in multiple occupation (HMO) / Fee (exc VAT): New licence £492.09; Licence with CLAS membership (10% reduction) £442.87; Licence for charitable organisation (50% reduction) £246.04; Licence variation £47.44'. Followed only by Immigration inspection, 'Notices - Housing act 2004 £382.86' and Caravan sites. Independent raw-HTML greps of four housing pages returned ZERO occurrences of 'selective licensing' or 'additional licensing'. ADDITIONAL LICENSING EXPRESSLY REJECTED AT CABINET, 8 September 2025, Agenda Item 8, para 6.18: 'It is not considered at present that the designation of discretionary additional licensing areas within the central area could be justified, because currently there is little evidence that the Borough's HMOs are consistently badly managed.' Para 5.1 confirms the threshold: 'There are currently 211 licensed Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) in Warrington. Any HMOs operating without a licence (i.e operating with fewer than five residents) are not reflected.' Cabinet's recommendation was an Article 4 Direction only. The Housing Policy Committee (30 July 2025) had offered additional licensing as an optional extra at para 12.3, but its formal recommendations were Article 4 plus SPD only, and Cabinet did not take the licensing option. HISTORIC CONSIDERATION, NO DESIGNATION EVER MADE: CMIS returned 23 documents for 'selective licensing', spanning 25 June 2013 to 4 March 2015 ONLY, nothing later. Building Stronger Communities Policy Committee, 9 July 2014 minutes: 'The findings of the group were that there was not a case currently for selective licensing in Warrington but the item could be revisited when Government Guidelines became available.' Work programme monitoring through March 2015 repeats: 'there was not a satisfactory case for selective licensing in Warrington at the present time'. No designation was ever made, so there is no start or end date to report. SITEMAP SWEEP: all 1,439 URLs independently retrieved and grepped; no housing-related licensing URL beyond the HMO page, and no URL containing 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION, the critical one, and it is brand new: 'On 13 May 2026 Warrington Borough Council... confirmed a without immediate effect Article 4 Direction, under Article 4(1) of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015... applies to the Central Six Wards of the Borough consisting of Orford, Poplars and Hulme, Fairfield and Howley, Latchford East, Latchford West, and Bewsey and Whitecross, and will come into force on 25 September 2026.' Cabinet then approved a BOROUGH-WIDE extension on 9 June 2026 alongside a new HMO Supplementary Planning Document. This is PLANNING CONTROL, NOT LICENSING. (2) The HMO Supplementary Planning Document. (3) Cheshire Landlord Accreditation Scheme (CLAS) 10% fee discount, voluntary accreditation. (4) 'The council may also apply additional conditions to the license', licence conditions not s.56. (5) s.254 definition versus the threshold of five. (6) Application form boilerplate 'Whether this application for an HMO licence under Part 2 or for a house licence under Part 3 of the Housing Act 2004', national model-form wording. (7) The Private Rented Sector Access Scheme, homelessness and tenancy access. (8) Caravan site licence fees and the £382.86 enforcement notice charge. (9) NEIGHBOUR BLEED: Liverpool and Halton excluded. COMMERCIAL WARNING WORTH SURFACING: several non-council aggregators currently assert Warrington operates selective licensing in 'Latchford, Fairfield and Howley, and Bewsey and Whitecross'. That is EXACTLY the Article 4 ward list. Competitors have mistaken the planning direction for a licensing scheme and are publishing a wrong answer; none was relied on here. WARD BOUNDARY POSITION: Warrington did NOT have new wards at the 2024 elections. The LGBCE electoral review is live now, with final recommendations December 2026 and 'electoral arrangements to be implemented for the May 2028 local elections'. The six Article 4 ward names above are therefore current and stable until May 2028. LIMITATIONS: (a) The council's own website search is BROKEN and proves nothing either way; the control returned '4041 results found' and the nonsense negative control returned the IDENTICAL 4041 results, i.e. it returns the whole index regardless of query. A full sitemap sweep was used instead. (b) CMIS search was validated with controls and is sound. (c) CMIS full-text indexing appears thinner before 2013, so a pre-2013 designation cannot be excluded from CMIS alone, but the 2013-2015 papers uniformly frame the question as whether to INTRODUCE a scheme, the council's own PDF says it has 'no plans to introduce' one, and any such designation could not be live now given the five-year statutory maximum. (d) warrington.moderngov.co.uk returns Cloudflare 522 and democracy.warrington.gov.uk does not resolve; the live committee system is cmis.warrington.gov.uk. (e) WebSearch budget exhausted. E07000103.research: PRIMARY: the 'Licensable HMOs' page (also served at /hmolicensing) states verbatim: 'Houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) require a licence if they are occupied by: five or more people from two or more households... A licence lasts up to five years.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, mandatory-only: a single fee ladder with no occupancy or area banding and no separate cost-recovery route: 'New Application Fee - £1,557.70 / New Application Fee Registered Charities - £1,236.90 / Renewal Fee - £1,295.90 / Renewal Fee Registered Charities - £1,033 / Assisted HMO licence application - £362.30 / Fast track licence application - £403.70.' There is no selective-licensing fee line and no second application route. SCOPE TEST: the council's Licensing index lists its full licence catalogue, 'Taxi and private hire, Entertainment and alcohol, Gambling, Landlord licences, Piercing and cosmetic procedure, Animal, Special event', and the 'Landlord licences' entry links to the HMO page, i.e. mandatory HMO licensing is the ONLY property licence Watford issues. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 (56,696 bytes) and was fully enumerated; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the only 'additional' hit is a food-waste news article, excluded. All five HMO sub-pages and the standards-in-rented-properties page were fetched and grepped in RAW HTML for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen': zero hits. TRAPS EXCLUDED: no Article 4 direction was mistaken for licensing; the Renters' Rights Act 2025 download was not read as Housing Act 2004 s.56 (the RRA s.56 rent-bidding trap); the s.254 three-person definition was not treated as a licensing threshold. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Three Rivers was carried across; only watford.gov.uk pages were used. E07000216.research: STRONGEST EVIDENCE IN THE BATCH, an explicit and unusually complete council denial, confirmed in RAW HTML rather than rendered text: 'Waverley operates a mandatory HMO licensing scheme that covers the entire Borough, no other licensing schemes are in operation or are being proposed. There are no Article 4 HMO Direction and Short-Term Let Schemes or Restrictions in force and under consideration.' That single sentence rules out BOTH Part 3 selective licensing and Part 2 s.56 additional licensing, disposes of any 'proposed' status, and pre-emptively rules out the Article 4 trap that has caught eight of the last twelve councils. THRESHOLD: 'you rent your property to five or more people who form more than one household [and] tenants share toilet, bathroom or kitchen facilities.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: fees are held as HTML entities, so the raw-HTML grep was rerun for the pound entity; the complete set recovered is £807.70 (new applications, per property), £710.50 (renewal after five years), £30.60 (surcharge for 11-15 units), £12.20 (per unit above 15), £25 (approved landlords association discount) and £100 (late application fee). The ladder starts at five occupants and every extra charge is a per-unit surcharge on a mandatory licence. The £30.60 and £12.20 lines were correctly excluded as the 'additional fee / per unit' trap rather than read as additional licensing. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 (185,936 bytes) and was fully enumerated; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the single 'Additional' hit is a planning application title ('Amended Additional Information'), excluded. A raw-HTML grep of the 156,932-byte HMO page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits beyond the denial quoted above.

E07000065.research: EXPLICIT DENIAL found by RAW-HTML grep, under its own h2 heading on the council's HMO page: 'Selective Licensing - Wealden District Council does not currently operate a selective licensing scheme and has no plans to do so.' A direct primary-source negative for Part 3 that also disposes of any 'proposed' status. ADDITIONAL LICENSING: no s.56 scheme. The page's licensing trigger is 'Which HMOs must be licensed? It is now compulsory from the 1st October 2018 to licence all HMOs that: Have five or more people from two or more households (i.e. people not related, living together as a couple, etc); and Share amenities', the 2018 mandatory extension, and the page elsewhere describes 'the revised mandatory scheme'. A raw-HTML grep for 'additional licen' returned zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: 'Initial Fee For a standard 5 person shared house - £808 / 6 persons - £823 / 7 persons - £839 / 8 persons - £855 / 9 persons - £870 (each person thereafter incurs an additional cost of £16)'. The shared-house ladder STARTS AT FIVE OCCUPANTS, the strong mandatory-only signal. A second band exists for bedsit-type HMOs ('2 individual bedsit units - £933... 6 units - £1184, each unit thereafter £63'); this starts at two UNITS, not two occupants, and was checked not to imply additional licensing: it is a fee band for converted and bedsit HMOs that must still cross the stated five-person occupancy trigger to be licensable. The £16 and £63 lines were excluded as the per-additional-unit surcharge trap. SITEMAP: /sitemap.xml 301s, but /wp-sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 and its posts-page sub-file (193,267 bytes) was fully enumerated; zero 'selectiv' URLs. The mandatory-conditions boilerplate on the page ('There are mandatory conditions which require the licence holder to: Produce an annual gas safety certificate...') was correctly read as licence conditions, not as evidence of a discretionary scheme.

E07000241.research: PRIMARY PAGE: 'Apply for a House of Multiple Occupation Licence' states 'If you are renting out a House of Multiple Occupation (HMO) which has five or more unrelated people occupying it you will need to apply for a licence.' All five sub-pages and the landlords hub were fetched and grepped in RAW HTML for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen': zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, AND THIS IS THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE. The web page defers fees to a document, so the council's 31-page General Fund Fees and Charges 2026-27 PDF (11.2MB) was downloaded and its full text extracted. The HMO section reads: 'HMO Application - Application for basic 5 person HMO* / Application for an HMO between 6 - 10 persons* / Application for an HMO with 11 or more persons* / *10% discount on HMO fee for member of PAL scheme', with amounts £1,290.00 / £1,443.00 / £1,589.00 rising to £1,339.00 / £1,498.00 / £1,650.00 for 2026-27. The ladder STARTS AT FIVE PERSONS, and critically, a full-text search of the entire 31-page statutory fee schedule for 'selective licen', 'additional licen', 'part 3' and 'section 56' produced NO cost-recovery line for any discretionary scheme. A live scheme must be self-financing, so its absence from the council's own statutory fee schedule is close to conclusive. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the one 'additional' hit in the PDF ('Combination of activities equal to highest fee plus 50% of each additional licensable activity') is Licensing Act 2003 alcohol and entertainment boilerplate, not s.56. The Renters' Rights Act pages were checked and not confused with Housing Act 2004 s.56. The 'PAL scheme' discount is voluntary landlord accreditation, excluded. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (24,441 bytes), fully enumerated, zero 'selectiv' URLs; the 'additional' hits are a benefits page and two local-plan documents, excluded.

E06000037.research: DELEGATION NOTE, IMPORTANT FOR SOURCING: West Berkshire delivers its housing regulation through the Public Protection Partnership (PPP), its statutory shared regulatory service with Bracknell Forest. Both council URLs 301-redirect there, verified with curl -I: /houses-multiple-occupation redirects to publicprotectionpartnership.org.uk/houses-in-multiple-occupation-hmo, and /article/40653/Rented-housing-standards-and-licensing redirects to publicprotectionpartnership.org.uk/housing. PPP is therefore the council's own service under delegation, not a third-party aggregator; the westberks.gov.uk URL is cited because the redirect makes it authoritative, and no landlord blog, letting agent or aggregator was relied on. PRIMARY TEXT, recovered by grepping the RAW HTML because the content sits below a large navigation block and is easy to miss in rendered text: 'What is a licensable HMO? The licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Description) (England) Order 2018, came into effect on 1 October 2018 which extends the current mandatory licensing scheme across England. Mandatory licensing applies to HMOs that are occupied by five or more occupants which form two households or more and meeting the "standard tests" (Section 254(2)...).' The scheme is described purely as mandatory. A raw-HTML grep of the page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. TRAP EXCLUDED: the page cites s.254(2), which is the DEFINITION of an HMO and not a licensing threshold, and was not read as evidence of a three-person discretionary scheme. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (60,490 bytes), fully enumerated; only two housing-licensing URLs exist in the entire sitemap, both redirecting to PPP as above, and zero URLs contain 'selectiv'. LIMITATION: WebFetch on the PPP host returned HTTP 403; this was worked around with curl using a browser user-agent plus Accept, Accept-Language, Referer and --compressed, which returned HTTP 200, so the 403 was a bot block and not evidence. PPP's HMO fee lines could not be extracted because they sit on a separate fees-and-charges route, so THE FEE-SCHEDULE TEST IS UNAPPLIED HERE; the negative rests on the explicit 'mandatory licensing' wording plus the sitemap sweep. This is the weakest-sourced record in the batch.

E07000047.research: PRIMARY: the dedicated 'HMO licensing' page states 'HMOs must be licensed by the council if the property is let to five or more people who form two or more households', repeated verbatim as the summary on the parent HMO page. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: 'The HMO Licence fee is £446.40. The licence needs to be renewed every five years. The Fit and Proper fee is £144.00.' A SINGLE flat licence fee with no banding, no area-specific route and no second application form; there is no separate cost-recovery fee for any discretionary scheme, which a live scheme would be legally required to carry. The only application routes offered are the West Devon HMO application and renewal forms, both emailed to the shared South West Devon licensing address; no selective or additional route exists. A raw-HTML grep of both HMO pages for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml HTTP 200 (36,518 bytes), fully enumerated; the complete HMO tree (about-hmos, hmo-fact-sheet and its appeals, exemptions, fit-and-proper-person, HHSRS and management-orders sub-pages) is present and contains no selective or additional licensing page; zero URLs contain 'selectiv'; the two 'additional' hits are a land-charges searches page and a tree-works page, both excluded. SeaMoor Lettings is the council's own lettings agency, a landlord and tenant matching service, and was correctly NOT read as a 'selective lettings' or property-licensing scheme. LIMITATION: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on this host; retrying with curl plus a browser user-agent and full headers returned HTTP 200, so the 403 was a bot block, not evidence. S12000039.research: RESOLVED BY STATUTE, NOT BY PER-COUNCIL RESEARCH, and that distinction matters. Selective licensing (Housing Act 2004 Part 3) and additional HMO licensing (Part 2 s.56) exist only where that Act applies. Section 270(11) provides that "this Act extends to England and Wales only" (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2004/34/section/270). West Dunbartonshire therefore has no legal power to designate either scheme, so this is a definite answer rather than an absence of evidence, and it cannot change without primary legislation at Westminster. Scottish councils have NO power to designate selective or additional licensing areas. The Housing Act 2004 extends to England and Wales only (s.270(11)). Landlord registration and HMO licensing apply nationally instead. WHAT DOES APPLY INSTEAD. (1) LANDLORD REGISTRATION under the Antisocial Behaviour etc. (Scotland) Act 2004 Part 8: all landlords must register with each council where they let (exemptions: resident landlords, holiday lets, agricultural tenancies); joint owners must all register; adverts must show the registration number. Registration lasts 3 years and costs about £85 per council plus £20 per property (no per-property fee where the property is a licensed HMO), with a £170 late fee and a maximum penalty of £50,000. (2) HMO LICENSING under the Housing (Scotland) Act 2006 Part 5 s.125: 3+ persons who are not all members of the same family or of one or other of two families (i.e. 3+ households), sharing a basic amenity, as only or main residence. Licences typically run 3 years, the fee is set by each council, and the maximum penalty is £50,000. NOTE THE THRESHOLD DIFFERENCE: Scotland's HMO test is THREE or more people from three or more households, which is broader than England's mandatory five. TRAP EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: Enhanced Enforcement Areas (Housing (Scotland) Act 2014 ss.27-28) are area-designated but are NOT a licence; they grant extra discretionary enforcement powers only. Enhanced Enforcement Areas are the single most likely thing to be mistaken for selective licensing in Scotland, because they are area-designated and housing-related, but they confer no licence requirement on any landlord.

E07000127.research: CHECKED WITH EXTRA CARE given Skelmersdale's large private rented sector. PRIMARY: the 'Houses in multiple occupation' page, footer-stamped 'Last Updated | Thursday, May 7, 2026 | 4:40 PM' and therefore current, states: 'Does a HMO have to be licensed? A HMO must be licensed if the property is occupied by five or more people forming two or more households. For example, a property being rented by 5 single people who are not related to each other will need a licence.' The only application route offered is the national portal: 'You can apply for a new HMO licence or renew an existing licence online through the gov.uk portal.' No area-specific or street-specific route exists anywhere on the site. SITE SEARCH, CONTROLS RUN AND PASSED, so a nil result here genuinely means something. The search endpoint was found by reading the homepage form (action=/searchresults.aspx, name='search'; note /search-results.aspx 404s and several parameter names silently return an empty shell). POSITIVE CONTROL 'council tax' returned '1283 results'. NEGATIVE CONTROL 'zzqxwvplopfoo' returned zero results with a distinct 13,093-byte response. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the page opens with the s.254 definition ('At least 3 tenants live there forming more than one household'), which defines an HMO and is NOT a licensing threshold; the threshold is separately and explicitly stated as five. The Mandatory Conditions of Licences Regulations 2018 discussion is licence conditions, not a scheme. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing was carried over from Liverpool, Sefton or Blackpool.
