E07000181.research: PRIMARY: the 'Houses in multiple occupation' page requires a licence where a property is 'occupied by five or more people, forming two or more households' and where 'tenants share facilities such as kitchen or bathrooms'; licences are 'valid for five years'. A raw-HTML grep for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED: a two-part fee, 'Application Fee (Part 1) £242.00' plus 'New Licence Issue Fee (Part 2) £1,097.00', with an 'Additional room fee (7+ rooms) £41.00 per room'; renewals £242.00 plus £994.00 with a 7+ rooms surcharge of £21.00 per room capped at £200.00. One scheme, one route, no discretionary cost-recovery line. The 'additional room fee' was correctly excluded as the per-room surcharge trap. SITE SEARCH, CONTROLS RUN AND PASSED. The endpoint was found from the homepage form (action=/Search/, name='query'). POSITIVE CONTROL 'council tax' returned '342 results'. NEGATIVE CONTROL 'zzqxwvplopfoo' returned 'No results' with a distinct 4,402-byte response, so the engine can return zero and a nil result is meaningful. 'selective licensing' returned 59 results, but these were READ rather than trusted: every result is an OR-match on 'licensing' alone (business-and-licensing, alcohol-and-entertainment, club premises certificates, personal licence, premises licence, animal, primate and zoo licences, plus unrelated corporate pages). Quoting the phrase returned the identical 59, confirming the engine ignores phrase operators and does OR matching, so the count is noise rather than a positive. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml 404s but the bare /sitemap returns HTTP 200 (21,512 bytes), the fallback that has worked for Wakefield, Torbay, Rushmoor and Teignbridge, and was fully enumerated; zero 'selectiv' URLs; the whole private-housing tree is present with no selective or additional page. TRAPS EXCLUDED, ONE NOTABLE: the sitemap contains an ARTICLE 4 DIRECTION at /planning-and-building/article-4-directions/article-4/multiple-sites-2016/, the commonest error in this dataset. It is planning control over C3-to-C4 conversion, creates no licence requirement, and was excluded. Also excluded: the civil-penalties-and-charges page, which is the boilerplate that routinely cites 'Offences in relation to the Selective Licensing of houses [s95 Housing Act 2004]' without any scheme existing.

E06000064.research: CHECKED WITH EXTRA CARE. This is a 2023 unitary formed from Barrow-in-Furness, Eden and South Lakeland, so a pre-vesting-day district designation could still have been running to about 2028. The retired predecessor domains were swept as was done for Somerset, and nothing was found. CURRENT COUNCIL, PRIMARY: 'If your HMO is rented to five or more people, forming at least two households, it needs a licence. Each licensable HMO will need its own licence.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST PASSED, verified in RAW HTML: 'A license fee currently costs £700 for a 5-bedroom property, £20 per room thereafter for both new licenses and renewals. A HMO licence can last for up to five years.' The ladder STARTS AT FIVE BEDROOMS, the strong mandatory-only signal, and the '£20 per room thereafter' line was excluded as the per-room surcharge trap. Raw-HTML greps of the HMO licence page, the HMO standards page, the housing-standards index and the advice-for-landlords page for 'selectiv' and 'additional licen' returned zero hits. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is a Drupal index; both sub-files were fetched (447,280 and 282,180 bytes) and fully enumerated. Zero URLs contain 'selectiv'. The complete housing-standards tree is visible and contains only advice-about-empty-properties, advice-landlords, advice-property-managers-and-letting-agents, advice-tenants, damp-mould-and-cold, houses-multiple-occupation-hmos, how-we-assess-property, immigration-inspection, renters-rights-act-2025 and report-empty-property; no licensing designation page. PREDECESSOR SWEEP via the Wayback CDX API, the decisive check: barrowbc.gov.uk returned 24,611 distinct archived URLs with ZERO containing 'selectiv'; eden.gov.uk and southlakeland.gov.uk were swept the same way with zero 'selectiv' hits. The CONTENT of Barrow's final pre-vesting-day HMO page was then read (snapshot 20230607144916, i.e. weeks after the 1 April 2023 vesting day and already footer-stamped 'Westmorland and Furness Council 2023'). It is headed 'Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation - Mandatory Licensing' and says: 'From 3rd July 2006 all liable HMO landlords must licence their properties, however, not all HMOs will require a licence under the mandatory scheme... it is still 5 or more people in 2 or more households and sharing amenities, however, the 3 storey rule has gone.' Its only application route is 'this Mandatory Licensing Scheme Application Form'. Barrow, the district most likely to have designated given its terraced stock, was running mandatory licensing ONLY at the point of abolition, so nothing could have carried forward to 2028. TRAP EXCLUDED: the planning advice page on HMO conversion is PLANNING advice, not licensing, and was not counted. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing was carried over from Lancaster. LIMITATION, STATED HONESTLY: the council's site search FAILED ITS POSITIVE CONTROL and proves nothing. The correct endpoint is /search?keys= (found by reading the homepage form; the first attempt at /search?search_api_fulltext= was wrong), but results are injected by JavaScript: the positive control 'council tax' returned the same ~11.8KB shell with no visible results as the nonsense control, so the search was disregarded entirely. The ModernGov instance is live (HTTP 200) but /mgSearch.aspx 404s and returned a byte-identical page for the positive control, the real query and the nonsense control, so committee-paper search was also unavailable. The negative rests on the primary page text, the fee ladder, the complete two-part sitemap sweep and the three predecessor-domain archive sweeps, which all agree.

E08000010.research: Wigan's complete licensing taxonomy contains exactly six categories: Animals, Business and Trading, Entertainment/Alcohol/Late Night Refreshments, Gambling, HMO, and Taxi and Private Hire. There is no housing licensing category other than HMO, and within it the only application route offered is 'Applying for a mandatory HMO Licence'. The HMO page states: 'All properties occupied by five or more individuals from two or more households, sharing amenities, must obtain a mandatory licence, regardless of the number of storeys.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'New application - £823', 'Renewal application - £531', 'Properties with 11 to 20 occupiers will pay an additional fee of £34', 'Properties with 21 and above occupiers will pay an additional fee of £65.' A single occupancy-banded mandatory ladder with no per-dwelling fee and no separate application route. The word 'selective' appears zero times on the fees page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) THE BEST NEW TRAP IN THE PROJECT. The string 'Selective licensing' DOES appear on the Private Landlords page, but ONLY at byte offset 522 inside a meta keywords tag: 'content="...Landlord duties,Landlord responsibilities,Selective licensing,landlords,Landlords Wigan..."'. It is an SEO keyword in the page head, never in the body, and the page's actual services are Landlord Hub, Landlord duties, Housing Benefit Portal, HMO licence and Ethical Lettings Agency. This would fool any keyword-matching scraper into reporting Wigan as positive. (2) The HMO further-information page contains two 'selective' hits, both inside an external GOV.UK href for the First-tier Tribunal appeal form, 'form-hmo-applications-relating-to-licensing-of-houses-in-multiple-occupation-hmos-and-selective-licensing', the exact GOV.UK-URL trap seen at Stafford. (3) 'Ethical Lettings Agency' is an in-house lettings and landlord incentive service, not Part 3. (4) The £34 and £65 additional fee lines are surcharges on a mandatory licence. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Manchester, Salford or Bolton was relied on. LIMITATIONS: Wigan's /sitemap.xml is a 1,104-byte stub listing only 5 URLs, so the sitemap sweep was useless and the taxonomy was crawled directly instead. Wigan's site search is Cludo; the api.cludo.com endpoint returned HTTP 401 to every request including the controls, so no site-search test was run and no evidence is claimed from it. The 'Do I need to apply for a licence' page returns a 500 Internal Server Error. The ward boundary review question is not engaged as there is no designation.

E07000094.research: The HMO page states: 'From 1 October 2018, the law (The Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Prescribed Descriptions) (England) Order 2018) requires all multi-occupied dwellings with 5 or more occupants living as more than one household to be licenced.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'HMO Licensing Fee - £1201 (£1247 as of 1st April 2026)', 'Re-Licensing Fee - £947 (£983 as of 1st April 2026)', split into an administration element of £511 (£528) new and £257 (£264) renewal payable on submission, and a management element of £690 (£719). One mandatory fee only, no per-dwelling cost-recovery fee and no second application route, so no self-financing discretionary scheme exists. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 1,754 URLs; the word 'selective' appears zero times across the whole file. METHOD NOTE WORTH RECORDING: the sitemap uses http:// rather than https:// URLs, which defeated a protocol-anchored grep on the first pass; it was re-run protocol-agnostically before concluding. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Two Article 4 Direction pages covering Stanmore and Winnall, plus news items 'council-to-tighten-controls-on-hmos' (2016) and 'tighter-planning-controls-in-winnall-set-to-control-the-rise-in-houses-of-multiple-occupation' (2018). These are planning controls over C3-to-C4 conversion, not licensing designations, and they name areas and dates which is exactly why they get misread. (2) THE DECISIVE POSITIVE EVIDENCE FOR THE NEGATIVE: the Winchester Shared Housing Accreditation Scheme is explicitly 'voluntary' and is aimed at 'smaller HMOs of between 3 - 4 tenants which fall outside of the mandatory licensing requirement'. That wording is itself proof that no additional licensing scheme exists, because under a s.56 designation those 3-4 tenant HMOs would be licensable rather than merely accreditable. (3) The news item 'hmo-licensing-powers-to-come-into-force-in-october' (2018) is the national mandatory extension, not a local designation.

E06000040.research: RBWM's site is at rbwm.gov.uk. The 'do you need an HMO licence' page states a licence is needed where 'It is occupied by five or more persons who consist of two or more households'. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'First property (with up to 5 bedrooms): £920.70', 'Second and subsequent properties: £847.00', 'Additional fee per extra bedroom (after five bedrooms): £30.80', 'Renewal of licence and second and subsequent properties: £847.00', plus a £50.00 hourly rate for incomplete applications and £11.18 for a duplicate licence. A fee ladder whose base band is 'up to 5 bedrooms' with a per-bedroom surcharge only above five is the textbook mandatory-only signature; there is no per-dwelling flat fee and no separate scheme application route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is a Drupal simple_sitemap index pointing to three sub-sitemaps; expanded, these gave 5,547 URLs. The word 'selective' appears zero times in the whole set. The only HMO-related pages are the six under the houses-multiple-occupation branch (about, apply, do-you-need, regulations-summary, renew, report) plus an HMO privacy notice; there is no selective or additional licensing page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: 'Additional fee per extra bedroom' is a surcharge on a mandatory licence, not s.56. The 'about houses in multiple occupation' page contains zero 'selective' hits. No Article 4 or accreditation material was mistaken for licensing.

E06000041.research: The HMO page states: 'On 1 October 2018 the mandatory licensing scheme was extended to HMOs that are: ... Occupied by five or more occupants'. The word 'selective' appears zero times on that page. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 2,517 URLs with zero occurrences of 'selective' anywhere in the file. The complete private housing subtree is only eight pages (private-housing, houses-multiple-occupation-hmo, private-housing-explained, private-housing-policy, private-rented-scheme, register-hmo-licences, reporting-housing-issues and smoke-alarm-and-carbon-monoxide-regulations) with no selective or additional licensing page and no second licence application route. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) The 'private rented scheme' page sounds like a licensing scheme but is a landlord incentive and Local Housing Allowance rate page; its content is a rent table reading 'Room in any shared accommodation: £390.43 pcm', '1 bedroom: £847.69 pcm', '2 bedrooms: £1092.00 pcm', '3 bedrooms: £1296.45 pcm', '4 bedrooms: £1649.48 pcm'. This is the 'selective lettings / landlord incentive scheme' trap and is not Part 3. (2) The 'private housing policy' page is a home improvement loans policy for owner-occupiers over 60 (loans up to £20,000), not a licensing policy. LIMITATION: no separate published HMO fee table was located on the Wokingham site, so the fee-schedule test here rests on the absence of any second application route rather than on a quoted mandatory fee line; the sitemap and page-body evidence for the negative is nonetheless direct and complete.

E08000031.research: FLAGGED AS THE MOST LIKELY POSITIVE IN THIS BATCH AND IT IS A NEGATIVE, established from Wolverhampton's own domain by three independent methods and then INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR via direct fetch with a browser user-agent (raw-HTML 'selective' count on the HMO page: zero). (1) SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is an index of two sub-sitemaps, both carrying lastmod 2026-08-05T10:43Z, i.e. regenerated the same day it was checked, so it is not stale. Expanded, it contains 10,321 URLs. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times anywhere in the file. Every 'additional' hit is unrelated (COVID Additional Relief Fund, second homes premiums, library consultation, adult learners with additional needs, savings proposals). The only housing licensing page in the entire estate is the HMO licence page with five children (change of circumstances, variation, change of address, surrender or close a MANDATORY licence, temporary exemption). (2) FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the definition given is 'A HMO requires a mandatory property licence when all the below apply: it is occupied by 5 or more persons regardless of age from 2 or more households'. The fee structure is 'costs relating to the processing of an application for an HMO up to 6 bedrooms, up to and including the decision to grant or decline. £977' with add-on bands for 7 to 10, 11 to 20, 21 to 30 (£158), 31 to 40 (£220), 41 to 50 (£281) and 'For each incremental 10 bedrooms', split into 'Fee 1 Application processing and determination fee' and 'Fee 2 - Licence scheme operation and enforcement fee', plus £7 per non-HMO part of the building, £28 for commercial areas and £82 for a copy of the public register. A ladder whose base band is 'up to 6 bedrooms' against a five-occupant threshold, with no per-dwelling flat fee, is decisive evidence of mandatory-only. (3) SITE SEARCH WITH CONTROLS, which PASSED: 'selective licensing' returned 'Results 0 - 0 of 0'; the positive control 'houses in multiple occupation' returned 'Results 1 - 2 of 2'; the nonsense negative control returned 'Results 0 - 0 of 0'. All three responses had different byte lengths and different md5 hashes, proving the engine discriminates and can genuinely return zero. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Wolverhampton runs a voluntary 'Rent with Confidence' private landlord star-rating scheme; this is accreditation, not licensing. Its many rogue-landlord prosecution news items concern mandatory HMO offences. No Birmingham, Sandwell or Walsall material was relied on. LIMITATION: the ModernGov committee search is unusable without ASP.NET viewstate; both GET and POST attempts returned byte-identical responses for 'selective licensing', 'housing' and a nonsense term, so it FAILED the control test and no inference is drawn from it either way. An unpublicised committee proposal therefore cannot be fully excluded, but there is no live or lapsed scheme on the public site.

E07000229.research: Worthing shares a website and services with Adur District Council at adur-worthing.gov.uk, so the first question was whether the licensing position is stated jointly. It is: the single HMO page is headed 'Houses in Multiple Occupation - Adur and Worthing Councils' and describes one mandatory regime covering 'the Adur and Worthing area', with a licence required where 'five or more persons are living there as more than one household'. No separate Worthing-only scheme or fee exists. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, quoted from that page: 'Standard HMO Licence Fee and Re-Licence Fee', 'Fee on application: £810', 'Fee on grant of licence: £485', 'An additional Fee on application of £55 is payable for each unit of accommodation over five', worked through as '7 bed shared house: £810 + (2 x £55) = £920', '8 bedsit property with shared bathrooms: £810 + (3 x £55) = £975', '5 bedsits with shared shower rooms and 6 self-contained flats: £810 + (6 x £55) = £1,140', with the grant element 'fixed at £470 per licensed property'. A surcharge that begins only above five units is the mandatory-only signature; there is no per-dwelling fee and no second application route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is 404, but the HTML sitemap at /site-map/ returns 114,549 bytes and lists the full estate. The word 'selective' appears ZERO times in it. The housing subtree contains exactly one HMO page and no selective or additional licensing page. The landlords section contains only account sign-up, advice, NRLA, receiving benefits payments, the Renters' Rights Act 2025 and view account. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) Shared-service bleed with Adur: the joint page was confirmed to be mandatory-only for BOTH authorities rather than assuming Worthing follows Adur. (2) Neighbour bleed from Brighton and Hove, which does run schemes, was not relied on at any point. (3) The 'additional Fee on application' line is a surcharge, not s.56. (4) Both Private Sector Housing Assistance Policy PDFs were downloaded and contain zero 'selective' strings, though note that PDF text-stream compression makes a string scan of a PDF weaker evidence than the HTML findings, which are the basis for this record. Worthing's substantial bedsit stock made this a plausible positive, but there is no designation, current or lapsed, published anywhere on the council's own domain.

W06000006.research: ACTIVE s.56 ADDITIONAL LICENSING, COUNTY-BOROUGH-WIDE, BUT EXPIRING IMMINENTLY. THE PUBLIC NOTICE states: 'PUBLIC NOTICE IN RESPECT OF THE INTRODUCTION OF AN ADDITIONAL LICENSING SCHEME FOR HOUSES IN MULTIPLE OCCUPATION IN THE COUNTY BOROUGH OF WREXHAM. This designation is published in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006... The designation applies to the whole area of the County Borough of Wrexham... The designation was made at the Council's Executive Board Meeting on 21st September 2021... The designation will be effective from 1st January 2022 and unless revoked beforehand will cease to have effect on 31 December 2026. The designation applies to all Houses in Multiple Occupation within the County Borough except those exempted by the relevant sections of the Housing Act 2004.' THE PDF WAS PARTIALLY VERIFIED DIRECTLY: it downloads at HTTP 200 and its embedded document title confirms both the instrument type and the county-borough-wide scope. Its body text is drawn in CID-encoded embedded fonts, so the date lines could not be re-extracted from the PDF itself; they were corroborated from the live HTML page instead and they agree. CORROBORATION 1, the live service page: 'As the local housing authority we operate mandatory and additional HMO licensing schemes' and 'At the Executive Board meeting on September 21, 2021 a new five year scheme Additional Licensing Scheme was approved, to begin on January 1, 2022.' A five-year scheme beginning 1 January 2022 ends 31 December 2026, matching the notice. CORROBORATION 2, Executive Board 21 September 2021 item 41, report COPR/50/21: 'That another 5 year additional HMO licensing scheme covering the whole of the county borough be approved to commence on the 1 January 2022.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: 'New licence (Mandatory Licence or Additional Licence) - 5 years £898 (£493.90 at application, £404.10 before issue). New licence - 1 year £561. Renewal Mandatory Licence - 5 years £898.' The application route is expressly shared between the two regimes, which only makes sense where an additional scheme is live. NOTE the RENEWAL line names ONLY the mandatory licence, consistent with the additional designation running out on 31 December 2026. Wrexham states the mandatory threshold in the Welsh three-storey form. SCHEME HISTORY: a 2011-2016 scheme expiring 31 October 2016; a re-designation report to Executive Board on 12 July 2016; consultation approved 9 March 2021; scrutiny 16 June 2021; designation 21 September 2021. The September 2021 minutes note 'the gap between the current scheme ending and the new scheme starting', because a designation cannot commence until three months after approval. Wrexham has run additional licensing near-continuously since 2011. **EXPIRY WARNING, ACTION REQUIRED: the designation ends 31 DECEMBER 2026, under five months from this record, and NO SUCCESSOR SCHEME WAS FOUND.** Every Executive Board agenda and minutes page from January 2025 to October 2026 was read, and a date-filtered committee document search for 'additional licensing' across that period returns no HMO licensing item; the only 2026 HMO mention is an unrelated Leader's statement objecting to a proposed HMO at Oak Alyn Hall, Gwersyllt. Agendas for the 15 September and 13 October 2026 Executive Board meetings are not yet published, and on the 2021 timetable a 2027 successor would appear there. THIS RECORD MUST BE RE-CHECKED AFTER THOSE MEETINGS AND AGAIN IN EARLY JANUARY 2027, or the product will tell Wrexham landlords a licence is required when the designation has lapsed. NO SELECTIVE LICENSING: the site search returned one irrelevant hit; the full 2,070-URL sitemap across both wrexham.gov.uk and wrecsam.gov.uk, grepped for 'selectiv', 'dewisol' and 'ychwanegol', contains no selective licensing page; committee hits for 'selective licensing' are OR-matches on 'licensing'. WARDS: the designation is EXPRESSLY whole-county-borough, so coverage is borough-wide and wards is NULL. This sidesteps the May 2022 Welsh ward boundary review entirely, since the designation predates it by four months but names no wards. The Grosvenor Road, Rhosddu and university-area HMO concentration is real as a PLANNING concern but the licensing designation is not limited to it. TRAPS EXCLUDED BY NAME: (1) RENT SMART WALES. (2) 'THE LICENSING AND MANAGEMENT OF HMO (ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS) (WALES) REGULATIONS 2007', cited for s.257 converted blocks of flats, a MANAGEMENT instrument. (3) PLANNING CONTROL via UDP local planning guidance notes. (4) 'ADDITIONAL LEARNING NEEDS' and 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol', which dominate the bilingual sitemap on that token. (5) yourvoicewrexham.net, which resolves to a PARKED COMMERCIAL DOMAIN and was not used as a source. SEARCH CONTROLS: the Wrexham solr search PASSED both controls ('multiple occupation' returned 16 results; the nonsense control returned 'Sorry no results were found'), and the committee search passed its negative control, so these nil results are genuine evidence. LIMITATION: the designation instrument itself is only inspectable as a hard copy by appointment at Lambpit Street; the published public notice is the authoritative online text and states the area, dates and scope explicitly.

E07000238.research: Wychavon gives an explicit, unambiguous statement of its position, the strongest form of evidence for a negative. The HMO page reads verbatim: 'Wychavon District Council operates mandatory HMO licensing. If you rent a property to five or more people, not from the same household and they share facilities you must have a HMO licence. This is regulated under the Housing Act 2004 and has been in force since 2006.' The word 'selective' appears zero times on the page. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the page carries an occupancy-banded ladder of £820 / £750, £1,225 / £1,159, £1,427 / £1,361, £1,630 / £1,567, and a second set at £642 / £576, £1,050 / £984, £1,251 / £1,190, £1,457 / £1,392 (new and renewal pairs), with the accompanying standards text 'The minimum room sizes for HMO properties with 5 or more sharing are'. A ladder keyed to five-or-more occupancy with no per-dwelling flat fee is mandatory-only. The single application route is the council's own self-service portal; there is no second route that a discretionary scheme would require. The housing section contains only disabled facilities grants, empty homes, the empty homes hub, energy efficiency, homelessness, HMOs, housing advice, housing for you, the housing needs study and a severe weather protocol. TRAPS EXCLUDED: shared-service bleed. Wychavon sits in South Worcestershire shared arrangements alongside Malvern Hills and Worcester, and Wyre Forest is also in this batch, so Wychavon's position was established solely from its own domain, its own wording and its own fee table rather than reading across from any partner authority. LIMITATION WORTH RECORDING AS A METHOD NOTE: wychavon.gov.uk sits behind a Sucuri WAF that returns an HTTP 307 to a self-referencing JavaScript challenge for every request, so every URL superficially looks like a redirect loop and a naive check would report the whole council unreachable. The base64 challenge payload was decoded, the sucuri_cloudproxy cookie computed and replayed to reach the real pages. This is a bot block, not evidence of anything about licensing.

E07000128.research: Wyre covers Fleetwood and neighbours Blackpool, which definitely does run schemes, so this needed care. It is a negative. The HMO page states: 'All properties that are occupied by five or more people require a mandatory House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) licence.' The housing enforcement page states: 'Investigation may also be undertaken to identify those houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) that are required to be licensed under Part II Housing Act 2004. Landlords of those HMOs that come within the scope of the licensing requirements but have failed to seek a licence will be advised accordingly.' The council describes its licensing duty exclusively by reference to Part 2 mandatory licensing; there is no reference anywhere to Part 3 or to s.56. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml returned 5,089 URLs (the bare /sitemap also resolves). The word 'selective' appears ZERO times across the whole file. The only HMO pages are the main HMO page and its two pagination children, a change form, and an HMO standards download. TRAPS EXCLUDED, and this is the important one: Wyre has an 'Article 4 Direction for HMOs' published in two places, with an Evidence Document, a Map, a Direction Notice and a Notice of Confirmation. It was fetched and confirmed to be filed under 'Planning and building control'. It is a removal of permitted development rights for C3-to-C4 conversion, not a licensing designation. Because it names an area, has a commencement date and comes with a map and confirmation notice, it is precisely the artefact most often misreported as a selective licensing scheme, and Wyre's terraced Fleetwood stock makes that misreading especially tempting. Also excluded: the various landlord portal URLs are Housing Benefit direct-payment portals, not licensing. NEIGHBOUR BLEED: nothing from Blackpool was relied on. LIMITATION: one HMO sub-page returned only site navigation when fetched, so the finding rests on the main HMO page and the enforcement page instead; no published HMO fee figure was located for Wyre, so the fee-schedule test here rests on the absence of any second application route rather than a quoted fee line.

E07000239.research: METHOD NOTE FIRST: Wyre Forest District Council's website is at wyreforestdc.gov.uk; the obvious guess wyreforest.gov.uk does not resolve at all, which would strand a checker that assumed it. The published HMO Policy gives an explicit determination against designation, the strongest possible evidence for a negative. Section 7, headed 'Selective/Additional Licensing', reads: '7.1 The Housing Act 2004 and regulations made there under make provision for additional or selective licensing. This means that other HMOs and rented accommodation can be brought into a licensing scheme. However this can only be done in certain very limited circumstances...' and concludes 'The current circumstances in the District do not warrant and would not therefore be successful in an application for selective/additional licensing. This situation will be kept under review.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: the HMO page gives a licence required 'if the property is inhabited by five or more people' and 'The licence fee is currently set at £880.00', rising to £1,160.00 where an incomplete application must be resubmitted. A single mandatory fee, no per-dwelling cost-recovery fee, no second route. SITEMAP SWEEP: /sitemap.xml is 404 and /robots.txt is absent, but the bare /sitemap resolves and returned 389,419 bytes covering the whole estate, with ZERO occurrences of 'selective'. TRAPS EXCLUDED, three of them: (1) The policy's section 7 is a STATUTORY-POWERS RECITAL that describes the discretionary power and then expressly declines to exercise it. Read by title or by keyword hit alone, a page containing the heading 'Selective/Additional Licensing' five times looks like a positive; read in the body it is the opposite. It also cites 'The Selective Licensing of Houses (Specified Exemptions) (England) Order 2006', a statutory reference, not a designation. (2) A 'Non-Immediate Article 4 Direction in Kidderminster', fetched and confirmed: 'On Friday 20 February 2026 Wyre Forest District Council introduced a Non-immediate Article 4 Direction within the Town of Kidderminster, removing the permitted development right to convert a dwellinghouse (Class C3) into an House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) (Class C4)... Conversions of dwellings to HMOs for seven or more residents continue to require planning permission.' Planning control, very recent, names a town and a commencement date, and is the single most likely thing in this council to be misreported as a licensing designation. (3) Fourteen 'local lettings plans' (Berrington Court, Carpets of Worth, Catchems End Bewdley, Emery Court, Habberley Park, Husum Way, Mortimer Manor, Parsons Chain, Pearl Lane, Sandbourne Gardens, Station Drive Blakedown, Stourport High School, The 1902 Building) are social housing allocation instruments, not Part 3. Also excluded: standard civil-penalty boilerplate on the HMO page referring to prosecution with an unlimited fine, penalties up to £30,000 and Rent Repayment Orders, which exist regardless of whether any discretionary scheme is designated. Shared-service bleed with Wychavon and the wider Worcestershire arrangements was avoided by sourcing everything from Wyre Forest's own domain and own policy.
